JISHUMI:v1p645/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p645/r12.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p645/r12.claim: Without reports of prayer toward Jerusalem, Abu Muslim could place this at Medina’s beginning: in Mecca Muhammad prayed with the Kaʿba between himself and Jerusalem, then awaited a command to face it.
JISHUMI:v1p645/r12.anchor: وقد ذكر أبو مسلم في هذه الآيات الواردة في نسخ القبلة تشككا في صلاة النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -

ITQAN:v1p65/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r2.speaker: ابن عمر
ITQAN:v1p65/r2.claim: In the Ṣaḥīḥayn report from Ibn ʿUmar, people at Quba were told at dawn that the Prophet had received revelation the previous night ordering them to face the Kaʿba.
ITQAN:v1p65/r2.anchor: من حديث ابن عمر بينما الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح إذا أتاهم آت فقال إن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أنزل عليه الليلة قرآن

ITQAN:v1p65/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r3.speaker: أنس
ITQAN:v1p65/r3.claim: Muslim's report from Anas says the qibla verse came while the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem; Banu Salima were told during the dawn prayer and turned toward the Kaʿba.
ITQAN:v1p65/r3.anchor: وروى مسلم عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي ببيت المقدس فنزلت ﴿ قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء ﴾

ITQAN:v1p65/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r4.speaker: البراء
ITQAN:v1p65/r4.claim: Al-Baraʾ's Ṣaḥīḥayn report says the qibla change came after sixteen or seventeen months; the first prayer toward the Kaʿba was ʿAsr, supporting a daytime revelation between noon and ʿAsr.
ITQAN:v1p65/r4.anchor: عن البراء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا

ITQAN:v1p65/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r5.speaker: جلال الدين
ITQAN:v1p65/r5.claim: Qadi Jalal al-Din judges nighttime revelation stronger, since Quba learned at dawn and it seems unlikely the Prophet delayed conveying the command from the prior afternoon.
ITQAN:v1p65/r5.anchor: قال القاضي جلال الدين والأرجح بمقتضى الاستدلال نزولها بالليل لأن قضية أهل قباء كانت في الصبح

ITQAN:v1p65/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r6.speaker: ابن حجر
ITQAN:v1p65/r6.claim: Ibn Hajar prefers daytime revelation: the news reached people inside Medina at ʿAsr and Quba at dawn; “last night” can refer idiomatically to part of the previous day and the following night.
ITQAN:v1p65/r6.anchor: وقال ابن حجر الأقوى أن نزولها كان نهارا والجواب عن حديث ابن عمر

ITQAN:v1p65/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p65/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
ITQAN:v1p65/r7.claim: Al-Suyuti cites al-Nasaʾi's report from Abu Saʿid ibn al-Muʿalla: the Prophet recited the qibla verse from the minbar, then descended and prayed noon, supporting daytime revelation.
ITQAN:v1p65/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال مررنا يوما ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاعد على المنبر

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r4.speaker: أهل التفسير
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r4.claim: One Qur'anic sense is the literal face.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p617/r4.anchor: أحدها : الوجه المعروف في الحيوان . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في البقرة ) : ﴿ فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام ﴾

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r1.claim: In response to earlier indications, the Prophet awaited revelation for the qibla change, watched for Gabriel, and prayed for the Kaaba, the qibla of his father Abraham.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r1.anchor: tahvîl-i kıble için vahyin vürûduna intizar ediyor, semâdan Cibrîl’i gözetiyor ve babası Hazret-i İbrâhim’in kıblesi olan Kâbe’yi temenni ederek duâ eyliyordu

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r2.claim: The command turns the Prophet toward the Kaaba and abrogates the former qibla; facing the sanctuary means turning the body's front fully toward it.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r2.anchor: Bu suretle eski kıble mensuh ve böyle istikbâl-i kıble farz oldu. Yüzün dosdoğru çevrilmesi, bedenin ön tarafından tamamen yönelmesi demek olduğu âşikârdır.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r3.claim: Turning the face or body away from the Kaaba invalidates prayer, while someone far away need not face the Kaaba's exact physical point.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r3.anchor: bedenin Kâbe’den başka bir tarafa bükülmesi namazı ifsad eder.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r4.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r4.claim: The wording commands facing the direction of the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaaba itself, since the mosque is the sacred precinct around the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r4.anchor: bizzat “Kâbe” denilmeyip, “Mescid-i Harâm şatrına” buyurulmuştur, Mescid-i Harâm ise Kâbe’nin kendi değil etrâfındaki harem-i şerîfidir

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r5.claim: The precinct is called sacred because fighting and aggression are forbidden there and complete security is sought.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r5.anchor: burada kıtal, taarruz memnû‘bulunduğu ve emn-i kâmil matlub olduğu için ona “harâm” veya “harem” denilmiştir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r6.claim: Shatr can mean a half, a distinct part, or a side of something.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r6.anchor: “Şatr”, bir şeyin nısfı veya bir cüz’-i mütemâyizi veya bir cânibi mânalarına gelir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r7.speaker: Cübbâî
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r7.claim: The Mu'tazili Jubbai holds that prayer must face the Kaaba's half, so facing one of its edges is insufficient.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r7.anchor: Mu‘tezile’den Cübbâî ve Kādî Abdülcebbâr, namazda Kâbe’nin nısfına isabet şart olduğuna

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r8.speaker: Kādî Abdülcebbâr
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r8.claim: The Mu'tazili Qadi Abd al-Jabbar holds that prayer must face the Kaaba's half, so facing one of its edges is insufficient.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r8.anchor: Mu‘tezile’den Cübbâî ve Kādî Abdülcebbâr, namazda Kâbe’nin nısfına isabet şart olduğuna ve bir kenarına teveccüh gayr-i kâfî bulunduğuna

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r9.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r9.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r9.claim: The majority of exegetes, including Companions, Successors and later scholars, hold that distant worshippers need only face the direction of the Sacred Mosque, while people in Mecca or inside it must face some side of the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r9.anchor: sahâbeden ve tâbi‘înden, müteahhirînden cumhûr-ı müfessirîn uzaktan Mescid-i Harâm semtine teveccüh kâfî bulunduğunu ve ancak Mekke’de ve Mescid-i Harâm içinde Kâbe’nin herhangi bir tarafına teveccüh vâcib olduğunu beyân eylemişlerdir

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r10.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r10.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r10.claim: On that reading, shatr means the Kaaba itself and the Sacred Mosque means the Kaaba's direction; detailed law belongs in the jurisprudence discussions of facing the qibla.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r10.anchor: “şatr” nefs-i Kâbe’yi ve “Mescid-i Harâm” semt-i Kâbe’yi ifâde eder. Ve bunun tafsîli kütüb-i fıkhıyenin istikbâl-i kıble bahsine aittir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r11.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r11.speaker: براء بن عازب
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r11.claim: The Prophet arrived in Medina, prayed toward Bayt al-Maqdis for sixteen months, and was then turned toward the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r11.anchor: Berâ b. Âzib radıyallahu ‘anh hazretlerinden rivayet olunuyor ki Resûl-i Ekrem sallallâhu aleyhi ve sellem Medine’ye gelmiş ve on altı ay Beyt-i Makdis tarafına namaz kılmış idi

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r12.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r12.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r12.claim: The qibla change is also dated to Rajab, after noon and two months before Badr; during noon prayer at Banu Salama Mosque, the Prophet turned toward the Mizab after two rakats, and men and women exchanged places, giving the mosque its name Qiblatayn.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r12.anchor: Bu tahvîlin Bedir gazâsından iki ay mukaddem Receb-i Şerîfte zevâl-i şemsten sonra vâki‘olduğu ve Resûlullah’ın Benî Seleme Mescidi’nde ashâbıyla beraber kılmakta bulunduğu öğle namazının iki rekâtını müte‘âkib namazda iken çevrilip “Mîzâb”a doğru yöneldiği

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r13.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r13.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r13.claim: News quickly reached the surroundings; a messenger told people praying in Quba Mosque that the Prophet had turned toward the Kaaba.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r13.anchor: Derhâl etrâfa haberler gitmiş “Mescid-i Kubâ”da dahi ahâli namazda iken biri gelmiş, “Resûlullah Kâbe’ye çevrildi!” diye bağırmış olduğu mervîdir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r14.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r14.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r14.claim: Earlier indications such as 2:115 became definitive through this command, and facing Bayt al-Maqdis was fully abrogated.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r14.anchor: gibi vâki‘olan işâretler, bu âyet ile tamâmen kesb-i kat‘iyyet eylemiş ve Beytü’l-Makdis’e teveccüh büsbütün nesh olunmuştur.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r15.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r15.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r15.claim: Some scholars considered 2:115 the abrogating verse, but the author's preferred view, shared by the majority, is that the command to turn the face is the abrogator.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r15.anchor: doğrusu cumhûrun dediği [529] gibi nâsih işbu فَوَلِّ وَجْهَكَ emridir.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r16.claim: The instruction is generalized to everyone and everywhere: wherever people pray, they must turn their faces toward the Kaaba's direction.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r16.anchor: ve her nerede bulunursanız, yani her nerede namaz kılarsanız yüzlerinizi o tarafa çeviriniz, o tarafa yöneliniz.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r17.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r17.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r17.claim: A particular mosque is not required, but facing the Kaaba's direction is obligatory except when a necessity such as fear of an enemy prevents it; then a nearby direction suffices.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r17.anchor: namaz kılmak için bir mescid gibi muayyen bir mahal ile tekayyüd farz değildir. Fakat muayyen bir kıble olarak Mescid-i Harâm’a doğru Kâbe tarafına teveccüh herkese farzdır.

ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r18.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r18.speaker: author
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r18.claim: The phrase “wherever you turn, there is God's face” applies to the necessity in which exact qibla orientation is impossible.
ELMALILI:2:142-145#3/r18.anchor: Meğer ki düşman havfı gibi zarûrî bir mazeret karşısında buna da imkân bulunmasın, o zaman buna yakın herhangi bir cihet kâfî olur. İşte فَأَيْنَمَا تُوَلُّوا۟ فَثَمَّ وَجْهُ ٱللَّهِ’ın mânası da budur.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p7/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p7/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p7/r3.claim: Al-ḥarām and al-ḥaram denote what is prohibited or inaccessible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.claim: The Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after arriving in Medina, wished to face the Kaaba, and then received the revelation directing him toward it; Jews asked what had turned them from their former qibla.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r2.anchor: رواه البخاري، عن البراء بن عازب قال: لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة، فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.claim: On the apparent future reading, God foretold the Jews' objection before the order to face the Kaaba, making it a prediction of the unseen and preparing the Prophet and Muslims for the objection with an answer ready.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r4.anchor: وذلك قبل أن يؤمروا باستقبال الكعبة، وتكون هذه الآية متقدمة في النزول

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.claim: An alternative chronology places the order to face the Kaaba before this verse in revelation, although this verse comes first in the recitation; Ibn Abbas and others state this, and the Barāʾ report supports it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p8/r5.anchor: وذهب قوم إلى أنها متقدمة في التلاوة، متأخرة في النزول، وأنه نزل قوله: قد نرى تقلب وجهك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r13.claim: The commentary recalls the report from al-Barāʾ and earlier disagreement about which of the adjacent revelations, سيقول السفهاء or قد نرى, came first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r13.anchor: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء: تقدم حديث البراء، وتقدم ذكر الخلاف في هذه الآية. وقوله: سيقول السفهاء: أيهما نزل قبل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r14.speaker: بعض النحويين
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r14.claim: Some grammarians say قد can shift a present verb to past meaning, citing several Qur'anic constructions.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p20/r14.anchor: ونرى هنا مضارع بمعنى الماضي، وقد ذكر بعض النحويين أن مما يصرف المضارع إلى الماضي قد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r1.claim: A poetic example likewise uses قد with a present form to refer to the past.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r1.anchor: لعمري لقوم قد نرى أمس فيهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses قد نرى as perhaps seeing, then says the construction conveys frequent seeing, comparing it with قد أترك.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r2.anchor: قال الزمخشري: قد نرى: ربما نرى، ومعناه: كثرة الرؤية، كقوله: قد أترك القرن مصفرا أنامله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r3.claim: Abū Ḥayyān rejects that explanation: perhaps usually conveys rarity, so it conflicts with the claim of frequency.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r3.anchor: ورب، على مذهب المحققين من النحويين، إنما تكون لتقليل الشيء في نفسه، أو لتقليل نظيره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r4.claim: The word قد itself does not indicate frequency; repeated seeing is inferred from تقلب, since turning one's gaze entails repeated movements.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r4.anchor: لأنه لم يوضع لمعنى الكثرة. هذا التركيب، أعني تركيب قد مع المضارع المراد منه الماضي، ولا غير المضي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r5.claim: Repeated movement is conveyed by تقلب, the reciprocal result of repeatedly turning the gaze, as in cutting until something is cut or breaking until it breaks.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r5.anchor: لأن من رفع بصره إلى السماء مرة واحدة، لا يقال فيه: قلب بصره في السماء، وإنما يقال: قلب إذا ردد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r6.claim: One view takes وجه in its apparent, literal sense.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r6.anchor: والوجه هنا قيل: أريد به مدلول ظاهره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r7.speaker: قتادة، السدي وغيرهما
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r7.claim: Qatada, al-Suddī, and others say the Messenger repeatedly looked toward heaven while praying that God turn him toward Mecca.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r7.anchor: قال قتادة والسدي وغيرهما: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقلب وجهه في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى أن يحوله إلى قبلة مكة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r8.claim: Another view says he looked toward the sky in order to be permitted to pray.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r8.anchor: وقيل: كان يقلب وجهه ليؤذن له في الدعاء

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r9.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r9.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the Prophet expected a change to the Kaaba, Abraham's qibla, which would attract Arabs through their pride and pilgrimage sites and oppose the Jews.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r9.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: كان يتوقع من ربه أن يحوله إلى الكعبة، لأنها قبلة أبيه إبراهيم، وأدعى للعرب إلى الإيمان، لأنها مفخرهم ومزارهم ومطافهم، ولمخالفة اليهود

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas's explanation is that the Prophet sought the qibla of Abraham.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r10.anchor: فالأول: قول ابن عباس، وهو ليصيب قبلة إبراهيم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r11.speaker: السدي، الربيع
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r11.claim: Al-Suddī and al-Rabīʿ explain the request as seeking to win Arabs over because they loved the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r11.anchor: والثاني: قول السدي والربيع، وهو ليتألف العرب لمحبتها في الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r12.speaker: مجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r12.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet sought to oppose Jews who claimed he had no settled religion until he followed them.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r12.anchor: والثالث: قول مجاهد، وهو قول اليهود: ما علم محمد دينه حتى اتبعنا، فأراد مخالفتهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r13.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r13.claim: The Prophet watched for Gabriel and revelation to announce the change.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r13.anchor: فكان يراعي نزول جبريل عليه السلام والوحي بالتحويل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r14.claim: Another interpretation uses وجه for sight, since the face is the noblest part and is invoked in seeking desired things; idioms and poetry support the usage.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p21/r14.anchor: وقيل: كنى بالوجه عن البصر، لأنه أشرف، وهو المستعمل في طلب الرغائب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r1.claim: The phrase is not an ellipsis for بصر وجهك: Arabic says your sight, eye, or nose, not the sight, eye, or nose of your face.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r1.anchor: ولا يحسن أن يقال: أنه على حذف مضاف، ويكون التقدير بصر وجهك، لأن هذا لا يكاد يستعمل، إنما يقال: بصرك وعينك وأنفك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r2.claim: In the preferred syntax, في السماء modifies the verbal noun تقلب and في retains its ordinary meaning; a Qur'anic parallel uses the same preposition.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r2.anchor: في السماء: متعلق بالمصدر، وهو تقلب، وهو يتعدى بفي، فهي على ظاهرها. قال تعالى: لا يغرنك تقلب الذين كفروا في البلاد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r3.claim: One alternative takes في to mean إلى, so the phrase means toward the sky.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r4.claim: Another analysis attaches في السماء to نرى and takes في to mean من, meaning God sees the turning from heaven; the wording magnifies the event without implying divine localization.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r4.anchor: وقيل: في السماء متعلق بنرى، وفي: بمعنى من، أي قد نرى من السماء تقلب وجهك، وإن كان الله تعالى يرى من كل مكان

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r5.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers attachment to تقلب with في literal; the sky is linked to mercy and blessings, supplication, and the expected descent of Gabriel.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r5.anchor: والظاهر الأول، وهو تعلق المجرور بالمصدر، وأن في على حقيقتها. واختص التقلب بالسماء، لأن السماء جهة تعود منها الرحمة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r6.claim: فلنولينك implies an omitted state: the Prophet was turning his face skyward while seeking another qibla.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r6.anchor: هذا يدل على أن في الجملة السابقة حالا محذوفة، التقدير: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء طالبا قبلة غير التي أنت مستقبلها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r7.claim: The promise is made under an unspoken oath to emphasize that it will be fulfilled.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r7.anchor: وجاء هذا الوعد على إضمار قسم مبالغة في وقوعه، لأن القسم يؤكد مضمون الجملة المقسم عليها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r8.claim: The promise precedes the command to delight the Prophet first by the response and again by its fulfillment; a promised result is also more reassuring than a sudden one.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r8.anchor: وجاء الوعد قبل الأمر لفرح النفس بالإجابة، ثم بإنجاز الوعد، فيتوالى السرور مرتين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r9.claim: قبلة is indefinite because no antecedent makes it definite; رضاه nearly identifies the qibla, revealing the Prophet's inward preference for the Kaaba although he did not say so explicitly.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r9.anchor: ونكر القبلة، لأنه لم يجر قبلها ما يقتضي أن تكون معهودة، فتعرف بالألف واللام. وليس في اللفظ ما يدل على أنه كان يطلب باللفظ قبلة معينة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r10.claim: The object of رضاه is the heart: the Prophet favored the Kaaba inwardly without expressly naming it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p22/r10.anchor: لأن متعلق الرضا هو القلب، وهو كان يؤثر أن تكون الكعبة، وإن كان لا يصرح بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r1.claim: The Prophet's approval of the Kaaba may stem from natural inclination or from the religious benefits it contains.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r1.anchor: ورضاه لها، إما لميل السجية، أو لاشتمالها على مصالح الدين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r2.claim: The promise means God will make the Prophet lead the community toward a qibla pleasing to him and enable him to do so.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r2.anchor: والمعنى: لنجعلنك تلي استقبال قبلة مرضية لك، ولنمكننك من ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r3.claim: The command فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام means to turn toward the Kaaba during prayer.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r3.anchor: أي استقبل بوجهك في الصلاة نحو الكعبة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r4.anchor: وبهذا الأمر نسخ التوجه إلى بيت المقدس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r5.claim: Some say the verse omits mention of prayer because it was revealed while the Prophet was praying; others say prayer is implicit because that is the only intended context.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r5.anchor: قالوا: وإنما لم يذكر في الصلاة، لأن الآية نزلت وهو في الصلاة، فأغنى التلبس بالصلاة عن ذكرها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān argues that the preceding promise of a qibla the Prophet approves already shows that prayer is intended.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r6.anchor: وأقول: في قوله: فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها ما يدل على أن المقصود هو في الصلاة، لأن القبلة هي التي يتوجه إليها في الصلاة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r7.claim: وجه means the whole body, since the entire body must face the qibla; the face can stand for the whole because it is the noblest and most identifying part.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r7.anchor: وأراد بالوجه: جملة البدن، لأن الواجب استقبالها بجملة البدن. وكنى بالوجه عن الجملة، لأنه أشرف الأعضاء، وبه يتميز بعض الناس عن بعض

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r8.claim: The wording may also mean the thing itself and pairs the turning of the face with the command to turn it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r8.anchor: وقد يطلق ويراد به نفس الشيء، ولأن المقابلة تقتضي ذلك، وهو أنه قابل قوله: قد نرى تقلب وجهك بقوله: فول وجهك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r9.speaker: الجمهور، الشافعي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r9.claim: Most exegetes, with al-Shāfiʿī, understand شطر as toward or the side of the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r9.anchor: وأكثر المفسرين على أن المراد بالشطر تلقاؤه وجانبه، وهو اختيار الشافعي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r10.speaker: الجبائي، القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r10.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī and the Qāḍī understand شطر as the middle of the mosque, where the Kaaba stands, and argue that the command requires facing that point.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r10.anchor: وقال الجبائي، وهو اختيار القاضي: المراد منه وسط المسجد ومنتصفه، لأن الشطر هو النصف، والكعبة بقعة في وسط المسجد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r11.speaker: الجبائي، القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r11.claim: Their argument is that facing the mosque while missing its center would invalidate prayer; reading شطر as merely a side would add nothing and fail to require facing the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r11.anchor: أن المصلي خارج المسجد متوجها إلى المسجد، لا إلى منتصف المسجد الذي هو الكعبة، لم تصح صلاته. وأنه لو فسرنا الشطر بالجانب، لم يكن لذكره فائدة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وغيرُه
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r12.claim: Ibn Abbas and others say the Messenger was directed toward the entire House.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r12.anchor: قال ابن عباس وغيره: وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى البيت كله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r13.speaker: ابن عمر
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r13.claim: Ibn ʿUmar says the Prophet and his community faced the line of the Kaaba's waterspout, the qibla for Medina, Syria, and approximately Andalusia.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r13.anchor: وقال ابن عمر: إنما وجه هو وأمته حيال ميزاب الكعبة، والميزاب هو قبلة المدينة والشام، وهناك قبلة أهل الأندلس بتقريب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r14.claim: There is no disagreement that the Kaaba is the qibla for people in every region.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r14.anchor: ولا خلاف أن الكعبة قبلة من كل أفق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r15.speaker: عبد الله
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r15.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh has تلقاء in place of شطر.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r15.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله، فول وجهك تلقاء المسجد الحرام

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r16.speaker: ابن عباس، مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas's hierarchy, also attributed to Mālik, makes the House the qibla for mosque-goers, the mosque for people of the sanctuary, and the sanctuary for people in east and west.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r16.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: البيت قبلة لأهل المسجد، والمسجد قبلة لأهل الحرم، والحرم قبلة لأهل المشرق والمغرب، وهذا قول مالك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r17.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r17.claim: Others say the Kaaba itself is the qibla; Abū Ḥayyān takes the apparent meaning of شطر as direction, since exact alignment would burden those far away.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r17.anchor: وقال آخرون: القبلة هي الكعبة، والظاهر أن المقصود بالشطر: النحو والجهة، لأن في استقبال عين الكعبة حرجا عظيما على من خرج لبعده عن مسامتتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r18.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r18.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r18.claim: Mentioning the Sacred Mosque instead of the Kaaba indicates that the obligation is to face the Kaaba's direction rather than its precise point.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r18.anchor: وفي ذكر المسجد الحرام، دون ذكر الكعبة، دلالة على أن الذي يجب هو مراعاة جهة الكعبة، لا مراعاة عينها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r19.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r19.speaker: مالك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r19.claim: Mālik infers from the command to face the mosque that a worshipper looks ahead rather than at the place of prostration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r19.anchor: واستدل مالك من قوله: فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام، على أن المصلي ينظر أمامه، لا إلى موضع سجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r20.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r20.speaker: الثوري، الشافعي، الحسن بن حي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r20.claim: Al-Thawrī, al-Shāfiʿī, and al-Ḥasan ibn Ḥayy prefer looking at the place of prostration.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r20.anchor: خلافا للثوري والشافعي والحسن بن حي، في أنه يستحب أن ينظر إلى موضع سجوده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r21.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r21.speaker: شريك القاضي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r21.claim: Sharīk al-Qāḍī prescribes different sightlines: prostration spot while standing, feet in bowing, nose in prostration, and lap while seated.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p23/r21.anchor: وفي الركوع إلى موضع قدميه، وفي السجود إلى موضع أنفه، وفي القعود إلى موضع حجره

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r1.claim: The Prophet should look ahead: lowering the head compromises upright posture, while keeping it erect and looking down is severe hardship, which religion removes.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r1.anchor: إن حنى رأسه ذهب ببعض القيام المعترض عليه في الرأس، وهو أشرف الأعضاء، وإن أقام رأسه وتكلف النظر ببصره إلى الأرض فتلك مشقة عظيمة وحرج،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r2.claim: Wherever you are covers every place a person may inhabit.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r2.anchor: وحيث ما كنتم: هذا عموم في الأماكن التي يحلها الإنسان، أي في أي موضع كنتم،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r3.claim: Grammatically, ḥaythu is initially a place adverb with a genitive complement; adding mā removes annexation, gives it conditional force, and lets it govern the verbs.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r3.anchor: فإذا وصلت بما زال منها معنى الإضافة، وضمنت معنى الشرط، وجوزي بها، وصارت إذ ذاك من عوامل الأفعال.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r4.claim: The command to face the Sacred Mosque applies equally to Muhammad and his community, avoiding any impression that the ruling was exclusive to him.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r4.anchor: أراد أن يبين أن حكمه وحكم أمته في ذلك واحد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r5.claim: The command is general across the earth, so the qibla is not restricted to Medina.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r5.anchor: فبين أنهم في أيما حصلوا من بقاع الأرض، وجب أن يستقبلوا شطر المسجد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r6.claim: The Prophet is addressed first because he longed for the change; the community follows him, and this order prevents assuming the command was his alone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r6.anchor: بدأ بأمره أولا ثم أتبع أمر أمته ثانيا لأنهم تبع له في ذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r7.claim: The reading attributed to ʿAbd Allāh says ‘toward it’ instead of ‘toward its direction.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r7.anchor: وفي حرف عبد الله: فولوا وجوهكم قبله.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r8.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads ‘in its direction’; these variants show that shatr means toward or in the direction of something.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: فولوا وجوهكم تلقاءه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r9.claim: The intended sense of shatr is direction or towardness.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r9.anchor: وهذا كله يدل على أن المراد بالشطر: النحو

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r10.claim: Those described as recipients of scripture are the leading Jews and Christians and their learned authorities.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r11.speaker: السدي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r11.claim: Al-Suddī identifies the recipients of scripture here as the Jews.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r12.claim: What they know to be true is facing the Sacred Mosque, the direction God prescribed for Abraham and his descendants.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r12.anchor: أي التوجه إلى المسجد الحرام، الحق: الذي فرضه الله على إبراهيم وذريته.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r13.speaker: قتادة والضحاك
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r13.claim: Qatāda and al-Ḍaḥḥāk say the qibla meant is the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r13.anchor: وقال قتادة والضحاك: إن القبلة هي الكعبة.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r14.speaker: الكسائي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r14.claim: Al-Kisāʾī takes the pronoun to refer to shatr, meaning the direction, close to the preceding explanation.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r14.anchor: وقال الكسائي: الضمير يعود على الشطر، وهو قريب من القول الثاني

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r15.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r15.claim: Another view, also given by Qatāda and Mujāhid, takes the pronoun as Muhammad: they know his truthfulness and prophethood.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p24/r15.anchor: وقيل: يعود على محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أي يعرفون صدقه ونبوته، قاله قتادة أيضا ومجاهد.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r1.claim: The Messenger pronoun refers to his own address; under this analysis the passage contains two shifts in address.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r1.anchor: ومفسر ضمير الرسول ضمير خطابه صلى الله عليه وسلم. فعلى هذا الوجه يكون التفاتان.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r2.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r2.claim: Abū Ḥayyān notes that this analysis of the pronouns yields two shifts in address.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r3.claim: The verb ‘know’ may take two objects or one, since its complement is an أن-clause.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r3.anchor: والعلم هنا يحتمل أن يكون مما يتعدى إلى اثنين

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r4.speaker: أبو العالية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r4.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says they knew from their scripture that the direction was toward the Kaaba.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r4.anchor: إما لأن في كتابهم التوجه إلى الكعبة،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r5.claim: Another explanation is that their scripture identifies Muhammad as a true prophet who commands only what is right.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r5.anchor: وإما لأن في كتابهم أن محمدا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r6.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r6.claim: A further basis for their knowledge is that abrogation is permissible.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r7.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r7.claim: They may also know because prophetic glad tidings said the Messenger would pray facing both qiblas.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r7.anchor: وإما لأن في بشارة الأنبياء أن رسول الله

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r8.claim: ‘From their Lord’ is a circumstantial phrase meaning that the truth is established by their Lord; the change was commanded by God, not reached through ijtihād.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r8.anchor: وفي ذلك دليل على أن التحول من بيت المقدس

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r9.claim: Calling God ‘their Lord’ signals that one must follow truth established by the one who cares for one's reform, as ‘the truth is from your Lord’ says.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r9.anchor: كما قال تعالى: الحق من ربك.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r10.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r10.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r10.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the closing verb with second-person tāʾ.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r10.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتاء على الخطاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r11.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r11.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r11.claim: With the second-person reading, the addressees may be believers, following the preceding command to face the mosque.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r11.anchor: فيحتمل أن يراد به المؤمنون لقوله: فولوا وجوهكم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r12.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r12.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r12.claim: Alternatively, the second-person reading addresses the People of the Book, shifting from third-person reference to direct speech.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r12.anchor: ويحتمل أن يراد به أهل الكتاب

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r13.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r13.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r13.claim: Direct address urges the People of the Book to act on the truth they know; confrontation intensifies blame and underscores the matter's gravity.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r13.anchor: تحريكا لهم بأن يعملوا بما علموا من الحق،

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r14.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r14.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r14.claim: Readers using third-person yāʾ most naturally refer to the People of the Book, continuing the surrounding third-person discourse.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r14.anchor: ومن قرأ بالياء، فالظاهر أنه عائد

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r15.claim: Either reading warns that God does not overlook people's deeds.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v2p25/r15.anchor: وعلى كلتا القراءتين، فهو إعلام بأن الله تعالى

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r17.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r17.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r17.claim: The Prophet maintained proper etiquette by not voicing his heart’s wish for a changed qibla, while looking toward heaven as the route of Gabriel.

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r18.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r18.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r18.claim: God knew the Prophet’s unspoken request and changed the qibla for him, describing this as the greatest act a beloved can receive from the Beloved.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r18.anchor: أي علمنا سؤلك عما لم تفصح عنه بلسان الدعاء

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r19.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r19.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r19.claim: Everyone else strives to win God’s pleasure, while God seeks the Prophet’s pleasure by giving him a qibla he likes.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r19.anchor: كل العبيد يجتهدون في طلب رضائي وأنا أطلب رضاك

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r20.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r20.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r20.claim: Believers should face the Kaaba outwardly without attaching their hearts to stones or relics; God alone should be the heart’s witness.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r20.anchor: ولكن لا تعلق قلبك بالأحجار والآثار

QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r21.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r21.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r21.claim: The believers are likewise commanded to face the qibla while purifying their hearts for God and directing their witnessing to Him alone.
QUSHAYRI:v1p73/r21.anchor: ولكن أخلصوا قلوبكم لي وأفردوا شهودكم بي

DURR-FULL:v1p353/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r4.speaker: البراء بن عازب
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r4.claim: Al-Bara reports that after eighteen months praying toward Jerusalem in Medina, Muhammad's longing for the Ka'ba was answered by the qibla change; he asked about earlier prayers, and 2:143 assured him they were preserved.
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r4.anchor: عن البراء قال صلينا مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس ثمانية عشر شهرا وصرفت القبلة إلى الكعبة بعد دخوله المدينة بشهرين

DURR-FULL:v1p353/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r5.claim: Mu'adh says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for seventeen months after arriving in Medina, then God commanded the turn toward the Ka'ba.
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل قال صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعد أن قدم المدينة إلى بيت المقدس سبعة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p353/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Prophet finished praying toward Jerusalem, he raised his head to the sky, and the verse was revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r6.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم من صلاته إلى بيت المقدس رفع رأسه إلى السماء فأنزل الله {قد نرى تقلب وجهك} الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p353/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r7.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r7.claim: Abu Sa'id reports that he and others used to pray in a mosque they passed on the way to the mosque; one day they saw the Prophet seated on the pulpit and he thought an event had occurred.
DURR-FULL:v1p353/r7.anchor: عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال كنا نغدو إلى المسجد على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فنمر على المسجد فنصلي فيه فمررنا يوما ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قاعد على المنبر

NAHHAS:v1p268/r12.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v1p268/r12.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v1p268/r12.claim: تلقاءه is a place adverb, like وجهته; it is accusative as an extra element and because the action occurs there.
NAHHAS:v1p268/r12.anchor: ظرف مكان كما تقول تلقاءه وجهته وانتصب الظرف لأنه فضلة بمنزلة المفعول به

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.speaker: عكرمة والحسن البصري
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.claim: Ikrima and al-Hasan say Muhammad chose Jerusalem, the Jews’ qibla, for 17 months to win them over and attract unschooled Arabs; they call qibla the first abrogated matter and cite 2:115.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r1.anchor: عن عكرمة، وعن يزيد النحوي، عن عكرمة، والحسن البصري، قالا: " أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة، وذلك أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يستقبل صخرة بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya says God gave the Prophet a choice, and he chose Jerusalem to reconcile the People of Scripture; after 16 months, he prayed and looked toward heaven until God directed him to the Sacred House.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r3.anchor: قال الربيع، قال أبو العالية، «إن نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم خير أن يوجه وجهه حيث شاء، فاختار بيت المقدس لكي يتألف أهل الكتاب

TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas gives the alternative that God commanded Jerusalem after the Hijra because most Medinans were Jews; they rejoiced, while Muhammad loved Abraham’s qibla and looked heavenward until 2:144 redirected him, provoking Jewish doubt.
TAB-FULL:v2p623/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قال: " لما هاجر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى المدينة، وكان أكثر أهلها اليهود، أمره الله أن يستقبل بيت المقدس

TABATABAI:2:142/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.claim: The verses form a coherent sequence announcing the Kaaba as the Muslims' qibla; reports alleging disorder or abrogation conflict with the apparent text and should not be accepted.
TABATABAI:2:142/r1.anchor: وهي تنبىء عن جعل الكعبة قبلة للمسلمين فلا يصغى إلى قول من يقول إن فيها تقدما وتأخرا أو إن فيها ناسخا ومنسوخا،

TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r4.speaker: الباقر عليه السلام
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r4.claim: Al-Bāqir explains “turn your face toward the Sacred Mosque” as facing the qibla and warns that turning away from it invalidates prayer.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r4.anchor: وفي تفسير العياشي عن الباقر عليه السلام في قوله تعالى { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام } الآية، قال استقبل القبلة، ولا تقلب وجهك عن القبلة فتفسد صلاتك

TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r5.claim: Numerous reports show that the qibla command was revealed for obligatory prayer and applies specifically to it.
TABATABAI:2:142-151#7/r5.anchor: والأخبار في نزول الآية في الفريضة واختصاصها بها كثيرة مستفيضة

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r1.claim: The change of qiblah was ordained by God, though commentators differ about how Jerusalem first became the qiblah and how the change occurred.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r1.anchor: Though the change in the qiblah was ordained by God, commentators give varying accounts of how Jerusalem came to be the qiblah in the first place

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r2.speaker: a few commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r2.claim: A few say the Prophet chose Jerusalem on his own to establish a bond with local Jews and recent converts to Islam.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r2.anchor: A few have said that the Prophet chose to pray toward Jerusalem of his own accord in order to establish a bond

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r3.speaker: most commentators
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r3.claim: Most accounts say God first instructed the Prophet to face Jerusalem and later commanded him to turn toward Makkah.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r3.anchor: most accounts say that the Prophet was instructed by God to face Jerusalem and then later commanded to change the direction toward Makkah

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r4.speaker: Ṭ
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r4.claim: Commentators say the Prophet hoped for a change because Jews arrogantly claimed he followed their religion and qiblah, which displeased him.

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r5.speaker: R
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r5.claim: Others explain the Prophet's hope by his love of Abraham's House and qiblah, or by hoping the Arabs would be more inclined to Islam if the Kaʿbah were the qiblah.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r5.anchor: Others understand that the hope to change the qiblah stemmed from the Prophet’s love of the House of Abraham and Abraham’s qiblah

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r6.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r6.speaker: al-Ṭabarī
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says the People of the Book know Makkah is the true qiblah for Muslims.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r6.anchor: Al-Ṭabarī says that those who have been given the Book know that it is the truth means that they know that Makkah is the true qiblah for Muslims

STUDYQURAN:2:144/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r7.claim: The author's gloss is that they know more generally the Prophet is right, making their objection to the qiblah change another instance of intransigence.
STUDYQURAN:2:144/r7.anchor: that the Prophet is right and thus that their opposition to the change in the qiblah is but one more example of their intransigence.

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r1.claim: Here taqallub means turning or moving, and fi al-sama means toward and facing the sky.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r1.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {في السماء} [البقرة: 144] نحو السماء وقبلها

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r2.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r2.claim: Qatāda reports that the Prophet looked skyward, wishing God to redirect him to the Kaaba, until God did so.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r2.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء} [البقرة: 144] قال: «كان صلى الله عليه وسلم يقلب وجهه في السماء

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r3.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r3.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem while longing for the Sacred House, so God turned him to the qibla he desired.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r3.anchor: عن قتادة قوله: {قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء} [البقرة: 144] «فكان نبي الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي نحو بيت المقدس

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r4.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r4.claim: Al-Rabīʿ glosses the turning as the Prophet's gaze skyward during prayer toward Jerusalem; God redirected him to the Kaaba he desired.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r4.anchor: عن الربيع، في قوله: {قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء} [البقرة: 144] يقول: نظرك في السماء

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r5.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says that after arriving in Medina eighteen months after the Hijra, the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem and looked upward for an order; the Kaaba replaced that direction, which he wanted.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r5.anchor: عن السدي، قال: " كان الناس يصلون قبل بيت المقدس، فلما قدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة على رأس ثمانية عشر شهرا

TAB-FULL:v2p656/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r6.speaker: قال بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r6.claim: Some say the Prophet disliked facing Jerusalem because Jews taunted him for following their qibla while opposing their religion.
TAB-FULL:v2p656/r6.anchor: قال بعضهم: كره قبلة بيت المقدس، من أجل أن اليهود قالوا. يتبع قبلتنا ويخالفنا في ديننا

TAB-FULL:v2p658/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r1.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r1.claim: Mujāhid reports that the Jews taunted Muhammad for following their qibla; revelation changed it during noon prayer, ending their taunt as men and women exchanged places.
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد، قال: " قالت اليهود: يخالفنا محمد، ويتبع قبلتنا

TAB-FULL:v2p658/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r2.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet initially chose Jerusalem because Jews faced a house of God; after hearing their taunt that he needed their guidance, he looked upward and the qibla changed.
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r2.anchor: سمعته يعني ابن زيد، يقول: " قال الله تعالى ذكره لنبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم. {فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله} [البقرة: 115]

TAB-FULL:v2p658/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet loved Abraham's qibla and would pray for it while looking toward the sky.
TAB-FULL:v2p658/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس: أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة وكان أكثر أهلها اليهود

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī defines shatr as the direction, aim, or facing of the Sacred Mosque.

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r2.speaker: الهذلي
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r2.claim: A Hudhayli line uses shatr-hā, ‘toward it,’ as poetic evidence for shatr meaning direction.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r2.anchor: قال الهذلي: [البحر البسيط] إن العسير بها داء مخامرها … فشطرها نظر العينين محسور

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r3.speaker: ابن أحمر
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r3.claim: Ibn Aḥmar's line uses shatr in the sense of heading toward a place, supporting Al-Ṭabarī's gloss.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r3.anchor: قال ابن أحمر: [البحر البسيط] تعدو بنا شطر جمع وهي عاقدة … قد كارب العقد من إيفادها الحقبا

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r4.speaker: ابن أبي العالية
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r4.claim: Ibn Abī al-ʿĀliya glosses shatr al-masjid as facing it.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r4.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند، عن ابن أبي العالية {شطر المسجد الحرام}

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses shatr al-masjid as toward it.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r5.anchor: عن علي بن أبي طلحة، عن ابن عباس: {شطر المسجد الحرام}

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r6.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r6.claim: Mujāhid likewise glosses the phrase as facing toward the Sacred Mosque.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r6.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} [البقرة: 144] نحوه

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r7.claim: Qatāda says the command means facing toward the Sacred Mosque.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r7.anchor: عن قتادة: { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} [البقرة: 144] أي تلقاء المسجد الحرام

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r8.speaker: الربيع
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r8.claim: Al-Rabīʿ says the command means facing toward the Sacred Mosque.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r8.anchor: عن الربيع: {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} [البقرة: 144] أي تلقاءه

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r9.speaker: البراء
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r9.claim: Al-Barāʾ glosses shatrahu as toward it.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r9.anchor: عن البراء، " {فولوا وجوهكم شطره} [البقرة: 144] قال: قبله "

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r10.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r10.claim: Ibn Zayd explains shatr as its side or direction, adding that its sides are its shatrs.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r10.anchor: قال ابن زيد، {شطره} [البقرة: 144] ناحيته جانبه، قال: وجوانبه: شطوره

TAB-FULL:v2p660/r11.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r11.speaker: قال بعضهم
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r11.claim: One reported view identifies the intended qibla as the direction directly opposite the Kaaba's waterspout.
TAB-FULL:v2p660/r11.anchor: فقال بعضهم: القبلة التي حول إليها النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعناها الله تعالى ذكره بقوله: {فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها} [البقرة: 144] حيال ميزاب الكعبة

TAB-FULL:v2p662/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r1.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r1.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAmr identifies the desired qibla as directly facing the Kaaba's waterspout.
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r1.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو، " {فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها} [البقرة: 144] حيال ميزاب الكعبة "

TAB-FULL:v2p662/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the whole House is a qibla and points to the House's door as its direction.
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس «البيت كله قبلة، وهذه قبلة البيت، يعني التي فيها الباب»

TAB-FULL:v2p662/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī holds that facing toward the Sacred Mosque fulfills the qibla: intention and orientation suffice, like following an imam across a row, provided one is not turned away or facing its back.
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r3.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندي ما قال الله جل ثناؤه: {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} [البقرة: 144] فالمولي وجهه شطر المسجد الحرام هو المصيب القبلة

TAB-FULL:v2p662/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r4.speaker: علي
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r4.claim: ʿAlī glosses shatr as toward it; Al-Ṭabarī adds that the House's qibla is its door.
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r4.anchor: عن علي، {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} [البقرة: 144] قال: شطره قبله

TAB-FULL:v2p662/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r5.claim: Al-Ṭabarī states that the door is the qibla of the House.
TAB-FULL:v2p662/r5.anchor: قال أبو جعفر: وقبلة البيت: بابه

TAB-FULL:v2p665/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r1.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r1.claim: Usāma ibn Zayd reports that the Prophet faced the House's door after leaving it and said twice, ‘This is the qibla.’
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r1.anchor: عن عطاء، قال: قال أسامة بن زيد " رأيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حين خرج من البيت أقبل بوجهه إلى الباب

TAB-FULL:v2p665/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r2.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r2.claim: Usāma reports that the Prophet prayed at the House's door after entering and supplicating in its corners; he called that direction the qibla.
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r2.anchor: أخبرني أسامة بن زيد، " أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما دخل البيت دعا في نواحيه كلها، ولم يصل حتى خرج

TAB-FULL:v2p665/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī concludes from the reports that the House itself is the qibla and its door indicates the qibla.
TAB-FULL:v2p665/r3.anchor: فأخبر صلى الله عليه وسلم أن البيت هو القبلة، وأن قبلة البيت بابه

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says believers anywhere on earth are obligated to face toward the Sacred Mosque in prayer.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r1.anchor: فرض التوجه نحو المسجد الحرام في صلاتهم حيث كانوا من أرض الله تبارك وتعالى

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r2.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r2.claim: The fa in fawallū is the response to the conditional expression ḥaythumā kuntum.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r2.anchor: وأدخلت الفاء في قوله: {فولوا} [البقرة: 144] جوابا للجزاء، وذلك أن قوله: {حيثما كنتم} جزاء

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r3.claim: Al-Ṭabarī identifies the recipients of scripture here as Jewish rabbis and Christian scholars.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r3.anchor: يعني بقوله جل ثناؤه: وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب أحبار اليهود وعلماء النصارى

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r4.speaker: السدي
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says this passage was revealed about the Jews specifically.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r4.anchor: عن السدي: {وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} [البقرة: 144] أنزل ذلك في اليهود

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r5.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r5.claim: The scholars of the People of the Book know that facing the Sacred Mosque is the truth God prescribed for Abraham, his descendants, and later worshippers.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r5.anchor: يعلمون أن التوجه نحو المسجد الحق الذي فرضه الله عز وجل على إبراهيم وذريته، وسائر عباده بعده

TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r6.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r6.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains ‘from their Lord’ as a binding prescription imposed on God's servants, true and from Him.
TAB-FULL:v2p665#2/r6.anchor: ويعني بقوله: {من ربهم} [البقرة: 5] أنه الفرض الواجب على عباد الله تعالى ذكره، وهو الحق من عند ربهم

TABATABAI:2:144/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144/r3.claim: The Prophet looked toward heaven in expectation of revelation and hoped for a qibla that would honor him; this did not mean he disliked Jerusalem.
TABATABAI:2:144/r3.anchor: وإن ذلك كان انتظارا منه، أو توقعا لنزول الوحي في أمر القبلة، لما كان يحب أن يكرمه الله تعالى بقبلة تختص به

TABATABAI:2:144/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144/r4.claim: Being pleased with a new qibla does not entail resentment toward the former one; the Prophet remains above such dissatisfaction.
TABATABAI:2:144/r4.anchor: فإن الرضا بشيء لا يوجب السخط بخلافه بل اليهود على ما في الروايات

TABATABAI:2:144/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r5.speaker: روايات واردة في شأن نزول الآية
TABATABAI:2:144/r5.claim: Reports about the occasion say Jews taunted and boasted that Muslims followed their qibla; grieving, the Prophet went out at night and waited for revelation, after which the verse came.
TABATABAI:2:144/r5.anchor: كانوا يعيرون المسلمين في تبعية قبلتهم، ويتفاخرون بذلك عليهم، فحزن رسول الله ذلك، فخرج في سواد الليل

TABATABAI:2:144/r6.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r6.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144/r6.claim: Keeping the former qibla would have answered the Jews' taunt because the Prophet's obedience was no disgrace; the new qibla instead silenced them and fixed the duty.
TABATABAI:2:144/r6.anchor: لكن نزلت بقبلة جديدة، فقطع تعييرهم وتفاخرهم، مضافا إلى تعيين التكليف، فكانت حجة ورضى

TABATABAI:2:144/r7.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r7.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144/r7.claim: Shatr means a part or side, and the side of the Sacred Mosque in this command is the Kaaba.
TABATABAI:2:144/r7.anchor: الشطر البعض، وشطر المسجد الحرام هو الكعبة

TABATABAI:2:144/r8.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144/r8.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144/r8.claim: The wording parallels the former command toward a side of the Farthest Mosque, replacing its known rock with the Kaaba; naming the Sacred Mosque adds nuances lost by saying Kaaba or Sacred House.
TABATABAI:2:144/r8.anchor: محاذاة للحكم في القبلة السابقة، فإنها كانت شطر المسجد الأقصى، وهي الصخرة المعروفة هناك، فبدلت من شطر المسجد الحرام

TABATABAI:2:144-146/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r1.claim: Addressing the Prophet first and then all believers suggests the qibla changed while he and the Muslims were praying in the mosque; the general command covers every time and place.
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r1.anchor: وتخصيص رسول الله بالحكم أولا بقوله فول وجهك، ثم تعميم الحكم له ولغيره من المؤمنين بقوله وحيث ما كنتم يؤيد

TABATABAI:2:144-146/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r2.claim: People of the Book know the ruling is true either because their books attest the Prophet's truth or because they identify his qibla; either way scripture contains it explicitly or implicitly, yet they conceal it.
TABATABAI:2:144-146/r2.anchor: وذلك لاشتمال كتابهم على صدق نبوة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم، أو كون قبلة هذا النبي الصادق هو شطر المسجد الحرام

TABRISI:2:144/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:144/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Muslims faced Jerusalem for seventeen months after the Prophet arrived in Medina.
TABRISI:2:144/r1.anchor: وعن ابن عباس كانت الصلاة إلى بيت المقدس بعد مقدم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة سبعة عشر شهرا

TABRISI:2:144/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r2.speaker: البراء بن عازب
TABRISI:2:144/r2.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib reports praying with the Prophet toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months before they were turned toward the Kaaba; Muslim includes the report in his Ṣaḥīḥ.

TABRISI:2:144/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r3.speaker: أنس بن مالك
TABRISI:2:144/r3.claim: Anas ibn Mālik gives the Jerusalem prayer period as nine or ten months.
TABRISI:2:144/r3.anchor: وعن أنس بن مالك: إنما كان ذلك تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر

TABRISI:2:144/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
TABRISI:2:144/r4.claim: Muʿādh ibn Jabal gives the period as thirteen months.
TABRISI:2:144/r4.anchor: وعن معاذ بن جبل ثلاثة عشر شهرا

TABRISI:2:144/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r5.speaker: الصادق
TABRISI:2:144/r5.claim: A report from al-Ṣādiq says the Prophet faced Jerusalem for thirteen years in Mecca and seven months in Medina; Jews taunted him, so he grieved and awaited revelation. Gabriel turned him toward the Kaaba during noon prayer at Banū Sālim's mosque after two rakʿas; he completed two facing the Kaaba, prompting Jewish and foolish criticism.
TABRISI:2:144/r5.anchor: ورواه علي بن إبراهيم بإسناده عن الصادق ع قال:

TABRISI:2:144/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144/r6.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:144/r6.claim: Al-Zajjāj explains that Jerusalem was initially appointed because Arabs were accustomed to pilgrimage to the Kaaba; God tested who would follow the Messenger despite a different direction.
TABRISI:2:144/r6.anchor: قال الزجاج: إنما أمر بالصلاة إلى بيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:144#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r1.claim: Ruʾya first means visual perception, like seeing, and is also used for knowledge.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r1.anchor: الرؤية هي إدراك الشيء بالبصر ونظيره الإبصار ثم تستعمل بمعنى العلم

TABRISI:2:144#2/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r2.claim: Taqallub, change, and disposition are synonyms describing movement in different directions.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r2.anchor: والتقلب والتحول والتصرف نظائر وهو التحرك في الجهات

TABRISI:2:144#2/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r3.claim: Wallaytuka al-qibla means I made you face the qibla; the verb here is distinct from walaytu al-dār, which only means that a house adjoins another.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r3.anchor: ويقال وليتك القبلة أي صيرتك تستقبلها بوجهك وليس هذا المعنى في فعلت منه لأنك تقول وليت الدار

TABRISI:2:144#2/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r4.claim: The verb is also used for turning one's back, as in 54:45 and 3:111, from expressions meaning that one side of a house lies next to another or that someone turns toward a side.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r4.anchor: وقد جاءت هذه الكلمة مستعملة على خلاف المقابلة والمواجهة

TABRISI:2:144#2/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r5.claim: Riḍā and love are near in meaning but contrasted with different opposites: love with hatred, satisfaction with displeasure; divine satisfaction signifies willing honor and reward.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r5.anchor: والرضا والمحبة نظيران وإنما يظهر الفرق بضديهما فالمحبة ضدها البغض والرضا ضده السخط

TABRISI:2:144#2/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r6.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r6.claim: Shatr means toward or in the direction of; a cited couplet uses it for toward a border or target.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r6.anchor: وشطر المسجد الحرام أي نحوه وتلقاءه

TABRISI:2:144#2/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r7.speaker: الزجاج
TABRISI:2:144#2/r7.claim: Al-Zajjāj says shāṭarūnā means that people's houses adjoin ours; yanāḥūnanā similarly means we are oriented toward one another.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r7.anchor: قال الزجاج: يقال هؤلاء القوم مشاطرونا أي دورهم تتصل بدورنا

TABRISI:2:144#2/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r8.speaker: صاحب العين
TABRISI:2:144#2/r8.claim: Ṣāḥib al-ʿAyn says shatr can mean half or direction and aim; an idiom uses it for half a milking, and shatartu means divided something.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r8.anchor: وقال صاحب العين: شطر كل شيء نصفه وشطره نحوه وقصده

TABRISI:2:144#2/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r9.claim: Ḥarām means forbidden, just as kitāb means written and ḥisāb means reckoned.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r9.anchor: والحرام المحرم كما أن الكتاب بمعنى المكتوب والحساب بمعنى المحسوب

TABRISI:2:144#2/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r10.claim: Al-ḥaqq is putting a thing in its proper place where there is no aspect of ugliness.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r10.anchor: والحق وضع الشيء في موضعه إذا لم يكن فيه وجه من وجه القبح

TABRISI:2:144#2/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r11.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r11.claim: Ghafla is inattention to particular things; broad inattention is more extensive, and calling a sleeper heedless is figurative.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r11.anchor: والغفلة هي السهو عن بعض الأشياء خاصة وإذا كان السهو عاما فهو فوق الغفلة

TABRISI:2:144#2/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r12.claim: Ḥaythumā kuntum is conditional, with the sense wherever you may be; its response is fa-wallū and what follows. Ḥaythu and idhā need mā to detach them from their following clause and enable conditional jussive syntax.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r12.anchor: حيث ما كنتم موضع كنتم جزم بالشرط وتقديره وحيثما تكونوا والفاء وما بعده في موضع الجزاء

TABRISI:2:144#2/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r13.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#2/r13.claim: Shatrahu is accusative as an adverb of direction.

TABRISI:2:144#2/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#2/r14.speaker: المفسرون
TABRISI:2:144#2/r14.claim: Exegetes report that the Kaaba was the Prophet's preferred direction. He asked Gabriel to seek a change from the Jewish qibla; Gabriel told him to pray to God, and the Prophet watched the sky awaiting revelation.
TABRISI:2:144#2/r14.anchor: قال المفسرون كانت الكعبة أحب القبلتين إلى رسول الله

TABRISI:2:144#3/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r1.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r1.claim: God sees Muhammad looking toward the sky while he awaits revelation about the qibla.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r1.anchor: يا محمد { في السماء } لانتظار الوحي في أمر القبلة

TABRISI:2:144#3/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r2.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:144#3/r2.claim: One explanation says the Prophet had been promised a change of qibla and looked toward the expected source of the awaited revelation, as people watch for what they expect.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r2.anchor: أحدهما: أنه كان وعد بتحويل القبلة عن بيت المقدس فكان يفعل ذلك انتظارا وتوقعا للموعود

TABRISI:2:144#3/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r3.speaker: قيل
TABRISI:2:144#3/r3.claim: Another explanation says he disliked Jerusalem and favored the Kaaba but could not ask God without permission: prophets must not request what they have not been authorized to ask, lest its refusal become a trial for their people.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r3.anchor: والثاني: أنه كان يكره قبلة بيت المقدس ويهوى قبلة الكعبة وكان لا يسأل الله تعالى ذلك

TABRISI:2:144#3/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:144#3/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet wanted the Kaaba because it was the qibla of his forefather Abraham and his ancestors.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r4.anchor: قبلة أبيه إبراهيم ع وقبلة آبائه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:144#3/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TABRISI:2:144#3/r5.claim: Mujāhid says Jews taunted that Muhammad differed from their religion yet followed their qibla.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r5.anchor: يخالفنا محمد في ديننا ويتبع قبلتنا عن مجاهد

TABRISI:2:144#3/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
TABRISI:2:144#3/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd says Jews claimed Muhammad and his companions did not know their qibla until the Jews guided them.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r6.anchor: أين قبلتهم حتى هديناهم عن ابن زيد

TABRISI:2:144#3/r7.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r7.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r7.claim: Another explanation is that Arabs deeply revered the Kaaba, so facing it would draw their hearts and make them more eager to pray toward it; the Prophet was keen to call them to Islam.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r7.anchor: كانت العرب يحبون الكعبة ويعظمونها غاية التعظيم

TABRISI:2:144#3/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r8.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r8.claim: The author allows that all these reasons together may explain the Prophet's preference because they do not conflict.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون إنما أحب ذلك لجميع هذه الوجوه إذ لا تنافي بينها

TABRISI:2:144#3/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r9.claim: God promises to turn Muhammad toward a qibla he wants and naturally loves; this does not mean he resented the first qibla.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r9.anchor: أي فلنصرفنك إلى قبلة تريدها وتحبها وإنما أراد به محبة الطباع

TABRISI:2:144#3/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r10.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r10.claim: Turn yourself toward the Sacred Mosque: wajh can mean the person himself, and the face is named because it visibly expresses orientation.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r10.anchor: أي حول نفسك نحو المسجد الحرام لأن وجه الشيء نفسه

TABRISI:2:144#3/r11.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r11.speaker: أبو علي الجبائي
TABRISI:2:144#3/r11.claim: Al-Jubbāʾī takes shatr to mean half, so the command targets half of the mosque directly opposite the Kaaba; the author rejects this as contrary to the exegetes' view.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r11.anchor: وقال أبو علي الجبائي: أراد بالشطر النصف فأمره الله تعالى بالتوجه إلى نصف المسجد الحرام

TABRISI:2:144#3/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r12.claim: Wherever people are on earth—land or sea, plain or mountain—they should face the Kaaba. The first command addresses the Prophet and Medina; the second extends the qibla to every worshipper across the world.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r12.anchor: أي أينما كنتم من الأرض في بر أو بحر وسهلا سهل أو جبل فولوا وجوهكم نحوه

TABRISI:2:144#3/r13.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r13.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:144#3/r13.claim: Al-Thaʿlabī quotes Ibn ʿAbbās: the House is qibla for the doorway, the House for mosque-goers, the mosque for the Sacred Precinct, and the Precinct for the whole earth. This matches the Imāmī view that the Precinct is qibla for those far away.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r13.anchor: وذكر أبو إسحاق الثعلبي في كتابه عن ابن عباس

TABRISI:2:144#3/r14.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r14.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r14.claim: Those given scripture refers either to Jewish scholars or to Jewish and Christian scholars together.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r14.anchor: أراد به علماء اليهود وقيل علماء اليهود والنصارى

TABRISI:2:144#3/r15.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#3/r15.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#3/r15.claim: They know that changing the qibla to the Kaaba is commanded truth from their Lord because their prophets' glad tidings described a prophet whose traits included praying toward both qiblas.
TABRISI:2:144#3/r15.anchor: أي يعلمون أن تحويل القبلة إلى الكعبة حق مأمور به من ربهم

TABRISI:2:144#4/r1.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r1.speaker: اليهود
TABRISI:2:144#4/r1.claim: The Jews objected that Muhammad had not been ordered to change direction and was inventing it himself, turning now one way and now another; the verse answers that they know this claim is false.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r1.anchor: وروي أنهم قالوا عند التحويل ما أمرت بهذا يا محمد وإنما هو شيء تبتدعه من تلقاء نفسك مرة إلى هنا ومرة إلى هنا

TABRISI:2:144#4/r2.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r2.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#4/r2.claim: God is aware of their concealment of Muhammad's description and their deliberate opposition. The addressed group must be small enough to collude and display beliefs contrary to what they know; such unified collusion is not plausible for a vast group.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r2.anchor: ليس الله بغافل عما يعمل هؤلاء من كتمان صفة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم

TABRISI:2:144#4/r3.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r3.speaker: author
TABRISI:2:144#4/r3.claim: The verse abrogates the obligation to face Jerusalem.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r3.anchor: وهذه الآية ناسخة لفرض التوجه إلى بيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:144#4/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:2:144#4/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the first abrogation mentioned in the Quran was the qibla matter.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r4.anchor: وقال ابن عباس أول ما نسخ من القرآن

TABRISI:2:144#4/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r5.speaker: قتادة
TABRISI:2:144#4/r5.claim: Qatāda says this verse abrogated what came before it.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r5.anchor: وقال قتادة نسخت هذه الآية ما قبلها

TABRISI:2:144#4/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r6.speaker: جعفر بن مبشر
TABRISI:2:144#4/r6.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Mubashshir says the Quran abrogated a Sunna; the author regards this as strongest because no Quranic text establishes the Jerusalem direction as obligatory.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r6.anchor: وقال جعفر بن مبشر هذا مما نسخ من السنة بالقرآن وهذا هو الأقوى

TABRISI:2:144#4/r8.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r8.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:144#4/r8.claim: One view says the Prophet prayed toward the Kaaba in Mecca, was commanded to face Jerusalem after migrating to Medina, then was turned back to the Kaaba.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r8.anchor: واختلف الناس في صلاة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى بيت المقدس

TABRISI:2:144#4/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r9.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:144#4/r9.claim: Another view says that in Mecca the Prophet faced Jerusalem while placing the Kaaba between himself and it, praying only where that alignment was possible.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r9.anchor: وقال قوم كان يصلي بمكة إلى بيت المقدس إلا أنه كان يجعل الكعبة بينه وبينها

TABRISI:2:144#4/r10.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:2:144#4/r10.speaker: قوم
TABRISI:2:144#4/r10.claim: A third view says the Prophet faced Jerusalem in Mecca and after arriving in Medina without needing to place the Kaaba between himself and it, until he was commanded to face the Kaaba.
TABRISI:2:144#4/r10.anchor: وقال قوم بل كان يصلي بمكة وبعد قدومه المدينة إلى بيت المقدس ولم يكن عليه أن يجعل

THALABI:v2p10/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r1.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p10/r1.claim: The qibla was the first ritual ruling abrogated: in Mecca the Prophet and Companions faced the Kaaba, then in Medina God directed them toward Jerusalem's rock to make Jews more likely to affirm him, since scripture described him; this is the majority view.
THALABI:v2p10/r1.anchor: إن أول ما نسخ من أمور الشرع أمر القبلة

THALABI:v2p10/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r2.speaker: عبد الرحمن بن زيد
THALABI:v2p10/r2.claim: Ibn Zayd says the earlier verse about turning wherever one wishes led the Prophet to say that Jews face one of God's houses, so he would face it too; he then turned toward Jerusalem.
THALABI:v2p10/r2.anchor: وقال عبد الرحمن بن زيد: قال الله لنبيه صلى الله عليه وسلم: فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله

THALABI:v2p10/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r3.speaker: المفسرون
THALABI:v2p10/r3.claim: The exegetes say the Prophet and Companions prayed toward Jerusalem for seventeen months, while the Ansar had faced it for two years before his arrival.
THALABI:v2p10/r3.anchor: فصلى النبي وأصحابه نحو بيت المقدس سبعة عشر شهرا وكانت الأنصار قد صلت إلى بيت المقدس سنتين

THALABI:v2p10/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p10/r4.claim: The Kaaba was the Prophet's more beloved of the two qiblas; the exegetes differ over why he disliked Jerusalem and longed for it.
THALABI:v2p10/r4.anchor: وكانت الكعبة أحب القبلتين إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v2p10/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p10/r5.claim: Ibn Abbas says he preferred the Kaaba because it had been Abraham's qibla.
THALABI:v2p10/r5.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: لأنها كانت قبلة إبراهيم عليه الصلاة والسلام

THALABI:v2p10/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r6.speaker: مجاهد
THALABI:v2p10/r6.claim: Mujahid says the Jews' taunt that Muhammad opposed their religion yet followed their qibla motivated his longing for change.
THALABI:v2p10/r6.anchor: مجاهد: من أجل أن اليهود قالوا: يخالفنا محمد في ديننا ويتبع قبلتنا

THALABI:v2p10/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p10/r7.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان
THALABI:v2p10/r7.claim: Muqatil ibn Hayyan says the Jews boasted that Muhammad followed their qibla and practice, claiming that if his prophethood were real they had the prior and greater claim; hearing this distressed him and increased his desire for the Kaaba.
THALABI:v2p10/r7.anchor: مقاتل بن حيان: لما أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أن يصلي نحو بيت المقدس

THALABI:v2p11/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r1.speaker: ابن زيد
THALABI:v2p11/r1.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet heard Jews claim that he and his Companions did not know their qibla until the Jews guided them.
