THALABI:v2p11/r1.anchor: ابن زيد: لما استقبل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بيت المقدس بلغه أن اليهود

THALABI:v2p11/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r2.speaker: النبي
THALABI:v2p11/r2.claim: The Prophet told Gabriel he wished God would redirect him from the Jews' qibla because he hated them and their conformity; Gabriel said he had no authority and told him to ask God, then ascended while the Prophet watched the sky for revelation.
THALABI:v2p11/r2.anchor: فقال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لجبرئيل: «وددت أن الله صرفني من قبلة اليهود

THALABI:v2p11/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r3.claim: The phrase describes Muhammad repeatedly turning and directing his face toward the sky.
THALABI:v2p11/r3.anchor: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء تحول وتصرف وجهك يا محمد في السماء

THALABI:v2p11/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r4.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r4.claim: The verb means that God will turn and redirect him.

THALABI:v2p11/r5.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r5.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r5.claim: The qibla is one the Prophet loves and approves.

THALABI:v2p11/r6.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r6.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r6.claim: Shatr means toward it and intending it; grammatically it is an adverbial expression.
THALABI:v2p11/r6.anchor: أي: نحوهم وهو نصب على الظرف

THALABI:v2p11/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r7.speaker: الشاعر
THALABI:v2p11/r7.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses shatr to mean toward, serving as linguistic evidence.
THALABI:v2p11/r7.anchor:
قال الشاعر:
واطعن بالقوم شطر الملوك

THALABI:v2p11/r8.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r8.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r8.claim: The phrase means the sacred or prohibited mosque; the author compares it to kitāb meaning written and ḥisāb meaning counted.
THALABI:v2p11/r8.anchor: والمسجد الحرام: المحرم كالكتاب بمعنى المكتوب والحساب بمعنى المحسوب

THALABI:v2p11/r9.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r9.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r9.claim: Wherever people are—land, sea, plain, mountain, east, or west—they must face the Kaaba; the change came in Rajab after noon, two months before Badr.
THALABI:v2p11/r9.anchor: في بر أو بحر أو سهل أو جبل شرق أو غرب فولوا وجوهكم شطره فحول القبلة في رجب بعد زوال الشمس

THALABI:v2p11/r10.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r10.speaker: مجاهد وغيره
THALABI:v2p11/r10.claim: Mujahid and others say the verse came at Banu Salama's mosque during noon prayer: after two rakʿas the Prophet turned toward the water spout, men and women exchanged places, and it became the Mosque of Two Qiblas.
THALABI:v2p11/r10.anchor: مجاهد وغيره: نزلت هذه الآية ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

THALABI:v2p11/r11.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r11.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v2p11/r11.claim: Ibn Abbas gives a hierarchy: the whole House is qibla, its door direction is the House's qibla, the House is the mosque's qibla, and the sanctuary is qibla for Earth's inhabitants.
THALABI:v2p11/r11.anchor: قال ابن عباس: البيت كله قبلة وقبلة البيت الباب والبيت قبلة أهل المسجد والمسجد قبلة أهل الحرم

THALABI:v2p11/r12.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r12.speaker: قتادة
THALABI:v2p11/r12.claim: Qatada says the Jews argued that if Muhammad had remained on their qibla they might have expected him to be their awaited companion, but they saw him turn to the Kaaba, a structure of stones.
THALABI:v2p11/r12.anchor: قتادة: فصلى إلى بيت المقدس وتارة يصلي إلى الكعبة ولو ثبت على قبلتنا لكنا نرجو أن تكون صاحبنا

THALABI:v2p11/r13.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r13.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r13.claim: Those given scripture know the command to face the Kaaba is true from God because it is Abraham's qibla.
THALABI:v2p11/r13.anchor: يعني أمر الكعبة الحق. من ربهم وإنها قبلة إبراهيم

THALABI:v2p11/r14.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r14.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن ... والكسائي
THALABI:v2p11/r14.claim: Abu Jaʿfar, an incompletely named reader, and al-Kisa'i read the clause with second-person tāʾ; the others use third-person yāʾ, referring to what the Jews do, for which God will requite them.
THALABI:v2p11/r14.anchor: قرأ ابو جعفر وابن ... والكسائي بالتاء وقال بريد

THALABI:v2p11/r15.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v2p11/r15.speaker: author
THALABI:v2p11/r15.claim: On the majority reading with yāʾ, God is not unaware of what the Jews do and will recompense them in this life and the next.
THALABI:v2p11/r15.anchor: يعني ما الله بغافل عما يعمل اليهود فأجازيهم في الدنيا والآخرة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r1.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r1.claim: Commentators say the Kaaba was the Prophet's preferred one of the two qiblas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r1.anchor: قال المفسرون: كانت الكعبة أحب القبلتين إلى رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Kaaba was dear to the Prophet because it had been the qibla of his father Abraham.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لأنها كانت قبلة أبيه إبراهيم (¬6).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r3.speaker: مجاهد، مقاتل، ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r3.claim: Mujahid, Muqatil, and Ibn Zayd say he preferred it because he disliked following the Jews.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r3.anchor: وقال مجاهد (¬7) ومقاتل (¬8) وابن زيد (¬9): لأنه كره موافقة اليهود (¬10).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r4.speaker: عامة المفسرين
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r4.claim: Most commentators say the Prophet and his companions faced the Kaaba in Mecca, then were directed in Medina toward Jerusalem's rock to make the Jews more likely to believe him when he faced their qibla.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r4.anchor: وقال عامة المفسرين: إن رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - وأصحابه كانوا بمكة يصلون إلى الكعبة، فلما هاجروا إلى المدينة

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Prophet cited 2:115 and reasoned that the Jews faced one of God's houses, so Muslims should face it; he did so for seventeen months.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r5.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: قال الله لنبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: {فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله} فقال: هؤلاء اليهود يستقبلون بيتا من بيوت الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r6.speaker: ابن زيد
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r6.claim: Ibn Zayd recounts that the Prophet wanted the qibla changed to draw his people toward Islam, asked Gabriel to pray for it, and kept looking skyward until this revelation came.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r6.anchor: وقال ابن زيد: قال الله لنبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: {فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله} فقال: هؤلاء اليهود يستقبلون بيتا من بيوت الله

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r7.speaker: أصحاب المعاني
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r7.claim: The phrase can mean the turning of the Prophet's eyes, with faces used for eyes as in 75:22–23, or the turning of his whole face along with his eyes.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p385/r7.anchor: قال أصحاب المعاني: أراد: تقلب عينيك، فذكرهما بلفظ الوجه، كما ذكر الأعين بلفظ الوجوه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r1.claim: In the sky means the Prophet was looking toward the sky.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {في السماء} أي: في النظر إلى السماء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r2.claim: The causative form wallaytuka al-qibla means that God made the Prophet turn his face toward the qibla; ordinary walaytu a wall does not itself mean facing it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فلنولينك قبلة} يقال، وليتك القبلة،: إذا صيرته يستقبلها (¬2) بوجهه

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r3.claim: The facing sense is an added semantic feature of wallaytuka, not a transfer from the intransitive pattern; unlike alqaytu from laqiya, it takes a preposition before the second object, as in placing one thing upon another.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r3.anchor: ولكن المعنى الذي هو المواجهة عارض (¬3) في فعلت، ولم يكن في (فعلت)، وإذا كان كذلك كان فيه دلالة على أن النقل لم يكن من فعلت

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r4.claim: Tawalla can mean turning away in the cited Qur'anic examples; the unaugmented forms also mean turning away, with mudbirin an emphatic circumstantial description. The augmented forms may denote leaving a direction, or the root may be an antonym meaning either turn toward or away.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p387/r4.anchor: وقد جاءت هذه الكلمة مستعملة على خلاف المقابلة والمواجهة، وذلك نحو: {ثم توليتم إلا قليلا منكم} [البقرة: 83]

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r1.claim: The Prophet desired and loved the Kaaba as qibla, although he was content with the first qibla and obedient while praying toward it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {ترضاها} أي: تحبها وتهواها (¬1)؛ لأن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - كان راضيا بالقبلة الأولى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r2.claim: The command means turn your face toward the qibla.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r2.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {فول وجهك} أي: أقبل وجهك نحوه.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r3.claim: Shatr means toward or in the direction of; anonymous lines and a line by Sadif use it for heading toward kings, Banu Tamim, and Iraq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r3.anchor: وأظعن بالقوم شطر الملوك ... حتى إذا خفق المجدح (¬5)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r4.speaker: سديف
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r4.claim: Sadif's line uses shatr for direction, telling someone to set his course toward Iraq.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r4.anchor: أقم قصد وجهك شطر العراق ... وخال الخليفة فاستمطر (¬1)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r5.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r5.claim: Abu Ishaq says Arab linguists agree that shatr means toward; shatir describes someone who has taken a skewed direction, and shatra is an adverb of place.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p389/r5.anchor: قال أبو اسحاق: لا اختلاف بين أهل اللغة أن الشطر معناه: النحو. قال: وقول الناس: فلان شاطر، معناه: إنه قد أخذ في نحو غير الاستواء.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r1.claim: Al-Haram means forbidden; the sanctuary is so named because restrictions apply there that do not apply elsewhere.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r1.anchor: وقوله تعالى: {الحرام} بمعنى المحرم، وأصله: من المنع، وسميت تلك البقعة حراما لما منع فيها من أشياء

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r2.claim: Wherever you are includes land and sea; the author points to his discussion of hayth at 2:199.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r2.anchor: {وحيث ما كنتم} في بر أو بحر (¬4)، وذكرنا الكلام في حيث عند قوله: {ثم أفيضوا من حيث أفاض الناس} [البقرة: 199].

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r3.claim: The phrase is elliptical: wherever you are and when you intend prayer, turn your faces toward the sanctuary.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r3.anchor: {فولوا وجوهكم شطره} فيه إضمار واختصار، أي: وحيثما كنتم، وأردتم الصلاة، فولوا وجوهكم شطره.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r4.speaker: المفسرون
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r4.claim: Commentators say the qibla command was the first matter of religious law to be abrogated.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون: إن أول ما نسخ من أمور الشرع أمر القبلة (¬5).

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r5.claim: The verse came during noon prayer at Banu Salama after two rakʿas; the Prophet turned toward the Kaaba and men and women exchanged places, so the mosque became known as the Mosque of the Two Qiblas.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r5.anchor: نزلت ورسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في مسجد بني سلمة، وقد صلى بأصحابه (¬1) ركعتين من صلاة الظهر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r6.claim: After the qibla changed, Jews accused Muhammad of inventing it; God then declared that the People of the Book knew the truth of the new direction.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r6.anchor: فلما حولت القبلة إلى الكعبة قالت اليهود: يا محمد، ما أمرت بهذا، وإنما هو شيء تبتدعه من تلقاء نفسك! فأنزل الله سبحانه:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r7.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Sacred Mosque: the People of the Book know it is Abraham's qibla and is true.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r7.anchor: والكناية في {أنه} يجوز أن ترجع إلى المسجد الحرام، أي: إنهم عالمون أن المسجد الحرام قبلة إبراهيم

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r8.claim: Alternatively, the pronoun refers to the turning toward the new qibla, since the promise to turn the Prophet implies that verbal noun; the author compares this ellipsis with 3:180.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r8.anchor: ويجوز أن تعود الكناية إلى التولية (¬1)، لأن قوله: {فلنولينك} دل على المصدر

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r9.speaker: أبو عمرو الدوري عن الكسائي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r9.claim: Al-Duri reports from al-Kisa'i that the pronoun refers to shatr: the direction toward which the community turned is the truth from its Lord.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p390/r9.anchor: وحكى ابن الأنباري: أن أبا عمرو الدوري روى عن الكسائي: أن الهاء تعود على الشطر (¬2)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p392/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p392/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p392/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says believers seek God's approval and will receive their reward, while Jews seek His displeasure and will face disgrace in this world and the next; God is heedful of both.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v3p392/r1.anchor: قال ابن عباس: يريد أنكم يا معشر المؤمنين تطلبون مرضاتي، وما أنا بغافل عن ثوابكم وجزائكم.

QASHANI:2:144/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r1.claim: The Prophet turns toward the sky of spirit in the station of unity, absorbed in oneness and veiled from creation; the burdens of prophecy and calling make return to people difficult before he is firmly established in subsistence after annihilation.
QASHANI:2:144/r1.anchor: في جهة سماء الروح في مقام الجمع عند الاستغراق في الوحدة والاحتجاب بالحق عن الخلق

QASHANI:2:144/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r2.claim: The desired qibla is the heart's direction through an opened breast: unity there appears in differentiated form without being obscured by multiplicity, enabling the Prophet to invite people while retaining the witness of unity.
QASHANI:2:144/r2.anchor: فلنجعلن وجهك يلي قبلة القلب بانشراح الصدر

QASHANI:2:144/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r3.claim: The Sacred Mosque signifies the side of the opened chest, protected from the qualities of the lower self and the promptings of desire and Satan.
QASHANI:2:144/r3.anchor: جانب الصدر المشروح المحرم من وصول صفات النفس، ودواعي الهوى والشيطان

QASHANI:2:144/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r4.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r4.claim: Believers and knowers turn toward that side whether in the east of spirit or west of soul: in the former it eases enjoining right and forbidding wrong; in the latter it enables ascent and protection from desire and satanic veiling.
QASHANI:2:144/r4.anchor: أيها المؤمنون والمحققون، سواء كنتم في جهة مشرق الروح ومغرب النفس

QASHANI:2:144/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r5.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r5.claim: The given books include Torah, Gospel, and the discriminating book of acquired intellect; their guidance shows unity of acts and attributes and points to Muhammad's essential unity.

QASHANI:2:144/r6.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:2:144/r6.speaker: author
QASHANI:2:144/r6.claim: They can also know the truth through intellect illuminated by revealed light, rather than intellect veiled by speculative analogy.
QASHANI:2:144/r6.anchor: أو بنور العقل المنور بالنور الشرعي لا المحجوب بالقياس الفكري

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r1.claim: The Kaaba was the Prophet's preferred qibla and he thought facing it would draw his people toward Islam; he asked Gabriel to request a change. Gabriel told him to ask God, and the Prophet kept looking skyward until the verse came.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r1.anchor: كانت الكعبة أحب القبلتين إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، ورأى أن الصلاة إليها أدعى لقومه إلى الإسلام، فقال لجبريل عليه السلام:

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r2.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r2.claim: The Prophet's turning his face to the sky means looking toward heaven.

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r3.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r3.claim: God will turn him means make him face a qibla he loves and desires.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r3.anchor: { فلنولينك } فلنصيرنك تستقبل { قبلة ترضاها } تحبها وتهواها

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r4.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r4.claim: Turn your face means direct it toward, toward the sanctuary.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r4.anchor: { فول وجهك } أي: أقبل بوجهك { شطر المسجد الحرام } نحوه وتلقاءه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r5.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r5.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r5.claim: Wherever you are, on land or sea, when praying, face the sanctuary.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r5.anchor: { وحيثما كنتم } في بر أو بحر وأردتم الصلاة { فولوا وجوهكم شطره }

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r6.speaker: اليهود
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r6.claim: When the qibla changed to the Kaaba, Jews claimed Muhammad had not been commanded to do it and had invented it.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r6.anchor: فلما تحولت القبلة إلى الكعبة قالت اليهود: يا محمد ما أمرت بهذا، وإنما هو شيء تبتدعه من تلقاء نفسك،

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r7.claim: The People of the Book know the sanctuary is the true qibla and the qibla of Abraham.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r7.anchor: { وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق } أن المسجد الحرام قبلة إبراهيم وأنه لحق

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r8.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r8.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r8.claim: The closing address concerns believers who seek God's pleasure.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r8.anchor: يا معشر المؤمنين من طلب مرضاتي

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r9.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r9.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r9.claim: Gabriel said he was only a servant like the Prophet and that the Prophet was honored by God, so he should ask Him; after Gabriel left, the Prophet kept looking skyward until the change came.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:2:144/r9.anchor: إنما أنا عبد مثلك، وأنت كريم على ربك فسله، ثم ارتفع جبريل عليه السلام وجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يديم النظر إلى السماء

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r1.claim: Abraham, forefather of the prophets representing the three great religions and pioneer of monotheism, built the Kaaba as a sanctuary, making it the most worthy qibla.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r1.anchor: Kâbe üç büyük dinin temsilcisi olan peygamberlerin atası ve tevhid inancının öncüsü durumundaki Hz. İbrâhim tarafından bir mâbed olarak inşa edilmişti

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r2.claim: As qibla, the Kaaba would become the unifying focus of monotheism toward which Muslims direct prayer to the one God.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r2.anchor: Kâbe kıble olarak benimsenmekle, bütün müslümanların bir olan Allah’a karşı ifa ettikleri en yüce ibadet sayılan namazda yönelecekleri bir tevhid odağı haline gelecekti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r3.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r3.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r3.claim: The next step after making the Kaaba qibla was to remove its idols and restore it, as at its founding, as the center and symbol of monotheism.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r3.anchor: bu kutsal mekânın putlardan arındırılmasına, böylece –ilk kuruluşunda olduğu gibi– her yönüyle tevhidin merkezi ve sembolü hüviyetine yeniden kavuşmasına gelecekti.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r4.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r4.speaker: Fahreddin er-Râzî
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r4.claim: Razi suggests that Muslims praying toward Jerusalem may have emboldened the Jews.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r4.anchor: müslümanların Kudüs’e doğru namaz kılmaları muhtemelen yahudileri de şımartıyordu (bk. Râzî, IV, 109).

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r5.claim: Islam preserves universal truths from earlier scriptural religions yet brings a new system of values suited to human dignity, not imitation of an older tradition; appearing to imitate Jews of a corrupted religion likely troubled the Prophet.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r5.anchor: İslâm, eski kitâbî dinlerdeki evrensel doğruları devam ettirmekle birlikte, hiçbir eski geleneğin taklidi olmayan, yepyeni ve insanlık onuruna en uygun değerler getiren bir sistemdi.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r6.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r6.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r6.claim: The change had major religious and political importance: the Prophet yearned for the Kaaba in his homeland Mecca, which he had been forced to leave, and God fulfilled his wish; from then on Muslims were obligated to pray toward the Sacred Mosque.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r6.anchor: Nihayet yüce Allah, “İşte şimdi kesin olarak seni memnun olacağın kıbleye döndürüyoruz. Artık yüzünü Mescid-i Harâm tarafına çevir; nerede olursanız olun yüzünüzü o yöne çevirin” buyruğu ile resulünün bu özlemini gerçekleştirdi

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r7.claim: The prevailing interpretation takes the truth known by the People of the Book, or by their religious scholars in some commentaries, to be the ruling that changed the qibla.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r7.anchor: Ağırlıklı görüşe göre Ehl-i kitabın, bazı müfessirlere göre onların din adamları ve âlimlerinin de bildiği ifade edilen “gerçek”ten maksat, kıblenin değiştirilmesiyle ilgili hükümdür.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r8.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r8.speaker: İbn Atıyye
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r8.claim: Ibn Atiyya says Jews and Christians knew from their scriptures that the Kaaba was Abraham's qibla and, as followers of Muhammad, all were obliged to face it.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r8.anchor: İbn Atıyye bu hususta şöyle demektedir: “Yahudiler ve hıristiyanlar Kâbe’nin, ümmetlerin imamı İbrâhim’in kıblesi olduğunu

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r9.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r9.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r9.claim: Despite knowing this, the People of the Book reacted wrongly to the qibla change; the closing statement that God is not unaware of their deeds warns and threatens them.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:2:144/r9.anchor: Âyetin sonundaki “Allah onların yaptıklarından habersiz değildir” cümlesi, Ehl-i kitabın bu yanlış tutumlarıyla ilgili bir uyarı ve tehdit anlamı taşımaktadır.

BURHAN:v2p37/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.speaker: author
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.claim: Zarkashī adds the qibla passages as another case: the earlier-positioned prediction سيقول السفهاء is abrogated by the later-positioned command to face the Sacred Mosque.
BURHAN:v2p37/r6.anchor: قلت وذكر بعضهم موضعا آخر وهو قوله تعالى ﴿ سيقول السفهاء من الناس ما ولاهم عن قبلتهم التي كانوا عليها ﴾

BURHAN:v4p308/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r1.speaker: جماعة من المتأخرين
BURHAN:v4p308/r1.claim: Some later scholars assign قد an unusual sense of abundance; al-Zamakhsharī applies that reading to قد نرى تقلب وجهك.
BURHAN:v4p308/r1.anchor: وأما التكثير فهو معنى غريب وله من التوجيه نصيب وقد ذكره جماعة من المتأخرين

BURHAN:v4p308/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v4p308/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes قد in قد نرى to indicate frequent or abundant occurrence.
BURHAN:v4p308/r2.anchor: وجعلها غيره للتحقيق وقال ابن مالك

BURHAN:v4p308/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p308/r3.claim: Other grammarians analyze قد here as a particle of confirmation.

BURHAN:v4p308/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r4.speaker: ابن مالك
BURHAN:v4p308/r4.claim: Ibn Mālik says the present نرى is understood as past: قد رأينا.
BURHAN:v4p308/r4.anchor: وقال ابن مالك إن المضارع هنا بمعنى الماضي أي قد رأينا

BURHAN:v4p308/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v4p308/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v4p308/r5.claim: قد confirms the occurrence of its verb with either present or past; in قد نرى and قد نعلم it can be understood with past reference.
BURHAN:v4p308/r5.anchor: وأما التحقيق فترد لتحقيق وقوع المتعلق مع المضارع والماضي

BURHAN:v3p381/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p381/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p381/r5.claim: The qibla command omits naming the Kaʿba because those far away need only face its direction; addressing the Prophet honors him, while explicit generalization confirms the rule for everyone.
BURHAN:v3p381/r5.anchor: ولم يذكر الكعبة لأن البعيد يكفيه مراعاة الجهة فإن استقبال عينها حرج عليه

BURHAN:v3p22/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p22/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p22/r1.claim: The qibla command is repeated in three al-Baqara verses because its opponents comprised Jews, hypocrites, and Quraysh, each objecting for a different reason; Quraysh thought Muhammad might return to their religion.
BURHAN:v3p22/r1.anchor: ومنه تكرير الأمر بالتوجه إلى البيت الحرام في ثلاث آيات من سورة البقرة

SULAMI:v1p67#3/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r1.speaker: قيل
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r1.claim: God first taught the Prophet that he belonged to the Truth so he would observe its etiquette; his confident gaze toward heaven was answered in keeping with his wish.
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r1.anchor: قيل فيه أعلمه أولا أنه من الحق ليكون متأدبا بآداب الحق

SULAMI:v1p67#3/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r2.claim: After granting the Prophet's wish, God teaches that His own will is to transfer him to the Kaaba and establish it as qibla for him and his community; the Prophet's pleasure never departs from God's pleasure.
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r2.anchor: أخبره بعد أن أجابه إلى مراده

SULAMI:v1p67#3/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r3.speaker: بعض العراقيين
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r3.claim: An Iraqi Sufi says the body should face the Kaaba outwardly while the heart remains turned toward witnessing God: the Kaaba is the body's qibla and God the heart's.
SULAMI:v1p67#3/r3.anchor: قال بعض العراقيين : ترسم معهم برسم الظاهر في استقبال الكعبة ببدنك

ITQAN:v1p95/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that after the Hijra the Prophet faced Jerusalem for thirteen months at God's command, though he longed for Abraham's qibla; after the qibla changed, Jewish critics asked what had turned him from his former direction, and 2:142 answered them.
ITQAN:v1p95/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة أمره الله أن يستقبل بيت المقدس ففرحت اليهود

ITQAN:v2p487/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p487/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p487/r4.claim: With an imperfect verb, قد can reduce the likelihood of an act or the extent of its object; some instead read it as certainty in examples such as قد يعلم ما أنتم عليه.
ITQAN:v2p487/r4.anchor: المعنى الثالث التقليل مع المضارع قال في المغني وهو ضربان تقليل وقوع الفعل نحو قد يصدق الكذوب وتقليل متعلقه

ITQAN:v2p487/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p487/r5.speaker: الزمخشري
ITQAN:v2p487/r5.claim: Sibawayh and others recognize an intensive sense of قد; al-Zamakhshari applies it to 2:144 as repeated seeing, glossing it as perhaps or often seeing the Prophet's face turn heavenward.
ITQAN:v2p487/r5.anchor: الرابع التكثير ذكره سيبويه وغيره وخرج عليه الزمخشري قوله ﴿ قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء ﴾

ITQAN:v3p98/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.claim: The reverse figure names a part for the whole: 'face' means God's essence or the person facing, body-wide states are expressed by faces or hands, and prayer's standing, reciting, bowing, or prostrating can stand for the whole prayer.
ITQAN:v3p98/r4.anchor: عبر بالوجوه عن جميع الأجساد لأن التنعم والنصب حاصل بكلها

ITQAN:v3p178/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.claim: “He turned away fleeing” is not emphatic because turning can occur without fleeing; the command to turn one’s face toward the Sacred Mosque shows the difference.
ITQAN:v3p178/r8.anchor: وليس منه ﴿ ولى مدبرا ﴾ لأن التولية قد لا تكون إدبارا

ITQAN:v2p380/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p380/r3.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p380/r3.claim: In Kinana usage, shatrahu means toward it.
ITQAN:v2p380/r3.anchor: 2468 ﴿ شطره ﴾ تلقاءه 2469 ﴿ لا خلاق ﴾ لا نصيب

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r1.claim: An unnamed speaker asks Muhammad to request a change from the current direction to Abraham's qibla; Muhammad watches the sky for Gabriel, and the verse is revealed.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r1.anchor: فسل ربك أن يحولك عنها إلى قبلة إبراهيم" ثم ارتفع جبريل وجعل رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - يديم النظر إلى السماء

WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r2.speaker: البراء
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r2.claim: Al-Bara says Muslims prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after arriving in Medina, then the verse came when God knew the Prophet's wish; al-Wahidi notes its transmission by both Muslim and al-Bukhari.
WAHIDI-ASBAB:v1p43/r2.anchor: عن البراء قال: صلينا مع رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بعد قدومه المدينة ستة عشر شهرا نحو بيت المقدس،

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r1.claim: The preposition fi can mean 'at' in the cited examples about being weak among a people, once favored among them, and living among them for years.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r1.anchor: والسادس : بمعنى عند . ومنه قوله تعالى في هود

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r2.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r2.claim: Fi can stand in the sense of bi in the examples of God's coming amid clouds and someone being apart.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r2.anchor: والسابع : بمعنى ' الباء ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في البقرة

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r3.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r3.claim: In the qibla passage, fi means 'toward' the sky, describing the Prophet's repeated turning of his face in that direction.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r3.anchor: والثامن : بمعنى نحو . ومنه قوله تعالى ( في البقرة )

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r4.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r4.claim: Fi can mean 'about' or 'concerning,' as in disputing over names invented by people and their fathers.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r4.anchor: والتاسع : بمعنى ' عن ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الأعراف

IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r5.claim: Fi can mean 'for,' as in striving for God with due striving and those who strive for Him.
IBNJAWZI-NUZHA:v1p476/r5.anchor: والعاشر : بمعنى ' اللام ' . ومنه قوله تعالى في الحج

FARRA:v1p84/r2.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v1p84/r2.speaker: author
FARRA:v1p84/r2.claim: Shatrahu means toward it, in its direction or facing it.
FARRA:v1p84/r2.anchor: يريد: نحوه وتلقاءه، ومثله في الكلام: ول وجهك شطره، وتلقاءه، وتجاهه.

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p65/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p65/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p65/r1.claim: Shatr means toward it and intending it.

SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r1.claim: Some grammarians say قد shifts a present verb into past meaning, applying it here and citing poetry with قد نرى أمس.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r1.anchor: " قد " هذه قال فيها بعضهم: إنها تصرف المضارع إلى معنى المضي

SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r2.speaker: الزمخشري
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r2.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī glosses قد نرى as perhaps we see and takes it to suggest abundant seeing, citing قد أترك القرن.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r2.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: " قد نرى ": ربما نرى، ومعناه كثرة الرؤية كقول الشاعر

SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r3.claim: The shaykh says al-Zamakhsharī contradicts himself: ربما suggests rarity on the relevant account, not abundance; قد itself does not encode abundance, which comes from repeated turning being seen.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144/r3.anchor: ثم هذا الذي ادعاه من كثرة الرؤية لا يدل عليه اللفظ لأنه لم توضع للكثرة

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r1.claim: في may attach to verbal noun تقلب with ordinary locative sense; it may mean إلى, but al-Samīn sees no need because this noun is attested with في, as in 3:196.

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r2.claim: A second view attaches في to نرى and takes في to mean من; heaven is mentioned honorifically, not to claim God occupies a direction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r2.anchor: والثاني من القولين: أنه " نرى " وحينئذ تكون " في " بمعنى " من "

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r3.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Baqāʾ makes في السماء an accusative حال from وجهك, attached to an omitted element.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r3.anchor: والثالث: أنه في محل نصب على الحال من " وجهك " ذكره أبو البقاء

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r4.claim: تقلب is annexed to its subject; it cannot be annexed to its object, for that verbal noun would be التقليب.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r4.anchor: والمصدر هنا مضاف إلى فاعله، ولا يجوز أن يكون مضافا إلى منصوبه

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r5.claim: There is no need to supply an omitted مضاف meaning sight of your face, a rare usage; face is the noblest feature and one turned by a petitioner, though another view takes it as metonym for sight.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#2/r5.anchor: ولا حاجة إلى حذف مضاف من قوله " وجهك " وهو بصر وجهك

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r1.claim: The فاء marks consequence, and the clause answers an omitted oath, فوالله لنولينك.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r1.anchor: الفاء هنا للتسبب وهو واضح، وهذا جواب قسم محذوف، أي: فوالله لنولينك

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r2.claim: نولي governs two objects, the suffix ك and قبلة; ترضاها is a clause in the accusative qualifying قبلة.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r2.anchor: الجملة في محل نصب صفة لقبلة

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r3.claim: The shaykh says the promise implies an omitted حال: God sees the Prophet turning his face toward heaven while seeking a different qibla from the one he faces.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r3.anchor: قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء طالبا قبلة غير التي أنت مستقبلها

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r4.claim: ولي governs وجهك and شطر as two objects; it can also take its second object with إلى.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r4.anchor: " ولى " يتعدى لاثنين أحدهما " وجهك " والثاني " شطر "

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r5.speaker: النحاس
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r5.claim: Al-Naḥḥās allows شطر as locative adverb, leaving ولي with one object; al-Zamakhsharī mentions only that analysis, but al-Samīn finds the two-object analysis clearer.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r5.anchor: ويجوز أن ينتصب " شطر " على الظرف المكاني فيتعدى الفعل لواحد وهو قول النحاس

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r6.claim: شطر can mean half or part, or direction and toward; lines 762–767 attest the directional sense, including Ibn Aḥmar's شطر نجد.

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r7.speaker: ابن أحمر
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r7.claim: Ibn Aḥmar's شطر نجد means toward Najd and witnesses the directional sense of شطر.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r7.anchor: وقال ابن أحمر: 765 تعدو بنا شطر نجد وهي عاقدة

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r8.claim: شطر also means far away: الشاطر is a youth distant from neighbors and home, شطير is distant, and شطر إليه can mean turning toward; al-Rāghib also uses الشاطر for distancing from truth, plural شطار.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#3/r8.anchor: ويقال: شطر: بعد ومنه: الشاطر وهو الشاب البعيد من الجيران الغائب عن منزله

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r1.claim: The clearest analysis takes ḥaythumā as conditional; the added mā is required for that force, contrary to al-Farrāʾ.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r1.anchor: في " حيثما " هنا وجهان، أظهرهما: أنها شرطية، وشرط كونها كذلك زيادة

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r2.claim: On the conditional analysis, kuntum is jussive, wallū answers the condition, and ḥaythumā is an accusative adverb governed by kuntum; Q 17:110 illustrates the construction.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r2.anchor: ب " كنتم " ، في محل جزم بها، و " فولوا " جوابها وتكون هي منصوبة على الظرف بكنتم،

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r3.speaker: الشيخ
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r3.claim: Although ḥayth is a locative noun normally annexed to a clause in the genitive, its connection with mā removes annexation and gives it conditional force and verbal governance.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r3.anchor: قال الشيخ: " وحيث هي ظرف مكان مضافة إلى الجملة فهي مقتضية للخفض بعدها،

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r4.speaker: أبو البقاء
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r4.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ treats ḥayth as a nonconditional adverb governed by wallū; the author rejects this because added mā necessarily makes it conditional.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r4.anchor: والثاني: أنها ظرف غير مضمن معنى الشرط، والناصب له قوله: " فولوا " قاله أبو البقاء،

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r5.claim: Wallū derives from waliyū: the heavy ḍamma on yā is dropped, then yā is deleted at the meeting of two sukūns and the preceding vowel is rounded to match the pronoun.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r5.anchor: وأصل ولوا: وليوا، فاستثقلت الضمة على الياء فحذفت فالتقى ساكنان

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r6.claim: Shatrahu has two analyses: it is either the direct object or an adverb of direction, as discussed earlier.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#4/r6.anchor: وقوله: " شطره " فيه القولان، وهما: إما المفعول به وإما الظرفية

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r1.speaker: الجمهور
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r1.claim: For the majority, the clause anna-hu al-ḥaqq supplies both objects of yaʿlamūn.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r1.anchor: قوله: { أنه الحق } يحتمل أن تكون " أن " واسمها وخبرها سادة مسد المفعولين ل " يعلمون " عند الجمهور،

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r2.speaker: الأخفش
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r2.claim: Al-Akhfash allows the clause to supply one object of a verb taking two, with the second object omitted.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r2.anchor: ومسد أحدهما عند الأخفش والثاني محذوف على أنها تتعدى لاثنين

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r3.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r3.claim: A further analysis has the clause supply one object because yaʿlamūn means to recognize or know.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r3.anchor: وأن تكون سادة مسد مفعول واحد على أنها بمعنى العرفان

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r4.claim: One proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the turning toward the qibla implied by wallū.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r4.anchor: أحدها: يعود على التولي المدلول عليه بقوله: " فولوا ".

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r5.claim: A second proposed antecedent of the pronoun in annahu is the direction, shatrahu.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r5.anchor: والثاني: على الشطر. والثالث: على النبي

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r6.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r6.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r6.claim: A third view refers the pronoun to the Prophet; this shifts from direct address in fa-lanuwalliyannaka to speaking of him in the third person.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r6.anchor: والثالث: على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم، ويكون على هذا التفاتا من خطابه

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r7.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r7.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r7.claim: Min rabbihim modifies an omitted circumstantial expression describing al-ḥaqq: the truth is from their Lord.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r7.anchor: متعلق بمحذوف على أنه حال من الحق أي: الحق كائنا من ربهم.

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r8.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r8.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r8.claim: The third-person reading may address the People of the Book or refer back to the believers, with a shift from the preceding address.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r8.anchor: وقرىء: " عما يعملون " بالغيبة ردا على الذين أوتوا الكتاب أو ردا على المؤمنين

SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r9.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r9.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r9.claim: The direct-address reading most naturally addresses the believers; it may instead turn to the People of the Book to spur them on.
SAMIN-DURR:2:144#5/r9.anchor: وبالخطاب على رده للمؤمنين وهو الظاهر، أو للذين على الالتفات تحريكا لهم وتنشيطا.

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r1.claim: The phrase means looking toward the sky; it is also explained as the movement of the eyes, since the Prophet awaited revelation after being told to stop praying toward Jerusalem.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r1.anchor: المعنى: في النظر إلى السماء، وقيل: تقلب عينك، والمعنى واحد

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r2.claim: Taqallub is the regular verbal noun; taqlāban is possible in speech but not in Qurʾānic text because it would alter the written muṣḥaf.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r2.anchor: وتقلب مصدر تقلب تقلبا، ويجوز في الكلام تقلابا، ولا يجوز في القرآن لأنه تغيير للمصحف.

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r3.claim: While in Medina, the Prophet was ordered to change prayer direction from Jerusalem to the Sacred House in Mecca.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r3.anchor: قد كان النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - بالمدينة حين أمر بأن ينتقل عن الصلاة إلى بيت المقدس

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r4.speaker: قوم
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r4.claim: One interpretation takes tardāhā as you love it, without implying the Prophet was displeased with the former qibla, since prophets accept what God commands.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r4.anchor: قال قوم معناه تحبها، لا أن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لم يكن راضيا بتلك القبلة

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r5.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r5.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r5.claim: The Prophet loved the new qibla, according to reports, because it had been the qibla of earlier prophets.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r5.anchor: وإنما أحبها النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - لأنها كانت - فيما يروى - قبلة الأنبياء

ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r6.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r6.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r6.claim: A second reported reason for loving it is that this qibla would more readily draw his people to faith.
ZAJJAJ:v1p221/r6.anchor: وقيل لأنها كانت عنده ادعى لقومه إلى الإيمان.

ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r1.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r1.claim: Shatra means toward or in the direction of; the command was to face Mecca and the Sacred House, including for people wherever they were, and shatra is an accusative of place or direction.
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r1.anchor: ومعنى الشطر: النحو. وشطر منصوب على الظرف.

ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r2.claim: The anonymous verse's shatrah means toward it, confirming the directional sense of shatr.
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r2.anchor: إن العسير بها داء يخامرها. . . فشطرها نظر العينين محسور

ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r3.claim: Shāṭir describes someone who has turned from the straight path toward another direction.
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r3.anchor: فلذلك قيل شاطر لعدوله عن الاستواء، يقال قد شطر الرجل

ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r4.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r4.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r4.claim: The phrase qawm mushāṭirūnā means their houses adjoin ours; the usage compares people whose directions lie toward one another.
ZAJJAJ:v1p222/r4.anchor: هؤلاء قوم مشاطرونا أي دورهم تتصل بدورنا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r1.claim: The Quraysh listeners returned on later nights despite agreeing not to; they listened until dawn, met by chance, reproached one another, and renewed their resolve.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r1.anchor: لكنهم عادوا فتسللوا في الليلة وباتوا يستمعون إلى القرآن.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r2.speaker: السيرة
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r2.claim: The Quraysh leaders sent ʿUtba ibn Rabīʿa to negotiate; after hearing verses from Fuṣṣilat, he returned visibly captivated, prompting their remark that he was changed.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r2.anchor: وفي (السيرة) أيضاً أن الملأ من قريش بعثوا أحد صناديدهم "عتبة بن ربيعة"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r3.claim: Though Quraysh called the Qur’an poetry, sorcery, or soothsaying, they knew it was none of these and recognized its extraordinary hold over minds and hearts.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r3.anchor: وقد تحير المشركون من قريش فيما بينهم، بم يصفون هذا القرآن: قالوا هو شعر، وقالوا هو سحر، وقالوا هم كهانة.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r4.claim: Before the pilgrimage season, Quraysh leaders planned to block routes to Mecca and agreed on a single account of the Qur’an so visiting tribes would not hear conflicting descriptions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p47/r4.anchor: تواطأ طواغيت قريش على أن يأخذوا سبل الناس إلى مكة ويصدوهم عن سماع القرآن.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r2.claim: Her comparison of Qur'anic clauses with unaccompanied ma shows a recurring pattern: the predicate of ma not followed by kana takes ba in the cited decisive verses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p184/r2.anchor: ونبدأ بخبر "ما" غير المتلوة بكان، فنلحظ في النظم القرآني أن الباء تلزمه في الآيات المحكَمات

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r1.claim: Samarrai observes that scripture is actively attributed to God in contexts of praise, while passive 'were given' appears in rebuke; 2:144 condemns those who know the truth yet evade it.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r15#2/r1.anchor: إذا كان المقام مقامَ مدح وثناء، أظهر ذاته ونسب إيتاء الكتاب إلى نفسه

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.claim: The extended, repetitive qibla passage runs from the fools' objection and the trial of the change through the command to face Mecca and the Book-holders' refusal; its length suits the explicit pronoun.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r5#3/r9.anchor: فأنت ترى أنه أطال القول ههنا، فكان المناسب أن يطيل بذكر الضيمر أيضاً وهو المناسب لإطالة السياق

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p965/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p965/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p965/r4.claim: The spelling of إبراهيم without yā in al-Baqarah is an issue of Qur’anic orthography that the program had discussed in detail in earlier episodes.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p965/r4.anchor: هذا يتعلق برسم القرآن وسبق أن أجيب على هذا الموضوع بتفصيل في حلقات سابقة

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r1.claim: With a past-tense verb, قد signals confirmation; with a present-tense verb, it can have several meanings rather than expressing only paucity.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r1.anchor: إذا دخلت على الماضي تفيد التحقيق وإذا دخلت على المضارع لها أكثر من معنى

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r2.claim: Here قد can indicate frequency: God has often seen the Prophet looking toward the sky for the direction of prayer.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p966/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى (قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء) أي كثيراً ما تنظر إلى السماء

NASHR:v2p149/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p149/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p149/r1.claim: The two-word sequence haythu ma is written separately wherever it occurs.
NASHR:v2p149/r1.anchor: (وحيث ما) كتب مفصولا حيث وقع نحو

QIRAAT-ER:2:144:43#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:2:144:43#1/r1.speaker: Imp
QIRAAT-ER:2:144:43#1/r1.claim: The second person plural reading shifts the warning from the People of the Book to the Muslim community, making them the addressees of divine surveillance.
QIRAAT-ER:2:144:43#1/r1.anchor: 2nd person plural variant: ""what YOU do"" — shifts the warning from 3rd person

IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r1.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r1.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r1.claim: Ibn Hisham defines shatrahu as toward it and its aim; Amr ibn Ahmar's camel poem supplies an example of the directional sense.
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r1.anchor: قال ابن هشام: شطره: نحوه وقصده. قال عمرو بن أحمر الباهلي

IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r2.speaker: قيس بن خويلد الهذلي
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r2.claim: Qays uses shatr in a verse about a camel looking toward something; the line is cited as evidence for the word's directional sense.
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r2.anchor: قال قيس بن خويلد الهذلي يصف ناقته: إن النعوس بها داء مخامرها ... فشطرها نظر العينين محسور

IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r3.speaker: ابن هشام
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r3.claim: Ibn Hisham says al-na'us is the camel afflicted by illness, whose owner looked at it with an exhausted gaze, as in the word hasir.
IBNHISHAM:v1p550#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن هشام: والنعوس: ناقته، وكان بها داء فنظر إليها نظر حسير، من قوله: وهو حسير

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r4.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r4.claim: A report from Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib says Muslims prayed toward Jerusalem in Mecca and for sixteen months after arriving in Medina.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة عن ابن المسيب صلوا بمكة وبعدما قدموا المدينة ستة عشر شهرا نحو بيت المقدس

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r5.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r5.speaker: الزهري
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r5.claim: Al-Zuhrī gives the duration of praying toward Jerusalem as eighteen months.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56/r5.anchor: قال معمر وقال الزهري ثمانية عشر شهرا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56#2/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56#2/r1.claim: Al-Barāʾ ibn ʿĀzib reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, then, after the change to the Kaaba was announced, Ansar turned toward it during prayer before bowing.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p56#2/r1.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال لما قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو قال سبعة عشر شهرا

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r1.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet kept turning his face toward heaven, wishing God would redirect him toward the Kaaba, until God did so.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء ﴾ قال كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقلب وجهه

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAmr recited “a qibla that pleases you” while seated opposite the water spout in the Sacred Mosque, pointing out the Kaaba’s direction.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r2.anchor: عن يحيى بن قمطة قال رأيت عبد الله بن عمرو جالسا في المسجد الحرام بإزاء الميزاب فتلا هذه الآية

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r3.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r3.claim: Qatāda glosses “shatr al-Masjid al-Ḥarām” as toward the Sacred Mosque.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r3.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام ﴾ قال نحو المسجد الحرام

ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r4.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v1p62/r4.anchor: ﴿ وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره ﴾ أي تلقاءه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r1.claim: The Prophet repeatedly turned his gaze toward the sky, eagerly expecting revelation about the direction of prayer.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r1.anchor: أي كثيرا ما نرى تردد وجهك وتصرف نظرك في جهة السماء متشوفا للوحي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r2.claim: He hoped God would turn him toward the Kaaba because Jews taunted him for following their qibla, and because it was Abraham's and the older qibla, more likely to draw Arabs to faith.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r2.anchor: يتوقع من ربه أن يحوله إلى الكعبة لما أن اليهود كانوا يقولون

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r3.claim: Al-Alusi thinks the Prophet awaited the change without explicitly asking; the verse's failure to mention a request suggests this and reflects his perfect propriety.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r3.anchor: والظاهر أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم لم يسأل ذلك من ربه بل كان ينتظر فقط إذ لو وقع السؤال لكان الظاهر ذكره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r4.speaker: قتادة والسدي وغيرهما
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r4.claim: Qatada, al-Suddi, and others say the Prophet repeatedly prayed to God to change the qibla to the Kaaba.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي وغيرهما : كان رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم يقلب وجهه في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r5.claim: On that account, the Prophet's request may have followed permission, since prophets do not ask without authorization lest an ungranted request become a trial for their people.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r5.anchor: لعل ذلك بعد حصول الإذن له بالدعاء لما أن الأنبياء لا يسألون الله تعالى شيئا من غير أن يؤذن لهم فيه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r6.claim: An unnamed report says the Prophet asked Gabriel for permission to pray, and Gabriel told him God had permitted it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r6.anchor: أخبره بأن الله تعالى قد أذن له بالدعاء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r7.claim: Al-Alusi rejects the need for explicit permission: the Prophet could ask for a religious benefit he understood, given his exceptional nearness to God; any admonition addressed hidden wisdom, not a lapse in his manners.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r7.anchor: والذي أراه أنه لا مانع من دعائه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم وسؤاله التحويل لمصلحة ألهمها ومنفعة دينية فهمها ولا يتوقف ذلك على الاستئذان

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r8.claim: Despite allowing that he could have asked, Al-Alusi thinks he did not explicitly pray in this incident: sound reports show only his desire for the change.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8/r8.anchor: حيث لم يكن فيها سوى حب التحويل

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r1.speaker: البراء
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r1.claim: Al-Bara reports that the Muslims prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after reaching Medina, then God revealed the verse, knowing the Prophet's desire.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r1.anchor: قال : صلينا مع رسول الله صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم بعد قدومه المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r2.claim: Some take “قد” here to indicate rarity, arguing that infrequent glances better show the Prophet's perfect manners.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من جعل ( قد ) هنا للتقليل زعما منه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r3.claim: Al-Alusi objects that one upward glance is not called repeated turning; the word therefore conveys frequent turning in this context.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r3.anchor: مرة واحدة لا يقال له : قلب بصره إلى السماء وإنما يقال : قلب إذا داوم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r4.speaker: سيبويه
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r4.claim: The frequency may be a lexical force of “قد” or an inference from the actual context; the latter account is attributed to Sibawayh.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r5.speaker: بعض النحاة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r5.claim: Some grammarians say “قد” shifts a present verb into the past, citing 24:64 and 15:97 as parallels.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r5.anchor: وذكر بعض النحاة أن ( قد ) تقلب المضارع ماضيا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r6.claim: “We will turn you toward a qibla” means either granting him the ability to face it or making him face its direction.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r6.anchor: من قولك : وليته كذا إذا جعلته واليا له

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r7.claim: The fāʾ marks the result of what precedes and introduces an implicit oath, whose lām intensifies the certainty of the promise.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r7.anchor: والفاء لسببية ما قبلها لما بعدها وهي في الحقيقة داخلة على قسم محذوف تدل عليه اللام

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r8.claim: The promise comes before the command so the Prophet rejoices first at the answer and again when it is fulfilled.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r8.anchor: وجاء قبل الأمر لفرح انفس بالإجابة ثم بإنجاز الوعد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r9.claim: In this construction, the verb takes two objects: the addressed person is first and the qibla is second.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r9.anchor: ونولي يتعدى لإثنين الكاف الأول وقبلة الثاني

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r10.claim: “You are pleased with” means that he loves and inclines toward it for sound purposes consonant with God's will and wisdom.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r10.anchor: أي تحبها وتميل إليها للأغراض الصحيحة التي أضمرتها ووافقت مشيئة الله تعالى وحكمته

ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r11.claim: “You are pleased with” is an accusative adjective of “qibla”; the noun is indefinite because no particular qibla has yet been mentioned, and the wording does not specify one already requested.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p8#2/r11.anchor: نصب صفة لقبلة ونكرها لأنه لم يجر قبلها ما يقتضي أن تكون معهودة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r1.claim: The command branches from the promise; the face is specified because it is the axis and measure of orientation, though it may stand metonymically for the whole body as the noblest and distinguishing limb.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r1.anchor: الفاء لتفريع الأمر على الوعد وتخصيص التولية بالوجه لما أنه مدار التوجه ومعياره

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas explains “shatr” as toward the Sacred Mosque.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r2.anchor: أي نحوه كما روى عن ابن عباس

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r3.speaker: علي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r3.claim: Ali explains “shatr” as in its direction or facing it.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r3.anchor: أو قبله كما روى عن علي كرم الله تعالى وجهه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r4.speaker: قتادة
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r4.claim: Qatada explains “shatr” as toward it or in its direction.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r4.anchor: أو تلقاءه كما روى عن قتادة ظرف مكان مبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r5.claim: Here the verb has one object, “your face,” and “shatr” is an ambiguous locative adverb equivalent to “toward,” with an omitted “to”; this yields direct alignment with the qibla.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r5.anchor: ظرف مكان مبهم كمفسره منصوب على الظرفية أغنى غناء إلى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r6.claim: Al-Alusi rejects making “shatr” a second object: that would mean making oneself face the mosque's direction, rather than turning the face toward the qibla as fulfillment of the promise requires.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r6.anchor: لأن ترتبه بالفاء وكونه إنجازا للوعد بأن الله تعالى يجعل مستقبل القبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r7.claim: The alternative takes “shatr” originally as a separated portion, then a side or part, making it a second object; Al-Alusi says this remains ill-suited to the promised turning, and “half” is untenable.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r7.anchor: وقيل : الشطر في الأصل لما أنفصل عن الشيء ثم أستعمل لجانبه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r8.claim: “Al-Haram” means either a place where fighting is forbidden or a place protected from aggressors.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r8.anchor: والحرام المحرم أي محرم فيه القتال أو ممنوع من الظلمة أن يتعرضوا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r9.claim: Naming the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaaba shows that a distant worshipper need only align with the qibla's direction, not hit the Kaaba's exact point.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r9.anchor: مع أنها القبلة التي دلت عليها الأحاديث الصحاح إشارة إلى أنه يكفي للبعيد محاذاة جهة القبلة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد وأكثر الخراسانيين من الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa, Ahmad, most Khurasani Shafi'is, and al-Ghazali in the Ihya hold that a distant worshipper faces the direction of the Kaaba.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r10.anchor: مذهب أبي حنيفة رضي الله تعالى عنه وأحمد وقول أكثر الخراسانيين من الشافعية

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة وأحمد وأكثر الخراسانيين من الشافعية
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r11.claim: Even those who require facing the Kaaba's direction say the worshipper must intend the Kaaba itself as the qibla.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r11.anchor: إلا إنهم قالوا : يجب أن يكون قصد المتوجه إلى الجهة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r12.speaker: العراقيون والقفال
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r12.claim: The Iraqi Shafi'is and al-Qaffal require facing the Kaaba's exact point.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9/r12.anchor: وقال العراقيون والقفال منهم : يجب إصابة العين

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r1.speaker: مالك
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r1.claim: Malik says the Kaaba is the qibla for people in the mosque, the mosque for Makkans, the Haram for Makkah, and Makkah's sanctuary for the world.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r1.anchor: مسجد قبلة مكة وهي قبلة الحرم وهو قبلة الدنيا

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r2.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn Abbas supports the tiered qibla view; the disagreement concerns those not physically present, since present worshippers must face the Kaaba exactly by consensus.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r2.anchor: وفي حديث ابن عباس رضي الله تعالى عنهما مرفوعا ما يدل عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r3.claim: The verse omits an explicit reference to prayer because the requested direction was the only matter at issue; another view says the verse came while the Prophet was praying, making that context sufficient.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r3.anchor: ولم يقيد سبحانه وتعالى التولية في الصلاة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r4.speaker: القاضي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r4.claim: Al-Qadi and others say the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months, then in Rajab, two months before Badr, turned during Zuhr at Banu Salima; men and women exchanged rows and the mosque became the Mosque of the Two Qiblas.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r4.anchor: ذكره القاضي تبعا لغيره أنه صلى الله تعالى عليه وسلم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r5.speaker: السيوطي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r5.claim: Al-Suyuti calls that account a distortion: the Banu Salima story did not have the Prophet leading or turning during prayer.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r6.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r6.claim: Al-Nasa'i reports from Abu Sa'id ibn al-Mu'alla that he and a companion heard the verse while the Prophet sat on the minbar; they prayed two rak'ahs before he descended, then he led the people in Zuhr.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r6.anchor: أخرج النسائي عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال : كنا نغدو إلى المسجد

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r7.speaker: أنس
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r7.claim: Abu Dawud reports from Anas that while the Prophet and companions prayed toward Jerusalem, a caller at Banu Salima announced the change during Fajr; they turned toward the Kaaba while still bowing.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r7.anchor: وروى أبو داؤد عن أنس رضي الله تعالى عنه أن النبي

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r8.claim: Al-Alusi rejects relying on the account that makes the Prophet turn during prayer at Banu Salima because it conflicts with sound, established reports.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r8.anchor: فما ذكر مخالف للروايات الصحيحة الثابتة عند أهل هذا الشأن فلا يعول عليه

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r9.speaker: أبي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r9.claim: Ubayy's reading, “تلقاء المسجد الحرام,” supports interpreting “shatr” as toward.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r9.anchor: وقرأ أبي ( تلقاء المسجد الحرام ) وهي تؤيد القول الأول في ( شطر )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r10.claim: The clause attaches to the first command, completing the promise; “wherever” with “ma” is conditional, and “kana” is complete, meaning wherever you are found.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r10.anchor: عطف على ( فول وجهك ) ومن تتمة إنجاز الوعد والفاء جواب الشرط

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r11.speaker: الفراء
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r11.claim: Al-Farra does not require “ma” for “haythu” to function conditionally.

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r12.claim: “Wallu” derives from “wallayu”: the heavy vowel on yāʾ is dropped, then the first of two meeting consonants is deleted, producing the form faʿū.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r12.anchor: وأصل ( ولوا ) وليوا فأستثقلت الضمة على الياء فحذفت

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r13.claim: This explicitly generalizes the qibla ruling: an address to the Prophet applies to everyone unless evidence restricts it to him.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r13.anchor: وهذا تصريح بعموم الحكم المستفاد من السابق

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r14.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r14.claim: One explanation for naming every place is to prevent people from thinking this qibla applied only to the people of Medina.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r14.anchor: أن هذه القبلة مختصة بأهل المدينة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r15.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r15.claim: Another explanation is that the change from the Kaaba to Jerusalem sought Jewish goodwill, so the verse stresses facing the Kaaba even where Jews are present.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r15.anchor: لا يتوجه إليها في حضورهم أشار إلى تعميم التولية جميع الأمكنة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r16.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r16.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r16.claim: A further explanation is to clarify that the Kaaba's direction remains obligatory even when Jerusalem is present, lest its presence be thought to prevent that orientation.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r16.anchor: فرض مع حضور بيت المقدس ولأهله أيضا لئلا يظن

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r17.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r17.speaker: عبدالله
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r17.claim: A reading attributed to ʿAbd Allah says, “turn your faces toward it.”

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r18.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r18.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r18.claim: “Those given the Book” means the Jews and Christians.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r18.anchor: وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ( أي من اليهود والنصارى

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r19.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r19.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r19.claim: The People of the Book know the change is true because Muhammad would not command falsehood, each law has its own qibla, and their books foretold that he would pray toward both qiblas.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r19.anchor: لا يأمر بالباطل إذ هو النبي المبشر به في كتبهم

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r20.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r20.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r20.claim: The Prophet and Abraham share the Kaaba as qibla because they share a religious law, as indicated by the call to follow Abraham's upright religion.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r20.anchor: على ما ينبيء عنه قوله تعالى : ( بل ملة إبراهيم حنيفا )

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r21.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r21.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r21.claim: The clause is linked to “We see” because the first states the change and this one establishes its truth; alternatively, it is parenthetical reinforcement of the qibla command.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r21.anchor: والجملة عطف على ( قد نرى ) بجامع أن السابقة

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r22.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r22.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r22.claim: The closing clause is parenthetical, promising and warning the two groups from the People of the Book, those who conceal and those who do not.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r22.anchor: اعتراض بين الكلامين جيء به للوعد والوعيد للفريقين من أهل الكتاب الداخلين تحت العموم السابق المشار إليهما فيما سيجيء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r23.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r23.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r23.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read “تعملون” in the second person; this promises the believers, while the third-person reading warns the People of the Book.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r23.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي ( تعملون ) بالتاء

ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r24.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r24.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r24.claim: Another view takes the pronoun in either reading to include all people, making the clause a promise and threat for believers and disbelievers.
ALUSI-FULL:v2p9#2/r24.anchor: وقيل : الضمير على القراءتين لجميع الناس

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r1.claim: Although this verse comes later in the recitation, it precedes the surrounding account in meaning and begins the story; the change of qibla was the first abrogation in Islamic law.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r1.anchor: هذه الآية وإن كانت متأخرة في التلاوة فهي متقدمة في المعنى فإنها رأس القصة، وأمر القبلة أول ما نسخ من أمور الشرع

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r2.claim: At Mecca the Prophet and Companions prayed toward the Kaaba; after migration God directed them toward Jerusalem's rock to draw the Jews toward affirming him, since they found his description in the Torah.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r2.anchor: كانوا يصلون بمكة إلى الكعبة، فلما هاجر إلى المدينة أمره الله أن يصلي نحو صخرة بيت المقدس ليكون أقرب إلى تصديق اليهود إياه

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r3.claim: The Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months after migration and wished to face the Kaaba, the qibla of his father Abraham.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r3.anchor: فصلى بعد الهجرة ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا إلى بيت المقدس وكان يحب أن يوجه إلى الكعبة لأنها كانت قبلة أبيه إبراهيم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r4.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet wanted the Kaaba because the Jews taunted that Muhammad opposed their religion yet followed their qibla; he asked Gabriel to request the change.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r4.anchor: وقال مجاهد: كان يحب ذلك لأجل اليهود لأنهم كانوا يقولون يخالفنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم في ديننا ويتبع قبلتنا

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r5.speaker: جبريل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r5.claim: Gabriel replied that he was only a servant like the Prophet and advised him to ask God himself, since he was honored with God.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r5.anchor: فقال جبريل: إنما أنا عبد مثلك وأنت كريم على ربك، فسل أنت ربك فإنك عند الله عز وجل بمكان

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r6.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r6.claim: The Prophet repeatedly looked toward the sky, hoping Gabriel would bring the desired direction, and God revealed the verse.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r6.anchor: وجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يديم النظر إلى السماء رجاء أن ينزل جبريل بما يحب من أمر القبلة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r7.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r7.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r7.claim: “We will surely turn you” means “We will change you to a qibla”; one he is pleased with means one he loves and desires.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r7.anchor: فلنحولنك إلى قبلة {ترضاها} أي تحبها وتهواها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r8.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r8.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r8.claim: Fawalli means “turn,” and shatr means “toward”; the intended sanctuary is the Kaaba, and ḥarām means sacred or forbidden.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r8.anchor: {فول} أي حول {وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} أي نحوه وأراد به الكعبة والحرام المحرم

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r9.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r9.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r9.claim: Muslims must face the Kaaba in prayer wherever they are, on land or sea and in any direction.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r9.anchor: {وحيثما كنتم} من بر أو بحر أو شرق أو غرب {فولوا وجوهكم شطره} عند الصلاة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r10.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Prophet entered the House, he supplicated in all its corners before beginning prayer; the excerpt breaks off before completing the report.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p161#2/r10.anchor: عن عطاء قال سمعت ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما: قال لما دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم البيت دعا في نواحيه كلها

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r1.speaker: اليهود
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r1.claim: After the qibla changed, the Jews accused Muhammad of inventing it and said that had he remained on their qibla they might have hoped he was the awaited prophet.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r1.anchor: قالت اليهود: يا محمد ما هو إلا شيء تبتدعه من تلقاء نفسك فتارة تصلي إلى بيت المقدس وتارة إلى الكعبة

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r2.claim: “It is the truth” means that the command to face the Kaaba is from their Lord.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r3.speaker: أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r3.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with second-person tāʾ; Ibn Abbas says it addresses believers seeking God's approval and promises awareness of their reward.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r3.anchor: قرأ أبو جعفر وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالتاء قال ابن عباس يريد أنكم يا معشر المؤمنين تطلبون مرضاتي

BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r4.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r4.claim: The other readers use third-person yāʾ, meaning God is aware of what the Jews do and will requite them in this world and the next.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v1p163/r4.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بالياء يعني ما أنا بغافل عما يفعل اليهود فأجازيهم في الدنيا والآخرة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r1.claim: The Prophet looked heavenward in expectation of revelation changing the qibla; he anticipated the Kaaba as Abraham’s qibla, the older qibla, more inviting to Arabs, and a departure from Jewish practice, yet waited without asking, showing perfect courtesy.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r1.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقع في روعه ويتوقع من ربه أن يحوله إلى الكعبة، لأنها قبلة أبيه إبراهيم، وأقدم القبلتين وأدعى للعرب إلى الإيمان، ولمخالفة اليهود، وذلك يدل على كمال أدبه حيث انتظر ولم يسأل

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r2.claim: The phrase may mean enabling the Prophet to face the qibla, from making someone a governor, or making him face its direction.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r2.anchor: فلنمكننك من استقبالها من قولك: وليته كذا، إذا صيرته واليا له، أو فلنجعلنك تلي جهتها

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r3.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r3.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r3.claim: The desired qibla is one the Prophet loves and longs for, for religious purposes that accord with God’s will and wisdom.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r3.anchor: تحبها وتتشوق إليها، لمقاصد دينية وافقت مشيئة الله وحكمته

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r4.claim: Shatr means toward; its original sense was what separates from a thing, then it came to mean its side even without separation.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r4.anchor: وقيل: الشطر في الأصل لما انفصل عن الشيء إذا انفصل، ودار شطور: أي منفصلة عن الدور، ثم استعمل لجانبه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r5.claim: The sanctuary is called forbidden because fighting there is forbidden, or because wrongdoers are barred from violating it.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r5.anchor: والحرام المحرم أي محرم فيه القتال، أو ممنوع من الظلمة أن يتعرضوه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r6.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r6.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r6.claim: The mosque is named instead of the Kaaba because the Prophet was in Medina: for the distant, facing its direction suffices, since requiring its exact point would be hardship; the nearby must face it exactly.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r6.anchor: وإنما ذكر المسجد دون الكعبة لأنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان في المدينة، والبعيد يكفيه مراعاة الجهة، فإن استقبال عينها حرج عليه بخلاف القريب
