BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r7.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r7.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after arriving in Medina, then the qibla changed in Rajab, two months before Badr.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r7.anchor: روي: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قدم المدينة، فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا، ثم وجه إلى الكعبة في رجب بعد الزوال قبل قتال بدر بشهرين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r8.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r8.speaker: روي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r8.claim: At Banu Salama mosque, during a two-rakʿa noon prayer, the Prophet turned toward the mihrab and men and women exchanged rows; the mosque became known as the Mosque of Two Qiblas.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r8.anchor: وقد صلى بأصحابه في مسجد بني سلمة ركعتين من الظهر، فتحول في الصلاة واستقبل الميزاب، وتبادل الرجال والنساء صفوفهم، فسمي المسجد مسجد القبلتين

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r9.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r9.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r9.claim: The Prophet is addressed first to honor him and fulfill his wish; the command then becomes general to state the ruling’s reach, reinforce the qibla command, and urge the community to follow.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r9.anchor: خص الرسول بالخطاب تعظيما له وإيجابا لرغبته، ثم عمم تصريحا بعموم الحكم وتأكيدا لأمر القبلة وتحضيضا للأمة على المتابعة

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r10.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r10.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r10.claim: People of the Book know this is true because God customarily assigns each law a qibla, and their books say the Prophet would pray toward both qiblas; the pronoun refers to the change or the facing.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r10.anchor: جملة لعلمهم بأن عادته تعالى تخصيص كل شريعة بقبلة، وتفصيلا لتضمن كتبهم أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي إلى القبلتين، والضمير للتحويل أو التوجه

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r11.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r11.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r11.claim: God’s not being heedless is both a promise and a threat directed to the two parties.

BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r12.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r12.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r12.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with yāʾ, “they do,” rather than the other form.
BAYDAWI-FULL:2:144/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي بالياء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r4.claim: The prior discussion leads rhetorically to a change of qibla: after general mercy toward people, God shows mercy specifically to His Messenger by turning him toward the Kaaba.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r4.anchor: ولما أشعر الكلام السابق أهل البلاغة بإحداث أمر في القبلة فتوقعوا الخبر عن ذلك

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r5.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r5.claim: Al-Ḥarālī reads the phrasing as an announcement to someone awaiting news and says قد signals the rarity of both the Prophet's turning and God's seeing it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r5.anchor: قال الحرالي : فيه نبأ إسماع لمن يرتقب أمرا أو خبرا يفيد مع المستقبل ندرة الوقوع

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r6.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r6.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the Prophet inwardly wanted the Kaaba, a qibla for all people, but relied on God's knowing his wish rather than asking; for one who asks, prayer obtains a need, while reliance on God's knowledge is worship.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r6.anchor: لأن الدعاء للطالبين قضاء حاجة وللمكتفين بعلم الله عبادة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī contrasts the worshipper, whose inward heart is his orientation and who should not raise his gaze, with the supplicant, who faces heaven and raises his hands.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r7.anchor: كما اختص غيب القلوب بوجهه المصلي , فالمصلي يرجع إلى غيب قلبه , ولا يرفع طرفه إلى السماء

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r8.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r8.claim: The passage cites a Prophetic warning that people must stop raising their eyes to heaven during prayer or their sight will be snatched; no grading is stated.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r8.anchor: ولينتهين أقوام عن رفع أبصارهم إلى السماء في الصلاة أو لتخطفن أبصارهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r9.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r9.claim: Al-Ḥarālī takes the indefinite qibla to anticipate a universal orientation to God, progressing from the Syrian qibla through the Hijazi qibla to an all-encompassing orientation.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r9.anchor: قال الحرالي : نكرها لما كان من ورائها قبلة التوجه العام في تنقله

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r10.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r10.claim: Al-Ḥarālī distinguishes what God wills from what is approved: an occurrence becomes pleasing only when approval follows, while a later removal shows it was willed but not approved.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r10.anchor: وفي قوله : { ترضاها } إنباء بإقراره للتوجه لهذه القبلة

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r11.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r11.claim: The Prophet's visible face turns toward the Kaaba, while his heart turns toward God: the unseen belongs to the unseen and the outward to the outward.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r11.anchor: وأما قلبك فإنما توجهه إلى الله , الغيب للغيب والظاهر للظاهر

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r12.speaker: الشافعي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r12.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī adduces Arab poetry to show that شطر means aiming at the very object when it is visible, and determining its direction through judgment when unseen.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r12.anchor: كما استدل الشافعي رحمه الله في الرسالة على ذلك بجملة من أشعار العرب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r13.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r13.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r13.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says calling it the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaaba broadens the expression; God called it sacred against entry marked by arrogance or confusion.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r13.anchor: قال الحرالي : سماه الله حراما على من يدخله دخول متكبر أو متحير

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r14.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r14.speaker: الماوردي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r14.claim: Al-Māwardī says “the Sacred Mosque” normally means the sanctuary elsewhere in the Qur'an, but here it means the Kaaba.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r14.anchor: وعن الإمام الماوردي أن كل موضع ذكر الله فيه المسجد الحرام فالمراد به الحرم إلا هذا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r15.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r15.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r15.claim: The expression suits a prayer context because prostration is prayer's greatest aim; the commentary returns to the phrase at 2:217.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r15.anchor: وعبر عنه بذلك لأن السياق للصلاة التي أعظم مقصودها السجود

BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r16.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r16.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r16.claim: God's mercy may uproot a sinner from his sins and place him where divine approval wills; the author says uncaused mercy excels in kind, while mercy answering a cause excels in its own force.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p265/r16.anchor: فإن رحمة من لا سبب منه تقتضي العطف عليه أبلغ في نوعها من حيث كونها ابتداء والأولى أبلغ في نفسها لما اقتضاها من السبب

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r1.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r1.claim: Saʿīd ibn al-Musayyib reports in the Muwaṭṭaʾ that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after arriving in Medina and the qibla changed two months before Badr.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r1.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب أنه قال

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r2.claim: The command “wherever you are” signals a third glad tiding: the community will multiply and spread across the regions of earth granted to it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r2.anchor: أشار إلى بشارة ثالثة بتكثير أمته ونشرهم في أقطار الأرض

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r3.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r3.claim: Al-Ḥarālī glosses turning faces toward it as directing one's acceptance toward God.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r4.claim: The People of the Book here are Jews and Christians, who know the qibla change is true and from their Lord, though they rejected the mercy they had awaited in the Messenger.

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r5.claim: They know this change is the truth from their Lord and the final truth about the qibla, with no further change to supersede it.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r5.anchor: أي ليس بعده في أمر القبلة حق آخر يرفعه أصلا

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r6.claim: The ending threatens the opponents while consoling, confirming, and strengthening the Prophet and his followers.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r6.anchor: وجعل ذلك سبحانه في سياق مهدد له مرج له ولأتباعه تسلية لهم وتثبيتا وتقوية لعزائمهم

BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r7.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r7.speaker: الحرالي
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r7.claim: Al-Ḥarālī says the yāʾ reading turns away from the opponents, while the tāʾ reading addresses them; this marks continued bad conduct in two degrees, with the worse degree met by God's turning to others.
BIQAI-FULL:v1p266/r7.anchor: قال الحرالي : بالياء أي التحتانية إعراضا عنهم , وبالتاء إقبالا عليهم

DURR-FULL:v1p342/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r1.speaker: البراء بن عازب
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r1.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet first prayed toward Jerusalem for six or seventeen months; after he turned toward the Kaaba, another congregation turned while bowing, and the community wondered about those who died before the change, leading to reassurance in 2:143.
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r1.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان أول ما قدم المدينة نزل على أخواله من الأنصار وأنه صلى إلى بيت المقدس ستة أو سبعة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p342/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r2.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r2.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports the Prophet repeatedly looked skyward awaiting the change; after the command Muslims asked about the dead and earlier prayers, the fools questioned it, and verses 2:143–142 followed.
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r2.anchor: عن البراء قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلي نحو بيت المقدس ويكثر النظر إلى السماء ينتظر أمر الله

DURR-FULL:v1p342/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r3.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r3.claim: Al-Barāʾ gives the Jerusalem-facing period as sixteen or seventeen months.
DURR-FULL:v1p342/r3.anchor: عن البراء قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر أو سبعة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p343/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r1.claim: The account continues that the Prophet wanted to pray toward the Kaaba and raised his head skyward; after the change, Jews asked what turned him from his former qibla.
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r1.anchor: وكان يجب أن يصلي نحو الكعبة فكان يرفع رأسه إلى السماء فأنزل الله (قد نرى تقلب وجهك

DURR-FULL:v1p343/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the qibla was the first abrogation: after migration to a largely Jewish city, the Prophet faced Jerusalem while longing for Abraham’s qibla; the Jews questioned the change, and 2:115 was also revealed.
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أول ما نسخ في القرآن القبلة وذلك أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لما هاجر إلى المدينة وكان أكثر أهلها اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p343/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports that at Mecca the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem with the Kaaba before him; after moving to Medina he did so for sixteen months before being turned to the Kaaba.
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم كان يصلي وهو بمكة نحو بيت المقدس والكعبة بين يديه وبعدما تحول إلى المدينة ستة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p343/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Prophet faced Jerusalem for seventeen months to win Jewish belief and following and draw in the Arabs; then the qibla changed, alongside the wording of 2:115.
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة وذلك أن محمدا كان يستقبل صخرة بيت المقدس وهي قبلة اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p343/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r5.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya reports that the Prophet wished God would turn him away from the Jews’ qibla and asked Gabriel about it.
DURR-FULL:v1p343/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم نظر نحو بيت المقدس فقال لجبريل وددت أن الله صرفني عن قبلة اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p344/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r1.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r1.claim: Gabriel said he could act only by God’s command and told the Prophet to pray to God; the Prophet kept looking up until the revelation came.
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r1.anchor: جبريل: إنما أنا عبد مثلك ولا أملك لك شيئا إلا ما أمرت فادع ربك وسله فجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

DURR-FULL:v1p344/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r2.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r2.claim: The report glosses the Prophet’s upward gaze as waiting for the answer he requested, and directs Muslims everywhere to turn in prayer toward the Kaaba.
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r2.anchor: يقول: إنك تديم النظر إلى السماء للذي سألت (فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام) يقول فحول وجهك في الصلاة نحو المسجد الحرام

DURR-FULL:v1p344/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās dates the shift from Syria to the Kaaba to Rajab, seventeen months after the Prophet arrived in Medina; Jewish leaders challenged him, seeking to turn him from his religion.
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: صرفت القبلة عن الشام إلى الكعبة في رجب على رأس سبعة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p344/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r8.claim: Through Mujāhid, Ibn ʿAbbās reports that the qibla was the first verse abrogated, followed by the first prayer.
DURR-FULL:v1p344/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: أول آية نسخت من القرآن القبلة ثم الصلاة الأولى

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.claim: Saʿd b. Abī Waqqāṣ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months and shifted to the Sacred Mosque two months before Badr.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r1.anchor: من طريق سعيد بن المسيب قال: سمعت سعد بن أبي وقاص يقول صلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم بعدما قدم المدينة

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.speaker: سعيد بن عبد العزيز
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.claim: Saʿīd b. ʿAbd al-ʿAzīz dates the Jerusalem-facing period from Rabīʿ I through Jumādā II.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r2.anchor: عن سعيد بن عبد العزيز أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس من شهر ربيع الأول إلى جمادى الآخرة

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.claim: Saʿīd b. al-Musayyib says the Anṣār prayed toward the first qibla for three years before the Prophet arrived, and he prayed that way sixteen months after arriving.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r3.anchor: عن سعيد بن المسيب أن الأنصار صلت للقبلة الأولى قبل قدوم النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة بثلاث حجج

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.claim: One report from Muʿādh b. Jabal gives the Prophet’s Jerusalem-facing period after arrival in Medina as sixteen months.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r4.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى للقبلة الأولى بعد قدومه المدينة ستة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.speaker: معاذ بن جبل
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.claim: A separate report from Muʿādh b. Jabal gives the period as thirteen months.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r5.anchor: عن معاذ بن جبل أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قدم المدينة فصلى نحو بيت المقدس ثلاثة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.claim: Anas reports nine or ten months; during noon prayer, after two rakʿas toward Jerusalem, the Prophet turned to the Kaaba and questioners asked why.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r6.anchor: عن أنس قال صلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم نحو بيت المقدس تسعة أشهر أو عشرة أشهر فبينما هو قائم يصلي الظهر بالمدينة

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.claim: Anas says he alone remained alive among those who prayed toward both qiblas.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r7.anchor: عن أنس قال: لم يبق ممن صلى للقبلتين غيري

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.speaker: أنس
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.claim: Anas reports a man from Banū Salima announced the change at dawn while the congregation was bowing, and they turned toward the Kaaba without leaving that posture.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r8.anchor: عن أنس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وأصحابه كانوا يصلون نحو بيت المقدس فلما نزلت هذه الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that worshippers at Qubāʾ were told during dawn prayer that the Prophet had been ordered to face the Kaaba, so they turned from Syria toward it.
DURR-FULL:v1p345#2/r9.anchor: عن الن عمر قال: بينما الناس بقباء في صلاة الصبح إذ جاءهم آت فقال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قد أنزل عليه

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r1.speaker: عثمان بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r1.claim: ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān reports that the Prophet awaited direction about the qibla and had adopted some People-of-the-Book practices that were neither commanded nor forbidden.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r1.anchor: في أخبار المدينة عن عثمان بن عبد الرحمن قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام يصلي انتظر أمر الله في القبلة

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r2.speaker: عثمان بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r2.claim: In ʿUthmān b. ʿAbd al-Raḥmān’s report, Gabriel signaled during the Prophet’s noon prayer after two rakʿas, prayed toward the Kaaba, and the Prophet followed as the verse came.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r2.anchor: في أخبار المدينة عن عثمان بن عبد الرحمن قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قام يصلي انتظر أمر الله في القبلة وكان يفعل أشياء لم يؤمر بها

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r3.speaker: عثمان بن عبد الرحمن
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r3.claim: The report recounts hypocrites saying Muhammad longed for home, polytheists accusing him of choosing them as his qibla, Jews objecting that he left the prophets’ qibla, and Muslims worrying about earlier dead.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r3.anchor: قال: فقال المنافقون: حن محمد إلى أرضه وقومه وقال المشركون: أراد محمد أن يجعلنا له قبلة

DURR-FULL:v1p346/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r4.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r4.claim: Qatāda calls the qibla a test: the Anṣār faced the first qibla for two years before the Prophet, who faced Jerusalem for sixteen months in Medina before the Kaaba; critics said he longed for home.
DURR-FULL:v1p346/r4.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله كانت القبلة فيها بلاء وتمحيص صلت الأنصار حولين قبل قدوم النبي وصلى نبي الله بعد قدومه المدينة نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r1.speaker: author
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r1.claim: The account says a witness and companion hid and prayed two rakʿas toward the Kaaba before the Prophet arrived and led the noon prayer facing it.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r1.anchor: فقرأ رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم هذه الآية {قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء} حتى فرغ من الآية

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r2.speaker: قتادة
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r2.claim: Qatāda says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem but longed for the Kaaba; God turned him to the desired qibla, and *shaṭr* means toward the Sacred Mosque.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r2.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله {قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها} قال: هو يومئذ يصلي نحو بيت المقدس

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r3.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r3.claim: Mujāhid reports that Jews claimed Muhammad opposed them while following their qibla; after he asked God for a qibla and the Kaaba was appointed, their claim ended and men and women exchanged places.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r3.anchor: عن مجاهد قال: قالت اليهود: يخالفنا محمد ويتبع قبلتنا فقال: يدعو الله ويستفرض القبلة فنزلت

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r4.claim: ʿAbd Allāh b. ʿAmr identifies the desired qibla as Abraham’s qibla, toward the mizāb.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r4.anchor: عن عبد الله بن عمرو في قوله {فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها} قال: قبلة إبراهيم نحو الميزاب

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r5.speaker: البراء
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r5.claim: Al-Barāʾ glosses *shaṭr* as the qibla of the Kaaba.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r5.anchor: عن البراء في قوله {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} قال: قبله

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r6.speaker: علي
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r6.anchor: عن علي في قوله {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} قال: شطره قبله

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r7.speaker: الحاكم
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r7.claim: Al-Ḥākim authenticates ʿAlī’s gloss that *shaṭr* means the Kaaba’s qibla.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r7.anchor: والحاكم وصححه والبيهقي في سننه عن علي في قوله {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} قال: شطره قبله

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses *shaṭr* as toward the Kaaba.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r8.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: شطره نحوه

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r9.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r9.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله {شطره} يعني نحوه

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r10.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r10.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya glosses the direction as toward the Sacred Mosque.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r10.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {شطر المسجد الحرام} قال: تلقاءه

DURR-FULL:v1p354/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r11.speaker: رفيع
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r11.claim: Rafīʿ says *shaṭr* means toward it in the Ethiopian language.
DURR-FULL:v1p354/r11.anchor: عن رفيع قال {شطره} تلقاءه بلسان الحبش

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r1.speaker: أبو رزين
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r1.claim: Abū Razīn reports that ʿAbd Allāh’s recitation has *qiblahu* in place of *shaṭrahu*.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r1.anchor: عن أبي رزين قال: في قراءة عبد الله (وحيثما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم قبله)

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the entire House is a qibla, and the doorway of the House is a qibla.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال: البيت كله قبلة وقبلة البيت الباب

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r3.claim: A Prophetic report from Ibn ʿAbbās sets nested qibla zones: the House for mosque-goers, the mosque for the Sacred Precinct, and the precinct for people across the earth.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس مرفوعا البيت قبلة لأهل المسجد والمسجد قبلة لأهل الحرم والحرم قبلة لأهل الأرض

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r4.speaker: السدي
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r4.claim: Al-Suddī says those given scripture here are the Jews.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r4.anchor: عن السدي في قوله {وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب} قال: أنزل ذلك في اليهود

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r5.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the truth they recognize is the qibla.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله {وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم} قال: يعني بذلك القبلة

DURR-FULL:v1p355/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r6.speaker: أبو العالية
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r6.claim: Abū al-ʿĀliya says they know the Kaaba was Abraham’s and the prophets’ qibla, but deliberately abandoned it.
DURR-FULL:v1p355/r6.anchor: عن أبي العالية في قوله {وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون أنه الحق من ربهم} يقول: ليعلمون أن الكعبة كانت قبلة إبراهيم والأنبياء ولكنهم تركوها عمدا

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r1.speaker: البراء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r1.claim: Al-Bara says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months in Medina, wished to turn toward the Kaaba, and was then redirected by revelation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r1.anchor: عن البراء ، قال : لما قدم رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة صلى نحو بيت المقدس

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r2.claim: Ibn Abbas calls the qibla the first Qur’anic abrogation: after migration, the Prophet faced Jerusalem for over a year among many Jews, longed for Abraham’s qibla, and prayed while looking skyward until revelation.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس : كان اول ما نسخ الله من القران القبلة ، وذلك ان رسول الله

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r3.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r3.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains the Prophet’s turning his face toward the sky as looking toward the sky.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r3.anchor: عن أبي العالية : قد نرى تقلب وجهك في السماء يقول : قد نرى نظرك إلى السماء .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r4.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r4.claim: Abdullah ibn Amr, standing opposite the Mizab, points toward the Kaaba and says this is the qibla God promised the Prophet.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r4.anchor: عن يحيى بن قمطة , قال : رايت عبد الله بن عمرو وهو بازاء الميزاب فقال : ان الله تعالى قال لنبيه - صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya says the Kaaba was the Prophet’s preferred qibla, so God turned him toward the qibla he desired and approved.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية : فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها : وذلك ان الكعبة كانت احب القبلتين إلى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r6.speaker: قتادة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r6.claim: Qatada glosses “turn your face” as “turn” or “direct yourself.”
IBNABIHATIM:v1p252#2/r6.anchor: عن قتادة , قوله : فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام : قال : توجه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r1.speaker: البراء
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r1.claim: Al-Bara glosses shatr al-masjid al-haram as its middle.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r1.anchor: عن البراء ، في قوله : فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام قال : وسطه .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r2.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r2.speaker: أبو العالية ومجاهد وقتادة والربيع بن أنس وسعيد بن جبير وعكرمة
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r2.claim: Abu al-Aliya rejects “middle” as intended and says shatr means toward it; the other named authorities report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r2.anchor: عن داود بن أبي هند قال : قلت لابي العالية قوله : فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام قال : هو عندك النصف

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r3.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r3.speaker: رفيع
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r3.claim: Rafiʿ says shatr means “toward it” in the language of the Abyssinians.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r3.anchor: عن داود عن رفيع : فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام قال تلقاءه بلسان الحبش .

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r4.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r4.speaker: علي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r4.claim: Ali says shatr means the qibla for the people addressed; al-Bara, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, and Qatada report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r4.anchor: عن على : وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره قال : شطره فينا قبلة

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r5.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r5.speaker: أبو العالية
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r5.claim: Abu al-Aliya explains “turn your faces toward it” as turning toward the Kaaba; Qatada and al-Rabiʿ report similarly.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r5.anchor: عن أبي العالية ، قوله : فولوا وجوهكم شطره اي تلقاءه

IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r6.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r6.speaker: السدي
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r6.claim: Al-Suddi says God then revealed that the People of the Book know the qibla is truth from their Lord, who is not heedless of their deeds.
IBNABIHATIM:v1p254/r6.anchor: عن السدى قال : ثم انزل الله في اليهود : وان الذين اوتوا الكتاب ليعلمون انه الحق من ربهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r1.claim: Ibrahim apparently faced the Kaaba in prayer and supplication when he built it, intending prayer around it because its interior could not hold the crowds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r1.anchor: فالظاهر أن إبراهيم عليه السلام لما بنى الكعبة استقبلها عند الدعاء وعند الصلاة وأنه بناها للصلاة حولها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r2.speaker: زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r2.claim: Ibn Ashur cites Zayd ibn Amr ibn Nufayl’s poem as evidence that Arabs knew prayer facing the Kaaba; he says there is no evidence Ibrahim faced it from distant locations.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r2.anchor: ويدل عليه قول زيد بن عمرو بن نفيل : عذت بما عاذ به إبراهم مستقبل المعبة وهو قائم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r3.claim: The obligation to orient prayer toward the Kaaba from far away appears to be a distinctive feature of this law and one way it completes the religion.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r3.anchor: فيكون الأمر بالتزام الاستقبال في الصلاة من خصائص هذه الشريعة ومن جملة معاني إكمال الدين بها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r4.claim: The verse implies Muslims changed from one prayer direction to another; because the destination was the Kaaba, the prior direction was Jerusalem, as the reports confirm.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r4.anchor: وقد دلت هذه الآية على أن المسلمين كانوا يستقبلون جهة ثم تحولوا عنها إلى جهة أخرى وليست التي تحول إليها المسلمون

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r5.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r5.claim: Ibn Umar reports that people at Quba were told during Fajr that revelation had commanded the Kaaba and turned from facing Syria; Ibn Ashur calls this the soundest report and the decisive account, transmitted by the Muwatta, Bukhari, and Muslim routes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r5.anchor: عن ابن دينار عن ابن عمر ( بينما الناس في صلاة الصبح بقباء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r6.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r6.claim: In Muslim’s report from Anas, a man told Banu Salima, already one rakah into Fajr, that the qibla had changed, and they turned while bowing.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r6.anchor: ثانيها : حديث مسلم عن أنس بن مالك وفيه ( فمر رجل من بني سلمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r7.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r7.claim: Al-Bara reports in Bukhari and Muslim that after sixteen or seventeen months facing Jerusalem, the Prophet turned to the Kaaba; an Ansar congregation changed to it after a worshipper informed them during Asr.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r7.anchor: عن البراء بن عازب قال كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r8.claim: Ibn Ashur reconciles Fajr and Asr in the reports by assigning them to different localities; he says other conflicting reports cited by al-Qurtubi have unsound chains.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r8.anchor: وحمل ذكر صلاة الصبح في روايتي ابن عمر وأنس بن مالك وذكر صلاة العصر في رواية البراء كل على أهل مكان مخصوص

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r9.claim: The qibla was changed in Rajab of 2 AH, two months before Badr; another report dates it to Tuesday, mid-Sha‘ban of that year.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p10/r9.anchor: فتحويل القبلة كان في رجب سنة اثنتين من الهجرة قبل بدر بشهرين وقيل يوم الثلاثاء نصف شعبان منها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r1.claim: The majority say the Prophet faced the Kaaba in Mecca when prayer was prescribed, then turned toward Jerusalem after reaching Medina to accommodate the Jews; Ibn Ashur calls that stated motive weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r1.anchor: فالجمهور على أنه لما فرضت عليه الصلاة بمكة كان يستقبل الكعبة فلما قدم المدينة استقبل بيت المقدس تألفا لليهود قاله بعضهم وهو ضعيف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r2.speaker: بعضهم
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r2.claim: A further view says he faced Jerusalem from a place where the Kaaba lay eastward, so he faced both; Ibn Ashur says this view is unsound.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r2.anchor: وقيل كان يستقبل بيت المقدس وهو في مكان يجعل الكعبة أمامه من جهة الشرق فيكون مستقبلا الكعبة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas and the majority say God commanded the Prophet by revelation to face Jerusalem and later abrogated it for the Kaaba, citing the verse about the former qibla.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r3.anchor: فقال ابن عباس والجمهور أوجبه الله عليه بوحي ثم نسخه باستقبال الكعبة ودليلهم قوله تعالى : { وما جعلنا القبلة التي كنت عليها }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r4.speaker: الطبري
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r4.claim: Al-Tabari says the Prophet could choose either the Kaaba or Jerusalem and chose Jerusalem to accommodate the Jews.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r4.anchor: وقال الطبري كان مخيرا بين الكعبة وبيت المقدس واختار بيت المقدس استئلافا لليهود

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r5.speaker: الحسن وعكرمة وأبو العالية
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r5.claim: Al-Hasan, Ikrima, and Abu al-Aliya attribute the Jerusalem direction to the Prophet’s own judgment: he followed the prior two religions’ qibla while wishing for a command to face the Kaaba.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r5.anchor: وقال الحسن وعكرمة وأبو العالية : كان ذلك عن اجتهاد من النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى هذا القول

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r6.speaker: الزجاج
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r6.claim: The “fools” who criticized the change are variously identified as Jews, hypocrites, or Quraysh disbelievers; al-Zajjaj cites the latter taunt that Muhammad missed his homeland and would soon return to their religion, attributed to al-Bara, Ibn Abbas, and al-Hasan.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r6.anchor: وقيل كفار قريش قالوا اشتاق محمد إلى بلده وعن قريب يرجع إلى دينكم ذكره الزجاج

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r7.speaker: القرطبي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r7.claim: Al-Qurtubi reports that Abu Said ibn al-Mualla was the first Muslim to pray toward the Kaaba, but Ibn Ashur says the report is weak.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p11/r7.anchor: وروى القرطبي أن أول من صلى نحو الكعبة من المسلمين أبو سعيد بن المعلى وفي الحديث ضعف

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r1.claim: The fā in “then We will turn you” marks sequence and stresses the explicit promise after the preliminary, implicit reassurance that God sees the Prophet’s gaze.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r1.anchor: والفاء في { فلنولينك } فاء التعقيب لتأكيد الوعد بالصراحة بعد التمهيد لها بالكناية في قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r2.claim: Tawliya here means directing the Prophet toward a qibla; qibla is expressed as an expanded second object, originally “turn you from a qibla.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r2.anchor: فمعنى { فلنولينك قبلة } لنوجهنك إلى قبلة ترضاها . فانتصب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r3.claim: The command to face the Kaaba follows the promise immediately; its two emphases and sequencing express exceptional kindness and attention to the Prophet’s wish.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r3.anchor: والمعنى أن تولية وجهه للكعبة سيحصل عقب هذا الوعد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r4.claim: The Prophet’s inclination toward the Kaaba seeks a good: it is the house most suited to signify monotheism and its qibla marks Islam’s independence from the People of the Book.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r4.anchor: وعبر بترضاها للدلالة على أن ميله إلى الكعبة ميل لقصد الخير بناء على أن الكعبة أجدر بيوت الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r5.claim: The word “pleased” suggests affection grounded in reflection, befitting the Prophet’s reasoned preference for a lasting benefit after the temporary reason for facing Jerusalem ended; the verse warns against following others’ desires.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p27/r5.anchor: ولما كان الرضى مشعرا بالمحبة الناشئة عن تعقل اختير في هذا المقام دون تحبها أو تهواها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r1.claim: The command follows the promise and hastens its fulfillment; prayer is understood from the context of the dispute with the fools, and the next clause extends the command to the whole community.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r1.anchor: وقوله : { فول وجهك } تفريع على الوعد وتعجيل به والمعنى فول وجهك في حالة الصلاة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r2.claim: Shatr with fatḥa on shīn and sukūn on ṭā means direction or side; Qatada glosses it as “toward.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r2.anchor: والشطر بفتح الشين وسكون الطاء الجهة والناحية وفسره قتادة بتلقاء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r3.speaker: أبي بن كعب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r3.claim: Ubayy ibn Kab’s reading has تلقاء (“toward”) in place of shatr, supporting the directional sense.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r4.speaker: الجبائي وعبد الجبار
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r4.claim: Al-Jubba’i and Abd al-Jabbar interpret shatr as the middle of the sanctuary, figuratively identifying the Kaaba; Abd al-Jabbar argues prayer aimed elsewhere in the mosque is invalid and this reading gives shatr a function.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r4.anchor: وفسر الجبائي وعبد الجبار الشطر هنا بأنه وسط الشيء

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r5.claim: The prior promise highlights how much the Prophet’s wish is valued, especially through the description “a qibla you are pleased with.”
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r5.anchor: فائدته إظهار الاهتمام برغبة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأنها بحيث يعتنى بها كما دل عليه وصف القبلة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r6.claim: Nuwallika means “we direct you”; the verb’s sense is linked to walī as attachment or connection when physical nearness is not intended.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r6.anchor: ومعنى ( نولينك ) نوجهنك ، وفي التوجيه قرب معنوي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r7.claim: Walla may take the face and destination as two objects, with a third introduced by ʿan to mark turning away; it can also be treated as intransitive with the other objects understood.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p28/r7.anchor: والظاهر أن تعديته إلى مفعول ثان من قبيل الحذف والتقدير ولى وجهه إلى كذا ثم يعدونه إلى مفعول ثالث بحرف عن

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.claim: Shatr is the second object of wallā, not an adverbial of place.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r1.anchor: وانتصب { شطر المسجد } على المفعول الثاني لول وليس منصوبا على الظرفية

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.claim: The added conditional expressly extends facing the Kaaba to all Muslims and places; the repeated command reinforces general application, while the Prophet-specific address first consoles him. Islamic rulings ordinarily include his community absent contrary evidence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r2.anchor: وقوله : { وحيث ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره } تنصيص على تعميم حكم استقبال الكعبة لجميع المسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.claim: These commands establish the obligation to face the Kaaba in prayer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r3.anchor: وهذه الآيات دليل على وجوب هذا الاستقبال وهو حكمة عظيمة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.claim: Prayer's aim is worship and submission; focusing on the worshipped strengthens humility, sincere obedience, and avoidance of sin. Because God is beyond sensory perception, a reminder associated with Him helps recall His majesty.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r4.anchor: ذلك أن المقصود من الصلاة العبادة والخضوع لله تعالى وبمقدار استحضار المعبود يقوى الخضوع له

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.speaker: الحديث الصحيح
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.claim: An authentic hadith defines ihsan as worshipping God as though one sees Him, or knowing that He sees the worshipper.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r5.anchor: جاء في الحديث الصحيح : ( الإحسان أن تعبد الله كأنك تراه فإن لم تكن تراه فإنه يراك )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.speaker: فخر الدين
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.claim: Fakhr al-Din says intellect grasps abstractions while imagination needs sensible forms; facing the qibla is like facing a king, Quranic praise like praising him, and bowing and prostration like serving him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p29#2/r6.anchor: قال فخر الدين : ( إن الله تعالى خلق في الإنسان قوة عقلية مدركة للمجردات والمعقولات

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r1.claim: The statement about those given scripture is parenthetical between the command in 2:144 and the renewed command in 2:149.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r1.anchor: اعتراض بين جملة : { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام } وجملة { ومن حيث خرجت فول وجهك }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r2.speaker: السدي
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies those given scripture as the Jewish and Christian religious scholars.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r2.anchor: أن المراد بالذين أوتوا الكتاب أحبار اليهود وأحبار النصارى كما روى عن السدي

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur prefers that the verse refers to those who remained unbelievers; the emphatic statement then answers their apparent rejection and threatens them for opposing what they knew.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r3.anchor: والأظهر أيضا أن المراد بالذين أوتوا الكتاب هم الذين لم يزالوا على الكفر ليظهر موقع قوله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r4.claim: Their knowledge that Muhammad is true, based on the glad tidings about him in their scriptures, entails knowing that what he brought is true.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r4.anchor: معنى كونهم يعلمون أنه الحق أن علمهم بصدق محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم حسب البشارة به في كتبهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r5.claim: The definite predicate implies exclusivity: facing the Kaaba is the truth rather than the former directions, in light of the supersession of earlier law by Islam.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r5.anchor: وقد دل التعريف في قوله : { أنه الحق } على القصر أي يعلمون أن الاستقبال للكعبة هو الحق دون غيره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r6.claim: An unnamed explanation says their scriptures foretold that their qibla would be abolished, perhaps through Jeremiah's and Isaiah's warnings that Jerusalem would be destroyed.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p33/r6.anchor: وقيل إنهم كانوا يجدون في كتبهم أن قبلتهم ستبطل ولعل هذا مأخوذ من إنذارات أنبيائهم مثل أرميا وأشعيا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r1.speaker: الجمهور
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r1.claim: The majority read the verb with third-person yāʾ, with its pronoun referring to those given scripture.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r1.anchor: قرأه الجمهور بياء الغيبة والضمير للذين أوتوا الكتاب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r2.claim: On the majority reading, their deeds are acting against what they know, including stubborn denial, obstinacy, and folly; the warning implicitly threatens them.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r2.anchor: عن عملهم بغير ما علموا فالمراد بما يعملون هذا العمل ونحوه من المكابرة والعناد والسفه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r3.claim: The threat to the opponents also implies good news for Muslims: it signals their high standing and that God rewards each group according to its deeds.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r3.anchor: ووعيدهم يستلزم في المقام الخطابي وعدا للمسلمين لدلالته على عظيم منزلتهم

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r4.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وروح عن يعقوب
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r4.claim: These readers use second-person tāʾ; this turns the statement into a promise for Muslims who obey and a threat to disbelievers, reversing the emphasis of the majority reading.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r4.anchor: وقرأه ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر وروح عن يعقوب بتاء الخطاب فهو كناية عن وعد للمسلمين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r5.claim: Under either reading the clause is a general concluding statement between the mention of those given scripture and the next clause in 2:145, allowing each group its share of warning or promise.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r5.anchor: وعلى القراءتين فهو تذييل إجمالي ليأخذ كل حظه منه وهو اعتراض بين جملة : { وإن الذين أوتوا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r6.claim: The two phrases form altered perfect paronomasia in the majority reading and incomplete near-consonant paronomasia in Ibn ʿĀmir's reading and those who agree with him.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v2p34/r6.anchor: وفي قوله : { ليعلمون } وقوله : { عما يعملون } ( البقرة : 96 ) الجناس التام المحرف على قراءة الجمهور والجناس الناقص المضارع

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.claim: The intended sense is the movement of the gaze; face is used because it is more inclusive and honored, and commonly appears in expressions of seeking what one wants.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r1.anchor: المقصد تقلب البصر، وذكر الوجه لأنه أعم وأشرف، وهو المستعمل في طلب الرغائب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.claim: The cited line uses face in the expression of spending one’s face, demonstrating its use in seeking a desired outcome.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r2.anchor: ومنه قول الشاعر: [الطويل] رجعت بما أبغي ووجهي بمائه

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r3.claim: The face also turns as the eyes turn.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.speaker: قتادة والسدي وغيرهما
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.claim: Qatāda, al-Suddī, and others say the Prophet looked toward heaven in prayer, asking God to turn him toward Mecca.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r4.anchor: وقال قتادة والسدي وغيرهما: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يقلب وجهه في الدعاء إلى الله تعالى أن يحوله إلى قبلة مكة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.claim: Another explanation is that he looked upward to be granted permission to supplicate.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r5.anchor: وقيل كان يقلب ليؤذن له في الدعاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.claim: He faced heaven because it is a direction from which mercy, rain, lights, and revelation may come; people turn their hopes toward the source of blessings.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r6.anchor: ومعنى التقلب نحو السماء أن السماء جهة قد تعود العالم منها الرحمة كالمطر والأنوار والوحي

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.claim: Tarḍāhā means that you love and welcome it, and that it delights your eye.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r7.anchor: وترضاها معناه تحبها وتقر بها عينك

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.speaker: مجاهد
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.claim: Mujāhid says the Prophet wanted the Kaaba because Jews claimed Muhammad did not know his religion until he followed them.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r8.anchor: فقال مجاهد: لقول اليهود ما علم محمد دينه حتى اتبعنا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the shift was desired so that the Prophet would face Abraham’s qibla.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r9.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: وليصيب قبلة إبراهيم عليه السلام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.speaker: الربيع والسدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.claim: Al-Rabīʿ and al-Suddī say the shift would draw the Arabs closer because they loved the Kaaba.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r10.anchor: وقال الربيع والسدي: وليستألف العرب لمحبتها في الكعبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.speaker: عبد الله بن عمر
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.claim: ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿUmar says the Prophet and his community faced the line of the Kaaba’s rainspout.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r11.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عمر: إنما وجه رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم وأمته حيال ميزاب الكعبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās and others say the Prophet was directed toward the whole House, not only its rainspout.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r12.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وغيره: بل وجه إلى البيت كله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.claim: The rainspout direction is the qibla for Medina and Syria, and clearly for al-Andalus; the Kaaba is the qibla from every region.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r13.anchor: والميزاب هو قبلة المدينة والشام، وهنالك قبلة أهل الأندلس بلا ريب، ولا خلاف أن الكعبة قبلة من كل أفق

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.claim: The command orders the change of qibla and abrogates the direction toward Syria.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r14.anchor: وقوله تعالى: فول وجهك شطر المسجد الآية، أمر بالتحول ونسخ لقبلة الشام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r15.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r15.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r15.claim: One report says the verse came during the noon prayer after two rakʿas and that the Prophet turned during the prayer; Abū al-Faraj names ʿAbbād ibn Nahīk as present.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r15.anchor: وقيل: نزل ذلك على النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وهو في صلاة الظهر بعد ركعتين منها فتحول في الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r16.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r16.speaker: أبو الفرج
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r16.claim: Abū al-Faraj reports that ʿAbbād ibn Nahīk was with the Prophet during this prayer.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r16.anchor: وذكر أبو الفرج أن عباد بن نهيك كان مع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في هذه الصلاة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r17.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r17.speaker: قيل
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r17.claim: Another view says the verse came outside prayer, and the first prayer toward the Kaaba was ʿAṣr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r17.anchor: وقيل: إنما نزلت هذه الآية في غير صلاة وكانت أول صلاة إلى الكعبة العصر

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r18.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r18.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r18.claim: Shatr is accusative as an adverbial expression, resembling a direct object because the verb reaches it; it means toward or in the direction of.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p221#2/r18.anchor: وشطر نصب على الظرف ويشبه المفعول به لوقوع الفعل عليه ومعناه نحو وتلقاء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r1.claim: A cited line uses شطر to mean toward, here toward Najd.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r1.anchor: تعدو بنا شطر نجد وهي عاقدة ... قد كارب العقد من إيفادها الحقبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r2.claim: A cited poem uses شطر in the sense of toward Banū Tamīm.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r2.anchor: أقول لأم زنباع أقيمي ... صدور العيس شطر بني تميم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r3.claim: A cited line uses شطر to mean toward the enemy’s pass or frontier.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r3.anchor: وقد أظلكم من شطر ثغركم ... هول له ظلم تغشاكم قطعا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r4.speaker: خفاف بن عمير
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r4.claim: Khifāf ibn ʿUmayr’s line uses شطر to mean toward ʿAmr.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r4.anchor: وقال غيره [خفاف بن عمير] : [الوافر] ألا من مبلغ عمرا رسولا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r5.claim: The command wherever you are addresses the whole community and abrogates the earlier rule.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r5.anchor: وحيث ما كنتم فولوا أمر للأمة ناسخ

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r6.speaker: داود بن أبي هند
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r6.claim: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind says Ibn Masʿūd’s codex has تلقاء المسجد الحرام in place of شطر المسجد الحرام.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r6.anchor: وقال داود بن أبي هند: إن في حرف ابن مسعود: فول وجهك تلقاء المسجد الحرام

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r7.speaker: محمد بن طلحة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r7.claim: Muḥammad ibn Ṭalḥa says the wording in the codex is فولوا وجوهكم قبله.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r7.anchor: وقال محمد بن طلحة: إن فيه: فولوا وجوهكم قبله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r8.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r8.claim: Ibn Abī ʿAbla reads فولوا وجوهكم تلقاءه.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة: «فولوا وجوهكم تلقاءه»

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r9.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r9.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r9.claim: Those given scripture are the Jews and Christians together.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r10.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r10.speaker: السدي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r10.claim: Al-Suddī says the phrase refers to the Jews.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r11.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r11.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r11.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya prefers the broader referent: Jews and Christians know that the Kaaba is Abraham’s qibla and the true direction binding on everyone, as Muhammad’s coming is in their books.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r11.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: والأول أظهر، والمعنى أن اليهود والنصارى يعلمون أن الكعبة هي قبلة إبراهيم إمام الأمم

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r12.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r12.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r12.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir, Ḥamza, and al-Kisāʾī read the verb with tāʾ as direct address, referring either to the People of the Book or Muhammad’s community; in either case it warns that God does not overlook their deeds.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r12.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «عما تعملون» بتاء على المخاطبة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r13.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r13.speaker: الباقون
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v1p222/r13.claim: The other readers use third-person yāʾ in يعملون.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r1.speaker: البراء وابن عباس وابن المسيب وأبو العالية وقتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r1.claim: The reported occasion is that the Prophet wanted to face the Kaaba; this is attributed to al-Bara, Ibn Abbas, Ibn al-Musayyib, Abu al-Aliya, and Qatada.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r1.anchor: قاله البراء واين ابن عباس وابن المسيب و أبوالعالية وقتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r2.speaker: بعض المفسرين
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r2.claim: Some commentators say this verse came down earlier than the verse beginning “The foolish among the people will say.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r2.anchor: وذكر بعض المفسرين أن هذه الآية مقدمة في النزول

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Prophet preferred the Kaaba because it had been Abraham's qibla.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r3.anchor: أحدهما أنها كانت قبلة إبراهيم روى عن ابن عباس

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r4.speaker: مجاهد
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r4.claim: Mujahid says the Prophet preferred the Kaaba to differ from the Jews.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r5.claim: The Prophet's turning his face means looking toward the sky, right and left.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r5.anchor: ومعنى تقلب وجهه نظره إليها يمينا وشمالا

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r6.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r6.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r6.claim: The preposition fi is used with the sense of “toward.”
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r6.anchor: في بمعنى إلى و ترضاها بمعنى تحبها

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r7.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r7.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r7.claim: Tardaha means “you love” or desire it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r7.anchor: ترضاها بمعنى تحبها والشطر النحو من غير خلاف

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r8.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r8.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r8.claim: Shatr means the direction or toward; the author reports no disagreement on this meaning.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r8.anchor: والشطر النحو من غير خلاف قال ابن عمر أتى الناس آت وهم في صلاة الصبح بقباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r9.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r9.claim: Ibn Umar reports that people praying dawn prayer at Quba turned toward the Kaaba after being told revelation had commanded it.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r9.anchor: قال ابن عمر أتى الناس آت وهم في صلاة الصبح بقباء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r10.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r10.speaker: البراء بن عازب ومعقل بن يسار
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r10.claim: Al-Bara ibn Azib and Maqil ibn Yasar date the change to Monday at noon in mid-Rajab, seventeen months after the Prophet arrived in Medina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r10.anchor: قاله البراء بن عازب و معقل بن يسار

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r11.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r11.speaker: قتادة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r11.claim: Qatada dates the change to Tuesday in mid-Shaʿban, eighteen months after the Prophet's arrival in Medina.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r11.anchor: والثاني أنها حولت يوم الثلاثاء للنصف من شعبان على رأس ثمانية عشر شهرا من مقدمه المدينة قاله قتادة

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r12.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r12.speaker: إبراهيم الحربي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r12.claim: Ibrahim al-Harbi's account, quoted by Ibn Salama, places the change in Jumada II.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r12.anchor: والثالث أنها حولت في جمادى الآخرة حكاه ابن سلامة المفسر عن إبراهيم الحربي

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r13.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r13.speaker: مقاتل
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r13.claim: Muqatil identifies the People of the Book who know this is true as the Jews.

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r14.speaker: أبو سليمان الدمشقي
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r14.claim: Abu Sulayman al-Dimashqi identifies them as both Jews and Christians.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v1p156#2/r14.anchor: والثاني اليهود والنصارى قاله أبو سليمان الدمشقي

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says the qibla was the first Qur'anic abrogation: after migration, the Prophet faced Jerusalem for over a year at God's command, though he loved Abraham's qibla and prayed looking skyward; the change unsettled the Jews, and God had tested who followed the Messenger.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r1.anchor: قال علي بن أبي طلحة عن ابن عباس: كان أول ما نسخ من القرآن القبلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r2.claim: Another Ibn ʿAbbas report says that after praying toward Jerusalem the Prophet raised his head to heaven; God revealed the change toward the Kaaba, with Gabriel directing him toward its water-spout.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r2.anchor: عن عكرمة، عن ابن عباس: قال: كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا سلم من صلاته إلى بيت المقدس رفع رأسه إلى السماء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r3.claim: Yahya b. Qumta saw ʿAbd Allah b. ʿAmr facing toward the Kaaba's mizab and explaining that the commanded direction was toward it; al-Hakim graded the chain sound and said the two compilers did not include it.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r3.anchor: قال: رأيت عبد الله بن عمرو (2) جالسا في المسجد الحرام، بإزاء الميزاب، فتلا هذه الآية

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r4.speaker: الشافعي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r4.claim: One of al-Shafiʿi's two positions requires facing the Kaaba itself, based on reports specifying its line or the direction of its mizab.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r4.anchor: وهكذا قال غيره، وهو أحد قولي الشافعي، رحمه الله: إن الغرض إصابة عين القبلة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r5.speaker: الأكثرون
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r5.claim: The majority position, also attributed to al-Shafiʿi, requires facing the Kaaba's direction; Ali glosses shatr as its qibla, and al-Hakim grades the report sound.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p458/r5.anchor: والقول الآخر وعليه الأكثرون: أن المراد المواجهة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r1.speaker: أبو العالية، مجاهد، عكرمة، سعيد بن جبير، قتادة، الربيع بن أنس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r1.claim: Abu al-ʿAliya, Mujahid, ʿIkrima, Saʿid b. Jubayr, Qatada, and al-Rabiʿ b. Anas support facing the Kaaba's direction; Ibn Kathir cites the rule that the area between east and west is qibla.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r1.anchor: وهذا قول أبي العالية، ومجاهد، وعكرمة، وسعيد بن جبير، وقتادة، والربيع بن أنس

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r2.speaker: النبي ﷺ
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r2.claim: A report quoted by al-Qurtubi from Ibn ʿAbbas says the qibla is between east and west for mosque-goers, the mosque for people of the Haram, and the Haram for people across the earth.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r2.anchor: وقال القرطبي: روى ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال: "ما بين المشرق والمغرب قبلة لأهل المسجد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r3.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r3.claim: Al-Bara' reports the Prophet faced Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months; after the change during the afternoon prayer, a man informed another congregation, who turned toward the House while still bowing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r3.anchor: عن البراء أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى قبل بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r4.speaker: البراء بن عازب
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r4.claim: A second route from al-Bara' says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months, wished to turn toward the Kaaba, and was redirected when this verse was revealed.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r4.anchor: وقال عبد الرزاق: أخبرنا إسرائيل، عن أبي إسحاق، عن البراء

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r5.speaker: أبو سعيد بن المعلى
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r5.claim: Abu Saʿid b. al-Muʿalla recounts hearing the Prophet read the verse from the minbar; before the Prophet led noon prayer, he and a companion hid to perform two cycles, becoming the first to pray toward the new qibla.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p459/r5.anchor: وروى النسائي عن أبي سعيد بن المعلى قال: كنا نغدو إلى المسجد على عهد رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r1.speaker: ابن عمر
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r1.claim: Ibn ʿUmar reports that the Prophet’s first prayer toward the Kaaba was Ẓuhr, which was the middle prayer.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r1.anchor: عن ابن عمر: أن أول صلاة صلاها رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إلى الكعبة صلاة الظهر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r2.claim: The well-known account makes the first prayer toward the Kaaba ʿAṣr, explaining why the people of Qubāʾ heard the news only by Fajr.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r2.anchor: والمشهور أن أول صلاة صلاها إلى الكعبة صلاة العصر، ولهذا تأخر الخبر عن أهل قباء إلى صلاة الفجر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r3.speaker: نويلة بنت مسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r3.claim: Nuwayla reports that worshippers at Banū Ḥāritha, facing Jerusalem in Ẓuhr or ʿAṣr, turned toward the Kaaba after hearing the Prophet had done so, and completed the prayer in the new direction.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r3.anchor: عن جدته أم أبيه نويلة بنت مسلم، قالت: صلينا الظهر -أو العصر

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r4.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r4.claim: A man of Banū Ḥāritha reports that the Prophet praised those who changed direction during prayer as men who believe in the unseen.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r4.anchor: فحدثني رجل من بني حارثة أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r5.speaker: عمارة بن أوس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r5.claim: ʿUmāra ibn Aws reports that a caller announced the qibla change while they were bowing toward Jerusalem, and the imam, men, and boys turned toward the Kaaba while still bowing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460/r5.anchor: عن عمارة بن أوس قال: بينما نحن في الصلاة نحو بيت المقدس، ونحن ركوع، إذ أتى مناد بالباب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r1.claim: The command requires facing the Kaaba from every direction on earth: east, west, north, and south.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r1.anchor: أمر تعالى باستقبال الكعبة من جميع جهات الأرض، شرقا وغربا وشمالا وجنوبا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r2.claim: A traveler may perform voluntary prayer facing whichever way the mount or body turns, while keeping the heart oriented toward the Kaaba.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r2.anchor: سوى النافلة في حال السفر، فإنه يصليها حيثما توجه قالبه، وقلبه نحو الكعبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r3.claim: In combat with weapons, a worshipper prays in whatever condition is possible.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r3.anchor: وكذا في حال المسايفة في القتال يصلي على كل حال

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r4.claim: Someone unable to identify the qibla prays after exercising judgment; even if mistaken, this is excused because God does not burden a soul beyond its capacity.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r4.anchor: من جهل جهة القبلة يصلي باجتهاده، وإن كان مخطئا في نفس الأمر، لأن الله تعالى لا يكلف نفسا إلا وسعها

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r5.speaker: المالكية
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r5.claim: The Mālikīs infer that a worshipper looks straight ahead, since looking at the place of prostration would require bending and impair full upright posture.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r5.anchor: قال المالكية لقوله: {فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام} فلو نظر إلى موضع سجوده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r6.speaker: الشافعي وأحمد وأبو حنيفة
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r6.claim: Al-Shāfiʿī, Aḥmad, and Abū Ḥanīfa hold that the worshipper looks at the place of prostration while standing, contrary to the Mālikī view.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r6.anchor: كما ذهب إليه الشافعي وأحمد وأبو حنيفة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r7.speaker: بعضهم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r7.claim: Some authorities say the worshipper looks toward the chest while standing.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r7.anchor: وقال بعضهم: ينظر المصلي في قيامه إلى صدره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r8.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r8.speaker: شريك القاضي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r8.claim: Sharīk al-Qāḍī agrees with the majority that one looks at the place of prostration when standing, since this better promotes humility and is supported by a hadith.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r8.anchor: وقال شريك القاضي: ينظر في حال قيامه إلى موضع سجوده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r9.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r9.speaker: شريك القاضي
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r9.claim: Sharīk assigns the gaze to the feet in bowing, the nose in prostration, and the lap while sitting.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p460#2/r9.anchor: وأما في حال ركوعه فإلى موضع قدميه، وفي حال سجوده إلى موضع أنفه وفي حال قعوده إلى حجره

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p461/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p461/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p461/r1.claim: The Jews who objected to the Kaaba direction knew God would direct the Prophet to it: their scriptures described the Prophet and his community and foretold his uniquely complete, honored law. They concealed this knowledge from envy, disbelief, and obstinacy, so God threatens them.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p461/r1.anchor: أي: واليهود -الذين أنكروا استقبالكم الكعبة وانصرافكم عن بيت المقدس -يعلمون

JISHUMI:v1p630/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r1.claim: The preceding point says this passage excludes the Prophet asking for a change without revelation.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r1.anchor: وهذا ينفي أن يسأله بغير الوحي

JISHUMI:v1p630/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r2.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p630/r2.claim: One explanation is that Muhammad looked toward heaven while waiting for the promised change of qibla.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r2.anchor: قيل: لانتظار الموعود، وقيل: لانتظار الوحي في أمر القبلة

JISHUMI:v1p630/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r3.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p630/r3.claim: Another explanation is that he awaited revelation about the qibla.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r3.anchor: وقيل: لانتظار الوحي في أمر القبلة

JISHUMI:v1p630/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r4.claim: He turned his gaze skyward because Gabriel brought revelation to him from heaven.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r4.anchor: وإنما قلب طرفه نحو السماء لأن جبريل (عليه السلام) يأتيه بالوحي من السماء

JISHUMI:v1p630/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r5.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p630/r5.claim: A view says he had been barred from Jerusalem before another qibla was specified, so he looked up anxiously as prayer time came.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r5.anchor: أنه منع عن استقبال بيت المقدس، ولم تعين له القبلة، فضاق صدره

JISHUMI:v1p630/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r6.claim: Jishumi rejects that account: prayer would not be required before the direction of prayer had been made clear.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r6.anchor: لأنه لا يجوز أن يؤمر بالصلاة إلا مع بيان موضع التوجه

JISHUMI:v1p630/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r7.claim: God will turn Muhammad toward a qibla that he wants and loves.

JISHUMI:v1p630/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r8.speaker: الأصم
JISHUMI:v1p630/r8.claim: Al-Asamm reads this as a qibla to which Muhammad is content, whatever direction he is commanded to face.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r8.anchor: قبلة وأنت راض بكل وجهة تؤمر بها، عن الأصم

JISHUMI:v1p630/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r9.speaker: مجاهد وابن زيد
JISHUMI:v1p630/r9.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say he wanted the change to differ from and distinguish Muslims from the Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r9.anchor: فيه مخالفة لليهود، وتميز منهم، عن مجاهد وابن زيد

JISHUMI:v1p630/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
JISHUMI:v1p630/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas says he wanted the change because the Kaaba was Abraham's qibla.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r10.anchor: لأنه قبلة إبراهيم (عليه السلام)، عن ابن عباس

JISHUMI:v1p630/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r11.speaker: الزجاج
JISHUMI:v1p630/r11.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the Kaaba would encourage Arabs to embrace faith because it accorded with their people.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r11.anchor: لاستدعاء العرب للإيمان؛ إذ هو موافق لقومه، حكاه الزجاج

JISHUMI:v1p630/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r12.claim: The soundest reason is that God promised the change and Muhammad knew it was beneficial, so he wanted it.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r12.anchor: لأنه وعد ذلك فعلم أنه المصلحة فأحبه لذلك، وهو الصحيح

JISHUMI:v1p630/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r13.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r13.claim: Jishumi allows that Muhammad wanted all these benefits, since the explanations do not conflict.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r13.anchor: ويحتمل أنه أحب جميع ذلك؛ إذ لا تنافي فيه

JISHUMI:v1p630/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r14.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r14.claim: Here, turning the face means turning the self.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r14.anchor: فول وجهك يعني فول نفسك، ووجه الشيء: نفسه

JISHUMI:v1p630/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r15.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p630/r15.claim: The face is singled out because orientation is manifested through it.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r15.anchor: ذكر الوجه لأنه به يظهر التوجه

JISHUMI:v1p630/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r16.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأكثر أهل العلم
JISHUMI:v1p630/r16.claim: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatada, and most scholars understand shatr as toward the Sacred Mosque.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r16.anchor: نحو المسجد الحرام، عن ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة وأكثر أهل العلم

JISHUMI:v1p630/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r17.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p630/r17.claim: A second view takes shatr as the mosque's middle: it is half from each side, where the Kaaba lies, and thus refers to the Kaaba.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r17.anchor: وسط المسجد الحرام؛ لأنه من سائر جنباته هو النصف والشطر النصف، والكعبة واقعة بين المسجد في النصف من كل جهة

JISHUMI:v1p630/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r18.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p630/r18.claim: Al-Qadi says the most accurate meaning is the Meccan mosque; the qibla is the Kaaba, which he identifies with the mosque.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r18.anchor: قال القاضي: هو الأصح المسجد الحرام يعني مسجد مكة، وإنما أمر به لأن القبلة هي الكعبة

JISHUMI:v1p630/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r19.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r19.claim: The entire House is the qibla, and Jishumi says this is agreed upon.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r19.anchor: فقيل: البيت كله قبلة، وعليه الإجماع

JISHUMI:v1p630/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r20.speaker: بعضهم
JISHUMI:v1p630/r20.claim: A report that everyone must aim at the roof's waterspout contradicts consensus.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r20.anchor: وروي عن بعضهم أن على الناس أن يقصدوا الميزاب، وهو خلاف الإجماع

JISHUMI:v1p630/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r21.speaker: قتادة وغيره
JISHUMI:v1p630/r21.claim: Qatada and others report that the qibla changed in Rajab after noon while the Prophet was praying, and he turned during the prayer.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r21.anchor: حولت القبلة في رجب بعد زوال الشمس، وهو يصلي، فتحول، عن قتادة وغيره

JISHUMI:v1p630/r22.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r22.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r22.claim: The command applies wherever people are on earth, whether at sea or on land, on level ground or a mountain.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r22.anchor: أينما كنتم من الأرض في بر أو بحر، سهل أو جبل فولوا وجوهكم شطره

JISHUMI:v1p630/r23.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r23.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r23.claim: The direction is repeated because the first address concerned Medina's residents and might have seemed local; the repetition makes it universal for worshippers.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r23.anchor: الأول كان خطابا لمن كان في المدينة، فجاز أن يظن أن ذلك قبلتهم، فبين تعالى أنه قبلة لجميع المصلين

JISHUMI:v1p630/r24.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r24.speaker: السدي
JISHUMI:v1p630/r24.claim: Al-Suddi says those given scripture are the Jews specifically, and the scripture is the Torah.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r24.anchor: أراد اليهود خاصة، والكتاب: التوراة، عن السدي

JISHUMI:v1p630/r25.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r25.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r25.claim: Jishumi prefers the broader sense: Jewish rabbis and Christian scholars, with Torah and Gospel, because the wording is general.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r25.anchor: أحبار اليهود وعلماء النصارى، وهو الصحيح، لعموم اللفظ، والكتاب: التوراة والإنجيل

JISHUMI:v1p630/r26.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r26.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r26.claim: He argues that the knowledgeable group must be small, since a large group could not collude to conceal the truth.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r26.anchor: ولا بد أن يكونوا عددا قليلا؛ لأن الكثير لا يجوز عليهم التواطؤ على الكتمان

JISHUMI:v1p630/r27.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r27.speaker: أبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p630/r27.claim: Abu Ali takes the truth to be the commanded change of qibla.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r27.anchor: التحويل حق مأمور به، عن أبي علي

JISHUMI:v1p630/r28.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r28.speaker: الحسن
JISHUMI:v1p630/r28.claim: Al-Hasan says facing the Kaaba is true because it was Abraham's qibla and that of prophets before him.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r28.anchor: التوجه إلى الكعبة حق؛ لأنها قبلة إبراهيم والأنبياء قبله، عن الحسن

JISHUMI:v1p630/r29.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r29.speaker: القاضي
JISHUMI:v1p630/r29.claim: Al-Qadi says the Prophet, his religion, and his qibla are all true, as the preceding passage had stated.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r29.anchor: النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - حق، ودينه حق، وقبلته حق؛ لأنه مذكور فيما تقدم، عن القاضي

JISHUMI:v1p630/r30.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r30.speaker: اليهود
JISHUMI:v1p630/r30.claim: The Jews reportedly accused Muhammad of inventing the change himself and switching directions; the verse says they knew this accusation was false.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r30.anchor: ما أمرت بها يا محمد، هذا شيء تبتدعه من تلقاء نفسك، مرة إلى ههنا، ومرة إلى ههنا

JISHUMI:v1p630/r31.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r31.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p630/r31.claim: God is not unaware of their concealment, opposition to the Prophet's truth, and attempts to frustrate his mission.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r31.anchor: من كتمان ذلك، ومخالفة حقك، وإبطال أمرك

JISHUMI:v1p630/r32.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p630/r32.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p630/r32.claim: Alternatively, God knows and preserves their deeds to repay them, promising believers and threatening unbelievers.
JISHUMI:v1p630/r32.anchor: يعلم أعمالكم ويحفظها لكم، ليجازيكم بها، وفيه وعد للمؤمنين ووعيد للكافرين

JISHUMI:v1p628/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r1.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
JISHUMI:v1p628/r1.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisai read the verb with second-person tāʾ, addressing Muslims; the others read third-person yāʾ, referring to Jews.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي تعلمون بالتاء على الخطاب للمسلمين، والباقون بالياء على أنه راجع إلى اليهود

JISHUMI:v1p628/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r2.speaker: author
