JISHUMI:v1p628/r2.claim: Ruʾya means perception by sight, as does absara; raʾā-yarā is the verb form cited.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r2.anchor: الرؤية: إدراك الشيء بالبصر، ونظيره أبصره، يقال: رأى يرى رؤية

JISHUMI:v1p628/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r3.claim: Ruʾya is also used to mean knowledge, as in 25:45 and 89:6.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r3.anchor: ثم يستعمل بمعنى العلم، قال الله تعالى (ألم تر إلى ربك كيف مد الظل) و(ألم تر كيف فعل ربك بعاد)

JISHUMI:v1p628/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r4.claim: Taqallub means movement among directions, and is synonymous with taṣarruf and taḥawwul.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r4.anchor: والتقلب: التحريك في الجهات، والتقلب والتصرف والتحول نظائر

JISHUMI:v1p628/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r5.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r5.claim: Riḍā returns to willing: approving an act is like willing it, while being pleased with someone is like willing reward and honor for them; its opposite seeks punishment.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r5.anchor: والرضا يرجع إلى الإرادة، فإذا قيل: رضي عمله، فكأنه أراده، وإذا قيل: رضي عنه

JISHUMI:v1p628/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r6.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r6.claim: Riḍā, love, and willing are near-synonyms, while sukhṭ is its opposite.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r6.anchor: ونقيضه السخط، وهو يرجع إلى أنه يريد عقابه، ورضي وأحب وأراد من النظائر

JISHUMI:v1p628/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r7.claim: Shatr means half, and shatra something can mean toward it.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r7.anchor: والشطر: النصف، ويقال: شطر كذا أي نحوه

JISHUMI:v1p628/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r8.claim: Ḥarām means prohibited or prevented, with the prohibited act varying by context: marriage to a mother, eating food, or using another's property.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r8.anchor: والحرام: المحرم، حرمه تحريما إذا منعه عنه، ثم يختلف باختلاف المواضع

JISHUMI:v1p628/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r9.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p628/r9.claim: One explanation calls the House inviolable because it was protected from destruction, as with the people of the Elephant; another says acts forbidden there are lawful elsewhere.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r9.anchor: سمي البيت الحرام قيل: لأنه ممنوع عن الاصطلام، كما منع من أصحاب الفيل، وقيل: لأنه يحرم فيه ما يحل في غيره

JISHUMI:v1p628/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r10.claim: Ghafla is a lapse that befalls a person: loss of knowledge about something one would ordinarily know.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r10.anchor: والغفلة: سهو يعتري الإنسان، وهو ذهاب العلم بما جرت العادة بعلمه

JISHUMI:v1p628/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r11.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r11.claim: In wa-ḥaythu mā kuntum, mā is jussive by the conditional construction; the fa is needed for the answer because ḥaythu is neither interrogative nor like its sister particles in annexation.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r11.anchor: جزم بالشرط، فإنه قيل: حيث تكونوا، والفاء جواب، ولولاها لم يجز الجواب ب (حيث)

JISHUMI:v1p628/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r12.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r12.claim: Shatrahu is accusative as an adverbial, governed by the command fa-walli.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r12.anchor: و (شطره) نصب على الظرف، والعامل فيه: فول

JISHUMI:v1p628/r13.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r13.speaker: الحسن والسدي وأبو علي
JISHUMI:v1p628/r13.claim: Al-Hasan, al-Suddi, and Abu Ali report that the Prophet had been promised a change without its destination being specified, and looked up expecting the promised qibla revelation.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r13.anchor: وعد التحويل عن بيت المقدس، ولم يبين إلى أي موضع يحوله، فكان يقلب طرفه في السماء

JISHUMI:v1p628/r14.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r14.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
JISHUMI:v1p628/r14.claim: Ibn Abbas and Qatada say he loved the Kaaba naturally but did not pray for it before permission; Gabriel told him to ask God, and he kept looking up until the verse came.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r14.anchor: كان يحب ذلك محبة طباع، ولم يكن يدعو به حتى أذن له فيه، وكان يستأذن جبريل

JISHUMI:v1p628/r15.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r15.speaker: أبو مسلم
JISHUMI:v1p628/r15.claim: Abu Muslim says, absent the reports, one could place the revelation at the Prophet's first arrival in Medina: at Mecca he faced Jerusalem with the Kaaba between, then awaited direction after migration.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r15.anchor: لولا الأخبار لاحتمل أن يكون ذلك أول مقدمه المدينة، فقد روي أنه كان بمكة يصلي

JISHUMI:v1p628/r16.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r16.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p628/r16.claim: One account says that in Mecca he prayed toward the Kaaba, then after migrating was ordered toward Jerusalem.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r16.anchor: فقيل: كان يصلي إلى الكعبة، فلما هاجر أمر بالتوجه إلى بيت المقدس

JISHUMI:v1p628/r17.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r17.speaker: قيل
JISHUMI:v1p628/r17.claim: Another account says that in Mecca he faced Jerusalem while placing the Kaaba between himself and Jerusalem.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r17.anchor: وقيل: بل كان بمكة يصلي إلى بيت المقدس، ويجعل الكعبة بينه وبين بيت المقدس

JISHUMI:v1p628/r18.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r18.speaker: أبو القاسم
JISHUMI:v1p628/r18.claim: A further view, cited by Abu al-Qasim, says he prayed toward Jerusalem in Mecca.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r18.anchor: وقيل: بل كان يصلي إلى بيت المقدس، حكاه أبو القاسم

JISHUMI:v1p628/r19.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r19.speaker: جعفر بن مبشر
JISHUMI:v1p628/r19.claim: Jaʿfar ibn Mubashshir says the Prophet was ordered to face Jerusalem rather than choosing it himself.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r19.anchor: أمر بالتوجه إلى بيت المقدس لا باختياره، والصحيح أنه كان وعد التحويل

JISHUMI:v1p628/r20.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r20.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r20.claim: Jishumi prefers that God promised the change; the Prophet did not follow personal inclination, knowing God's command contains the benefit.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r20.anchor: والصحيح أنه كان وعد التحويل، وكان لا يحب من تلقاء نفسه؛ لأنه يعلم أن المصلحة ما يأمره به ربه

JISHUMI:v1p628/r21.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p628/r21.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p628/r21.claim: The Prophet would only ask with God's permission, lest rejection discourage people or the request seek something harmful; his love and requests were governed by God, as 53:3 says he does not speak from desire.
JISHUMI:v1p628/r21.anchor: وما يسأله يسأله بإذنه، وقد قال تعالى

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r1.claim: “We may see” conveys frequent seeing; a poetic line beginning “قد أترك القرن” illustrates the construction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r1.anchor: ربما نرى ومعناه كثرة الرؤية كقوله

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r2.claim: The Prophet repeatedly turned his face and shifted his gaze toward the sky.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r2.anchor: تردد وجهك وتصرف نظرك في جهة السماء

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r3.claim: He hoped God would turn him toward the Kaaba: Abraham’s qibla, attractive to Arabs through their pride and sanctuary, and different from the Jews’ direction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r3.anchor: وكان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يتوقع من ربه ان يحوله إلى الكعبة لأنها قبلة أبيه إبراهيم وادعى للعرب

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r4.claim: The Prophet watched for Gabriel’s descent and revelation announcing the change of direction.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r4.anchor: فكان يراعى نزول جبريل عليه السلام والوحي بالتحويل

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r5.claim: The phrase means giving and enabling him to face the Kaaba, or setting him facing its direction; the verb can describe appointing someone over something.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r5.anchor: فلنعطينك ولنمكننك من استقبالها من قولك وليته كذا إذا جعلته واليا له

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r6.claim: “You approve” means loving and inclining toward it for sound reasons that accord with God’s will and wisdom.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r6.anchor: تحبها وتميل اليها لأغراضك الصحيحة التي اضمرتها ووافقت مشيئة الله وحكمته

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r7.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r7.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r7.claim: Shatr means toward; a poetic line about driving a people “شطر الملوك” illustrates it.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r7.anchor: نحوه قال ( وأظعن بالقوم شطر الملوك )

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r8.speaker: أبي
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r8.claim: Ubayy reads “toward the Sacred Mosque” using the word “tilqāʾ.”

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r9.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r9.speaker: البراء بن عازب
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r9.claim: Al-Baraʾ ibn ʿAzib reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen months after reaching Medina, then turned toward the Kaaba.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r9.anchor:
وعن البراء بن عازب
67 قدم رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم المدينة فصلى نحو بيت المقدس

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r10.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r10.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r10.claim: Another report dates the change to Rajab, after noon, two months before Badr, during prayer at Banu Salama’s mosque; the Prophet turned mid-prayer and the rows changed places.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r10.anchor:
وقيل
68 كان ذلك في رجب بعد زوال الشمس قبل قتال بدر بشهرين ورسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في مسجد بني سلمة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r11.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r11.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r11.claim: Shatr is an adverbial accusative meaning toward the mosque; facing the exact Kaaba would burden distant worshippers, so the required direction is its general bearing.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p227/r11.anchor: نصب على الظرف أي اجعل تولية الوجه تلقاء المسجد أي في جهته وسمته لأن استقبال عين القبلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r1.claim: The change to the Kaaba is true because the prophets’ glad tidings about the Messenger said he would pray toward both qiblas.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r1.anchor: أن التحويل إلى الكعبة هو الحق لأنه كان في بشارة أنبيائهم برسول الله انه يصلي إلى القبلتين

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p229/r2.claim: The verb “they know” is read with either yāʾ or tāʾ.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r1.claim: This verse was revealed before the following passage about people calling the change foolish, 2:142.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r1.anchor: هذه الآية متقدمة في النزول على قوله تعالى : { سيقول السفهاء من الناس } .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r2.speaker: الطبري
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r2.claim: Al-Tabari takes this as the Prophet turning his face toward the sky.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r2.anchor: معناه : تحول وجهك نحو السماء , وهذا قول الطبري .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r3.speaker: الزجاج
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r3.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes it as the Prophet's eyes repeatedly looking up at the sky.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r3.anchor: والثاني : معناه : تقلب عينيك في النظر إلى السماء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r4.claim: The desired qibla is the Kaaba, which the Prophet liked, chose, and asked God to make his direction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r4.anchor: يعني الكعبة كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يرضاها ويختارها ويسأل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r5.speaker: مجاهد، ابن زيد
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r5.claim: Mujahid and Ibn Zayd say he chose it to differ from the Jews, who objected that he followed their qibla while opposing their religion.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r5.anchor: أحدهما : مخالفة اليهود وكراهة لموافقتهم , لأنهم قالوا : تتبع قبلتنا وتخالفنا في ديننا ؟ وبه قال مجاهد , وابن زيد .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says he chose the Kaaba because it had been the qibla of his forefather Abraham.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r6.anchor: والثاني : أنه اختارها , لأنها كانت قبلة أبيه إبراهيم , وبه قال ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r7.claim: The wording does not mean the Prophet disliked Jerusalem as qibla: prophets must accept God's commands.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r7.anchor: لا يجوز أن يكون رسول الله غير راض ببيت المقدس , لما أمره الله تعالى به , لأن الأنبياء يجب عليهم الرضا بأوامر الله تعالى

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r8.claim: Here tarḍāhā means that the Prophet loved and desired the Kaaba, which could unite his people and make them answer him quickly.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r8.anchor: لكن معنى ترضاها : أي تحبها وتهواها , وإنما أحبها مع ما ذكرنا من القولين الأولين , لما فيها من تآلف قومه وإسراعهم إلى إجابته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r9.claim: Alternatively, the phrase may mean satisfaction with the unity and prompt response resulting from the new qibla.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r9.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون قوله : { ترضاها } محمولا على الحقيقة بمعنى : ترضى ما يحدث عنها من التأليف

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r10.claim: The instruction means to turn one's face in prayer toward the Sacred Mosque.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p201/r10.anchor: أي حول وجهك في الصلاة , شطر المسجد الحرام أي : نحو المسجد الحرام

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r1.claim: The Huthali verse uses shatr to mean toward: the eye looks toward the subject.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r1.anchor: فشطرها نظر العينين محسور أي نحوها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r2.claim: Shatr is an antonym: shatr ila is to approach something, while shatr an is to move away and turn aside.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r3.claim: Shatr can also mean half of a thing.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r4.claim: A shatir is so called because he has turned toward something other than the straight way.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r4.anchor: فأما الشاطر من الرجال فلأنه قد أخذ في نحو غير الاستواء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r5.claim: The Sacred Mosque refers to the Kaaba, which lies within it; the place names what it contains.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r5.anchor: يعني به الكعبة , لأنها فيه فعبر به عنها .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r6.speaker: عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r6.claim: Abd Allah ibn Amr ibn al-As says the commanded direction was directly opposite the Kaaba's Mizab.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r6.anchor: فقال عبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص : { فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها } قال : حيال ميزاب الكعبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r7.speaker: عبد الله بن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r7.claim: Ibn Abbas says the whole House is the direction, and the House's door is its qibla.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r7.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن عباس : البيت كله , وقبلة البيت الباب .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r8.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r8.claim: The second command reaffirms the first, guarding against restriction: one addresses the Prophet, the other all people, though both apply generally to the Prophet and community.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r8.anchor: ثم قال تعالى : { وحيثما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره } يعني نحو المسجد الحرام أيضا تأكيدا للأمر الأول لأن عمومه يقتضيه , لكن أراد بالتأكيد احتمال التخصيص

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r9.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r9.claim: The different addresses prevent changing the commanded direction and keep each command general.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r9.anchor: كلا الأمرين عام في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وجميع أمته , لكن غاير بين الأمرين ليمنع من تغيير الأمر في المأمور به , وليكون كل واحد منهما جاريا على عمومه .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r10.claim: Those given the Book are the Jews and Christians.

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r11.claim: What they know to be true from their Lord is the change of qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r11.anchor: يعني تحويل القبلة عن بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة .

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r12.claim: Their conduct is their arguing in an attempt to turn Muslims away from their religion over this change.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p203/r12.anchor: من الخوض في إفتان المسلمين عن دينهم بذلك .

MUJAHID:v1p91/r1.author: Mujāhid b. Jabr
MUJAHID:v1p91/r1.speaker: مجاهد
MUJAHID:v1p91/r1.claim: Mujahid glosses shatrahu as toward it.
MUJAHID:v1p91/r1.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح عن مجاهد في قوله ﴿ شطره ﴾ يعني نحوه

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r1.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r1.claim: God sees Muhammad gazing toward heaven and promises to turn him toward his desired qibla because the Kaʿba was dearer to him than Jerusalem.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r1.anchor: يعنى نرى أنك تديم نظرك إلى السماء

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r2.claim: “Turn” means change direction, and shatr means toward; worshippers are to face the Kaʿba in prayer.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r2.anchor: فول } ، يعنى فحول { وجهك شطر } ، يعني تلقاء

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r3.claim: The command applies to all worshippers: turn toward the Kaʿba in prayer wherever on earth they may be.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r3.anchor: يعنى فحولوا وجوهكم فى الصلاة تلقاءه

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r4.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r4.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r4.claim: At Banu Salima’s mosque Muhammad had prayed one rakʿa when the qibla changed to the Kaʿba; fasting Ramadan, the qibla change, and prayer toward the Kaʿba were prescribed two months before Badr, and wine was forbidden before the Trench.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r4.anchor: كان النبى صلى الله عليه وسلم يصلى فى مسجد بنى سلمة، فصلى ركعة

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r5.claim: The People of the Torah are Jews; al-Khamis ibn ʿAmr protested that the Kaʿba command was invented, prompting the reply that they know it is true.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r5.anchor: وهم اليهود، منهم الحميس بن عمرو، قال: يا محمد

MUQATIL:2:144-145/r6.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r6.speaker: author
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r6.claim: The Jews know that the Kaʿba is the true qibla from their Lord; their disbelief concerning the qibla is not hidden from God.
MUQATIL:2:144-145/r6.anchor: بأن القبلة هى الكعبة، فأوعدهم الله، فقال

BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r1.claim: The Prophet faced the Kaaba in Mecca; after migration God directed him toward Jerusalem for Jewish acceptance. He prayed that way for sixteen months while expecting a return to Abraham's qibla.
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r1.anchor: كان يصلي بمكة مع أصحابه إلى الكعبة فلما هاجر إلى المدينة أمره الله أن يصلي نحو بيت المقدس

BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r2.claim: At the Mosque of Banū Salama, the command came during noon prayer after two rakʿas; the congregation turned, giving the mosque its name, Mosque of the Two Qiblas.
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r2.anchor: وذلك في مسجد بني سلمة فصلى الظهر ولما صلى الركعتين

BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r3.claim: Opposition to the change became a divine test, separating those who follow the Messenger from those who turn back, as 2:143 says.
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r3.anchor: فلما تحولت القبلة أنكر من أنكر فكان هذا ابتلاء من الله تعالى

BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r4.claim: A first veiled group viewed the shift from the Kaaba to Jerusalem as an ascent from the heart's unveiling to the spirit's witnessing station; they feared the return meant descent and loss of rank.
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r4.anchor: التحويلة من الكعبة إلى بيت المقدس كانت صورة العروج من مقام المكاشفة أعني مقام القلب إلى مقام المشاهدة أعني مقام الروح

BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r5.claim: Bursevī corrects that reading: the return images a perfected return to the heart's station for calling others, seeing unity within multiplicity and detail within unity, without being veiled by either.
BURSEVI:v1p168#2/r5.anchor: لم يعلموا أنه صورة الرجوع إلى مقام القلب حالة التمكين للدعوة ومشاهدة الجمع في عين التفصيل

BURSEVI:v1p201/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r1.claim: Although قد with a present verb usually suggests rarity, here it is used by antithetical metaphor to suggest abundance.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r1.anchor: لفظ قد في المضارع للتقليل وقد استعمل ههنا للتكثير بطريق الاستعارة للمجانسة بين الضدين

BURSEVI:v1p201/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r2.claim: نرى is formally present but carries past meaning, ‘We saw and knew’; the verse comes later in recitation but earlier in the narrative because it opens the story.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r2.anchor: مستقبل لفظا ماض معنى ومتأخر تلاوة متقدم معنى

BURSEVI:v1p201/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r3.claim: The Prophet repeatedly turned his gaze toward the sky, awaiting revelation and expecting God to redirect him toward the Kaaba.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r3.anchor: أي : تردد وجهك في تصرف نظرك

BURSEVI:v1p201/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r4.claim: He longed for the Kaaba as Abraham's qibla and the older qibla, and because it could draw Arabs toward faith through its prestige as sanctuary, pilgrimage site, and place of security.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r4.anchor: لأنها قبلة أبيه إبراهيم وأقدم القبلتين وأدعى للعرب إلى الإيمان من حيث أنها كانت مفخرة لهم وأمنا ومزارا ومطافا

BURSEVI:v1p201/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r5.claim: The Prophet also disliked following the Jewish qibla because Jews taunted that he followed their religion's direction and would not know where to face without them.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r5.anchor: فإنهم كانوا يقولون : إنه يخالفنا في ديننا

BURSEVI:v1p201/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r6.claim: A report says the Prophet told Gabriel he wished God would turn him from the Jews' qibla; Gabriel replied that he too was God's servant and urged him to pray to his Lord.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r6.anchor: حتى روي أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم قال لجبريل

BURSEVI:v1p201/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r7.claim: The Prophet kept looking up in hope of Gabriel's answer, and God revealed this verse in response.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r7.anchor: وجعل رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يديم النظر إلى السماء رجاء أن يأتيه جبريل بالذي سأل ربه فأنزل الله هذه الآية

BURSEVI:v1p201/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201/r8.claim: Bursevī says the first abrogation was reducing fifty prayers to five; the qibla first shifted to Jerusalem in Mecca to test polytheists, then to the Kaaba in Medina to test Jews, citing al-Fanārī's Fātiḥa commentary.
BURSEVI:v1p201/r8.anchor: نسخت إلى خمس للتخفف ثم تحويل القبلة إلى بيت المقدس بمكة امتحانا للمشركين

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r1.claim: The phrase may mean ‘We will surely give it to you and enable you to face it,’ from making someone a wali or granting him authority; alternatively, ‘make you face its direction,’ from nearness.

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r2.claim: ‘That you are pleased with’ figuratively expresses love and longing; the Prophet sought it for religious purposes aligned with God's will, not natural appetite.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r2.anchor: مجاز عن المحبة والاشتياق لأنه عليه السلام لم يكن ساخطا للتوجه إلى بيت المقدس كارها له

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r3.claim: ‘Face’ here means the whole body, since a worshipper must turn the whole body toward the qibla; the face is named as the leading organ of orientation.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r3.anchor: والمراد بالوجه ههنا جملة البدن لأن الواجب على المكلف أن يستقبل القبلة بجملة بدنه لا بوجهه فقط

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r4.claim: The command means to turn the face so it points toward the direction of the sanctuary.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r4.anchor: أي : اجعل وجهك بحيث يلي شطره

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r5.claim: The apparent referent is the great mosque containing the Kaaba; ḥarām can mean that fighting there is forbidden or that wrongdoers are barred from violating it.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r5.anchor: والمتبادر من لفظ المسجد الحرام هو المسجد الأكبر

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r6.claim: The Hanafis and Shafiʿis agree that distant worshippers need only face the Kaaba's direction: aiming at its exact site is inaccessible from afar and would impose hardship.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r6.anchor: وفي ذكر المسجد الحرام دون الكعبة إيذان بكفاية مراعاة جهة الكعبة باتفاق بين الحنفية والشافعية

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r7.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r7.claim: Wherever believers are on land or sea, east or west, they must face the sanctuary when praying; the command explicitly extends the Prophet's instruction to the whole community.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r7.anchor: في أي : موضع كنتم من الأرض من بحر أو بر

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r8.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r8.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r8.claim: The command addresses all believers, present and absent, and urges the community to follow the Prophet.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r8.anchor: أمر لجميع المؤمنين بذلك بعدما أمر به النبي عليه السلام تصريحا بعمومه لكافة العباد

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r9.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r9.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r9.claim: Jews and Christians know the change to the Kaaba is true because their scriptures foretell that the Prophet will pray toward both qiblas; it comes from God, not the Prophet's invention.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r9.anchor: لما أن المسطور في كتبهم أنه عليه السلام يصلي إلى القبلتين بتحويل القبلة إلى الكعبة

BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r10.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r10.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r10.claim: The closing address collectively includes Muslims and Jews: it promises Muslims reward and warns Jews over their obstinacy.
BURSEVI:v1p201#2/r10.anchor: خطاب للمسلمين واليهود جميعا على التغليب فيكون وعدا للمسلمين بالإثابة وجزيل الجزاء ووعيدا وتهديدا لليهود على عنادهم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.claim: The Prophet repeatedly turned his face and shifted his gaze toward the sky.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r1.anchor: تردد وجهك وتصرف نظرك فى جهة السماء

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.claim: The Prophet expected to be turned toward the Kaʿba, to follow Abraham, distinguish himself from the Jews, and attract Arabs to faith because the sanctuary was their pride and pilgrimage center.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r2.anchor: يتوقع من ربه أن يحوله إلى الكعبة موافقة لإبراهيم

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.claim: Nu walliyannaka may mean ‘give and enable you to face it,’ or ‘make you turn toward its direction rather than Jerusalem.’
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r3.anchor: فلنعطينك ولنمكننك من استقبالها من قولك وليته كذا

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.claim: The desired qibla is one the Prophet loves and inclines toward for sound purposes that accord with God’s will and wisdom.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r4.anchor: تحبها وتميل اليها لأغراضك الصحيحة التى أضمرتها ووافقت مشيئة الله وحكمته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.claim: Shatr means toward; it is an adverbial accusative, directing the face toward the mosque’s direction, since exact alignment is difficult for someone far away.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r5.anchor: أى نحوه وشطر نصب على الظرف أى اجعل تولية الوجه تلقاء المسجد أى فى جهته وسمته

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.claim: Mentioning the Sacred Mosque rather than the Kaʿba indicates that distant worshippers must face its general direction, not its exact physical point.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r6.anchor: وذكر المسجد الحرام دون الكعبة دليل على أن الواجب مراعاة الجهة دون العين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.claim: A report says the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for ten months after arriving in Medina, then was turned toward the Kaʿba; no authority or grading is given.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r7.anchor: روى أنه عليه السلام قدم المدينة فصلى نحو بيت المقدس سنة عشر شهرا ثم وجه إلى الكعبة

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.claim: Wherever on earth people are, when they intend to pray they must face the Sacred Mosque’s direction.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r8.anchor: من الأرض وأردتم الصلاة ﴿ فولوا وجوهكم شطره

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.claim: People of the Book know the turn toward the Kaʿba is true because their prophets’ glad tidings said the Messenger would pray toward both qiblas.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r9.anchor: أى التحويل إلى الكعبة هو الحق لأنه كان فى بشارة انبيائهم برسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنه يصلى إلى القبلتين

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.speaker: مكي
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r10.claim: The phrase is read with yāʾ by the Meccan reader, Abū ʿAmr, Nāfiʿ, and ʿĀṣim; others read it with tāʾ.

NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r11.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r11.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r11.claim: The yāʾ reading threatens unbelievers with punishment for rejection, while the tāʾ reading promises believers reward for acceptance and performance.
NASAFI-FULL:v1p76#2/r11.anchor: وعد للمؤمنين بالثواب على القبول والأداء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r1.claim: The scholars say this verse was revealed before 2:142, although it appears after it in the sūra.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r1.anchor: قال العلماء: هذه الآية مقدمة في النزول على قوله تعالى: سيقول السفهآء من الناس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r2.speaker: الطبري
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r2.claim: Al-Ṭabarī explains the Prophet's turning his face as turning it toward the sky; al-Zajjāj says he turned his eyes to gaze upward, a similar sense.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r2.anchor: تحول وجهك إلى السماء قاله الطبري. الزجاج: تقلب عينيك في النظر إلى السماء

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r3.claim: The sky is singled out because things associated with it are held in special reverence and come from it, such as rain, mercy, and revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r3.anchor: وخص السماء بالذكر إذ هي مختصة بتعظيم ما أضيف إليها ويعود منها كالمطر والرحمة والوحي

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r4.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r4.claim: Tarḍāhā means that you love or desire it.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r5.speaker: السدي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r5.claim: Al-Suddī says that while praying toward Jerusalem, the Prophet raised his head toward the sky awaiting an instruction because he wished to pray toward the Kaʿba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r5.anchor: قال السدي: كان إذا صلى نحو بيت المقدس رفع رأسه إلى السماء ينظر ما يؤمر به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r6.speaker: البراء
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r6.claim: Al-Barāʾ reports that the Prophet prayed toward Jerusalem for sixteen or seventeen months and wished to face the Kaʿba before this revelation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r6.anchor: وروى أبو إسحق عن البراء قال: كان رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم صلى نحو بيت المقدس ستة عشر شهرا أو سبعة عشر شهرا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r7.claim: The command to turn one's face toward the Sacred Mosque means toward the Kaʿba, with no disagreement on that point.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r7.anchor: يعني الكعبة، ولا خلاف في هذا

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r8.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the direction is aligned with the whole House; Ibn ʿUmar says it is aligned with the Kaʿba's rainspout, as reported by Ibn ʿAṭiyya.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r8.anchor: قيل: حيال البيت كله عن ابن عباس. وقال ابن عمر: حيال الميزاب من الكعبة قاله ابن عطية

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r9.claim: A report from Ibn ʿAbbās through ʿAṭāʾ says the Kaʿba is the direction for the mosque, the mosque for the sanctuary, and the sanctuary for people across the earth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r9.anchor: روى ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r10.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r10.claim: Shatr means direction or side here and functions as a locative adverb, like toward or opposite; it is accusative as an adjunct where the action occurs.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r10.anchor: الشطر له محامل: يكون الناحية والجهة، كما في هذه الآية، وهو ظرف مكان

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r11.speaker: داود بن أبي هند
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r11.claim: Dāwūd ibn Abī Hind says Ibn Masʿūd's codex read تلقاء المسجد الحرام in place of شطر المسجد الحرام.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144/r11.anchor: وقال داود بن أبي هند: إن في حرف ابن مسعود «فول وجهك تلقاء المسجد الحرام»

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r1.claim: The cited anonymous poetic lines use shatr for a direction or destination, including toward Banū Tamīm and toward a fortress; another says a message sent toward ʿAmr does not suffice.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r1.anchor:
أقول لأم زنباع أقيمي
صدور العيش شطر بني تميم

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r2.claim: Shatr also means half, as in the prophetic saying that purification is half of faith.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r2.anchor:
وشطر الشيء: نصفه ومنه الحديث:
" الطهور شطر الإيمان "

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r3.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r3.claim: The verb shatara can mean to approach in one construction and turn away in another; shāṭir is named for departing from the straight way, with a reported gloss of distancing oneself from God's prohibitions.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r3.anchor: ويكون من الأضداد، يقال: شطر إلى كذا إذا أقبل نحوه، وشطر عن كذا إذا أبعد منه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r4.speaker: أبو عمر
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r4.claim: Scholars agree that the Kaʿba is the qibla in every region; anyone who sees it and knows its direction must face it, and prayer performed while knowingly facing away must be repeated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#2/r4.anchor: لا خلاف بين العلماء أن الكعبة قبلة في كل أفق، وأجمعوا على أن من شاهدها وعاينها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r1.claim: Scholars agree that anyone away from the Kaaba must face its direction, side, or bearing.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r1.anchor: وأجمعوا على أن كل من غاب عنها أن يستقبل ناحيتها وشطرها وتلقاءها

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r2.claim: When the direction is uncertain, a worshipper should infer it from available signs, including stars, winds, and mountains.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r2.anchor: فعليه أن يستدل على ذلك بكل ما يمكنه من النجوم والرياح والجبال

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r3.speaker: عطاء ومجاهد
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r3.claim: A person praying in the Sacred Mosque should face and look at the Kaaba; looking at it is reported to be worship.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r3.anchor: فإنه يروى أن النظر إلى الكعبة عبادة قاله عطاء ومجاهد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r4.speaker: بعضهم
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r4.claim: Some jurists held that an absent worshipper must face the Kaaba itself rather than only its direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r4.anchor: واختلفوا هل فرض الغائب استقبال العين أو الجهة فمنهم من قال بالأول

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r5.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r5.claim: Ibn al-Arabi rejects requiring the Kaaba itself as an impracticable obligation.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r5.anchor: قال ابن العربي: وهو ضعيف لأنه تكليف لما لا يصل إليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r6.claim: Facing the direction is correct because it is feasible, commanded by the verse, and confirmed by prayer rows much wider than the Kaaba.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r6.anchor: ومنهم من قال بالجهة وهو الصحيح لثلاثة أوجه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r7.claim: The verse commands people everywhere, east or west, to face the Kaaba's direction.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r7.anchor: أنه المأمور به في القرآن لقوله تعالى: { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r8.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r8.claim: The long prayer row, certainly many times wider than the Kaaba, supports facing its direction rather than the exact structure.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r8.anchor: أن العلماء احتجوا بالصف الطويل الذي يعلم قطعا أنه أضعاف عرض البيت

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r9.speaker: مالك
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r9.claim: Malik and those agreeing with him use this verse to support looking straight ahead while praying, rather than at the place of prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r9.anchor: في هذه الآية حجة واضحة لما ذهب إليه مالك ومن وافقه في أن المصلي حكمه أن ينظر أمامه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r10.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r10.speaker: الثوري وأبو حنيفة والشافعي والحسن بن حي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r10.claim: Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, al-Shafi'i, and al-Hasan ibn Hayy recommend looking at the place of prostration.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r10.anchor: وقال الثوري وأبو حنيفة والشافعي والحسن بن حي: يستحب أن يكون نظره

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r11.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r11.speaker: شريك القاضي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r11.claim: Sharik al-Qadi assigns different gaze points by posture: prostration while standing, feet in bowing, nose in prostration, and lap when seated.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r11.anchor: وقال شريك القاضي: ينظر في القيام إلى موضع السجود، وفي الركوع إلى موضع قدميه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r12.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r12.speaker: ابن العربي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r12.claim: Ibn al-Arabi says to look ahead: lowering the head diminishes required upright posture, while holding it up and straining the eyes downward is hardship; looking down is better for one able.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r12.anchor: قال ابن العربي: إنما ينظر أمامه فإنه إن حنى رأسه ذهب بعض القيام المفترض عليه

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r13.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r13.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r13.claim: Those given the Book here are Jews and Christians.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r13.anchor: قوله تعالى: { وإن الذين أوتوا الكتاب } يريد اليهود والنصارى

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r14.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r14.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r14.claim: What they know to be true is the change of the qibla from Jerusalem.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r14.anchor: يعني تحويل القبلة من بيت المقدس

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r15.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r15.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r15.claim: One explanation is that scripture taught them Muhammad was a prophet, so they knew he spoke and commanded only truth.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r15.anchor: أنهم لما علموا من كتابهم أن محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم نبي علموا أنه لا يقول إلا الحق ولا يأمر إلا به

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r16.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r16.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r16.claim: A second explanation is that they knew abrogation was permissible in their religion, even though some denied it, and thus knew the new qibla was valid.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r16.anchor: أنهم علموا من دينهم جواز النسخ وإن جحده بعضهم فصاروا عالمين بجواز القبلة

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r17.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r17.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r17.claim: God does not neglect people's deeds; the statement also carries a threat.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r17.anchor: وعلى الوجهين فهو إعلام بأن الله تعالى لا يهمل أعمال العباد ولا يغفل عنها، وضمنه الوعيد.

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r18.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r18.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r18.claim: Ibn Amir, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read with second-person ta, addressing either the People of the Book or Muhammad's community.
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r18.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي «تعملون» بالتاء على مخاطبة أهل الكتاب أو أمة محمد

QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r19.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r19.speaker: الباقون
QURTUBI-FULL:2:144#3/r19.claim: The other readers use the third-person ya reading.

RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r1.speaker: أكثر المفسرين
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r1.claim: The well-known view of most exegetes is that the Prophet looked toward heaven while awaiting transfer of the qibla from Jerusalem to the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r1.anchor: القول الأول : وهو المشهور الذي عليه أكثر المفسرين أن ذلك كان لانتظار تحويله من بيت المقدس إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports that the Prophet wished to be turned away from the Jews’ qibla, and Gabriel told him to ask God; he then watched for Gabriel’s answer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r2.anchor: روى عن ابن عباس أنه قال : ( يا جبريل وددت أن الله تعالى صرفني عن قبلة اليهود إلى غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r3.speaker: القائلون بهذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r3.claim: Proponents explain the wish by the Jews’ taunts, Abraham’s qibla, hope of attracting Arabs to Islam, and honor of the Prophet’s hometown mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r3.anchor: والقائلون بهذا القول ذكروا وجوها . أحدها : أنه كان يكره التوجه إلى بيت المقدس ، ويحب التوجه إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r4.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r4.claim: Al-Qadi objects that it is unfitting for a Prophet to dislike a qibla God commanded or want a change from natural desire, since he knows righteousness may oppose inclination.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r4.anchor: واعترض القاضي على هذا الوجه وقال : أنه لا يليق به عليه السلام أن يكره قبلة أمر أن يصلي إليها

RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r5.claim: Al-Razi says the objection is unpersuasive: blame lies in disobeying God, not privately hoping for permission to face a naturally preferred direction, especially without saying so.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100/r5.anchor: واعلم أن هذا التأويل قليل التحصيل ، لأن المستنكر من الرسول أن يعرض عما أمره الله تعالى به

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r1.speaker: قائلون بهذا الوجه
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r1.claim: Another explanation is that the Prophet asked Gabriel permission to pray for a change; prophets seek permission to avoid asking for what lacks benefit and risking an unanswered prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r1.anchor: أنه عليه السلام قد استأذن جبريل عليه السلام في أن يدعو الله تعالى بذلك فأخبره جبريل بأن الله قد أذن له في هذا الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r2.speaker: الحسن
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r2.claim: Al-Hasan says Gabriel told the Prophet that the qibla would change but did not name the destination; the Prophet’s favorite was the Kaaba, so he watched heaven awaiting revelation.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r2.anchor: قال الحسن : إن جبريل عليه السلام أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم يخبره أن الله تعالى سيحول القبلة عن بيت المقدس

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r3.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r3.claim: Al-Asamm’s version says the Prophet had been forbidden to face Jerusalem without another direction specified, so he feared prayer time would arrive before the qibla appeared.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r3.anchor: فكان يخاف أن يرد وقت الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r4.speaker: قائلون بهذا الوجه
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r4.claim: Another version says Jerusalem remained valid pending the promised change; the Prophet awaited the Kaaba for its religious benefits, including attracting Arabs and distinguishing believers from Jews and hypocrites.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r4.anchor: بل وعد بذلك وقبلة بيت المقدس باقية بحيث تجوز الصلاة إليها

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r5.claim: Al-Razi prefers the version in which Jerusalem remained valid: otherwise the Kaaba would be a new direction, not an abrogation, contrary to exegetes’ consensus that it abrogated the first qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r5.anchor: وهذا الوجه أولى ، وإلا لما كانت القبلة الثانية ناسخة للأولى ، بل كانت مبتدأة ، والمفسرة أجمعوا على أنها ناسخة للأولى

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r6.claim: Al-Razi adds that God would not command prayer without first clarifying where to turn.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r6.anchor: ولأنه لا يجوز أن يؤمر بالصلاة إلا مع بيان موضع التوجه

RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r7.speaker: قائلون بهذا الوجه
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r7.claim: A fourth explanation is that the Prophet’s turning his face toward heaven itself meant that he was praying.
RAZI-FULL:v4p100#2/r7.anchor: الرابع : أن تقلب وجهه في السماء هو الدعاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r1.speaker: أبو مسلم الأصفهاني
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r1.claim: Abu Muslim al-Isfahani says the wording can support another view: the Prophet looked heavenward at the beginning of the Madinan period; in Mecca he faced the Kaaba with Jerusalem behind it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r1.anchor: القول الثاني : وهو قول أبي مسلم الأصفهاني ، قالوا : لولا الأخبار التي دلت على هذا القول وإلا فلفظ الآية يحتمل وجها آخر

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r2.speaker: قائلون بهذا القول
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r2.claim: On this view, after the Hijra the Prophet did not know which way to face and waited for God’s instruction until the command to face the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r2.anchor: فلما هاجر لم يعلم أين يتوجه فانتظر أمر الله تعالى حتى نزل قوله : { فول وجهك شطر المسجد الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r3.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r3.claim: One group says the Prophet faced the Kaaba in Mecca, then was commanded to face Jerusalem for seventeen months in Medina.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r3.anchor: فقال قوم : كان بمكة يصلي إلى الكعبة فلما صار إلى المدينة أمر بالتوجه إلى بيت المقدس سبعة عشر شهرا

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r4.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r4.claim: A second group says that in Mecca he faced Jerusalem while placing the Kaaba between himself and it; in Medina he first faced Jerusalem for seventeen months.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r4.anchor: وقال قوم : بل كان بمكة يصلي إلى بيت المقدس ، إلا أنه يجعل الكعبة بينه وبينها

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r5.speaker: قوم
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r5.claim: A third group says he faced Jerusalem alone in Mecca and for the first seventeen months in Medina, then was directed to the Kaaba for its benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r5.anchor: وقال قوم : بل كان يصلي إلى بيت المقدس فقط وبالمدينة أولا سبعة عشر شهرا ، ثم أمره الله تعالى بالتوجه إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r6.speaker: الربيع بن أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r6.claim: Al-Rabiʿ ibn Anas says the Prophet had a choice in facing Jerusalem.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r6.anchor: فقال الربيع بن أنس : قد كان مخيرا في ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r7.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says facing Jerusalem was an established obligation, not an option.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r7.anchor: وقال ابن عباس : كان التوجه إليه فرضا محققا بلا تخيير

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r8.claim: Whichever account is accepted, al-Razi says the earlier qibla was subsequently abrogated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r8.anchor: واعلم أنه على أي الوجهين كان قد صار منسوخا

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r9.speaker: قائلون بالقول الأول
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r9.claim: Those who say the Prophet was free to choose cite 2:115, “To God belong the East and the West,” as allowing prayer in whichever direction one turns.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r9.anchor: أما القرآن فقوله تعالى : { ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا فثم وجه الله }

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r10.speaker: أبو بكر الرازي
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r10.claim: Abu Bakr al-Razi reports that before the Hijra al-Baraʾ ibn Maʿrur prayed toward the Kaaba en route to Mecca while others insisted on Jerusalem; the Prophet later said Jerusalem would have sufficed, suggesting choice.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r10.anchor: فما روى أبو بكر الرازي في كتاب ( أحكام القرآن ) : أن نفرا قصدوا الرسول عليه الصلاة والسلام من المدينة إلى مكة للبيعة قبل الهجرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r11.speaker: قائلون بالقول الثاني
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r11.claim: Those denying a choice argue that God promised a qibla pleasing to the Prophet; if he could choose Jerusalem or the Kaaba, he would not have faced the qibla he disliked.
RAZI-FULL:v4p101/r11.anchor: واحتج الذاهبون إلى القول الثاني بأنه تعالى قال : { فلنولينك قبلة ترضاها } فدل على أنه عليه السلام ما كان يرتضي القبلة الأولى

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r1.speaker: المشهور
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r1.claim: The common view is that the command to face Jerusalem was abrogated by the command to face the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r1.anchor: المشهور أن التوجه إلى بيت المقدس إنما صار منسوخا بالأمر بالتوجه إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r2.speaker: بعض الناس
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r2.claim: Some hold that 2:115 first abrogated facing Jerusalem and 2:144 later abrogated the all-directions permission in 2:115.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r2.anchor: ومن الناس من قال : التوجه إلى بيت المقدس صار منسوخا بقوله تعالى : { ولله المشرق والمغرب فأينما تولوا

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r3.claim: The Quran's sequence supports direct abrogation of the Jerusalem direction by 2:144; placing 2:142 before it in the text means 2:142 would be later in revelation, against the usual order.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r3.anchor: وهذا الترتيب يقتضي صحة المذهب الذي قلناه بأن التوجه إلى بيت المقدس صار منسوخا بقوله : { فول وجهك

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the command concerning the qibla was the first Quranic matter abrogated; al-Razi gives no grading for the report.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r4.anchor: فما روي عن ابن عباس أمر القبلة أول ما نسخ من القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r5.claim: Because facing Jerusalem is not stated in the Quran, whereas 2:115 is, al-Razi concludes that 2:144 abrogates 2:115 rather than an unstated command to face Jerusalem.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r5.anchor: والأمر بالتوجه إلى بيت المقدس غير مذكور في القرآن ، إنما المذكور في القرآن : { ولله المشرق والمغرب

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r6.claim: The verb can mean granting and enabling the Prophet to face the Kaaba, or making him face its direction instead of Jerusalem.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r6.anchor: فلنعطينك ولنمكننك من استقبالها من قولك وليته كذا

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r7.claim: One interpretation is that the Prophet loved and naturally inclined toward the Kaaba, which was dearer to him than other directions.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r7.anchor: ترضاها تحبها وتميل إليها ، لأن الكعبة / كانت أحب إليه من غيرها

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r8.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r8.claim: Al-Qadi rejects natural inclination as the meaning, arguing that basing a divine command on the Prophet's temperament would impugn divine wisdom in imposing duties and the Prophet's state in obeying them.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r8.anchor: قال القاضي : هذا لا يجوز فإنه من المحال أن يقول الله تعالى : فلنولينك قبلة يميل طبعك إليها

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r9.claim: Al-Razi says al-Qadi's objection fails: the objection applies only if inclination alone caused the change, whereas wisdom and benefit may accord with the Prophet's natural preference.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r9.anchor: وهذا الاعتراض ضعيف لأن الطعن إنما يتوجه لو قال الله تعالى : أنا حولناك إلى القبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r10.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r10.claim: Al-Razi cites the Prophet's saying that prayer was made the delight of his eyes as an example of natural inclination coinciding with religious benefit; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r10.anchor: وقال عليه الصلاة والسلام : ( وجعلت قرة عيني في الصلاة ) فكان طبعه يميل إلى الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r11.claim: A second interpretation is that the Prophet approves of the qibla because it encompasses religious benefits.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r11.anchor: { قبلة ترضاها } أي تحبها بسبب اشتمالها على المصالح الدينية

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r12.speaker: الأصم
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r12.claim: Al-Asamm reads this as meaning that any direction God appoints is acceptable and must not be resented, unlike Arabs who reverted after the qibla changed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r12.anchor: قال الأصم : أي كل جهة وجهك الله إليها فهي لك رضا لا يجوز أن تسخط

RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r13.claim: A fourth interpretation takes approval as approval of the outcome: the change distinguishes sincere followers of Islam from those seeking worldly gain or money.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102/r13.anchor: أي ترضى عاقبتها لأنك تعرف بها من يتبعك للإسلام

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r1.claim: Here face means the person's whole body, since prayer requires facing the qibla with the whole person; the honored, distinguishing face can stand for the whole self.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r1.anchor: المراد من الوجه ههنا جملة بدن الإنسان لأن الواجب على الإنسان أن يستقبل القبلة بجملته لا بوجهه فقط

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r2.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r2.claim: Linguists describe shatr as a shared word meaning either half or toward/in the direction of something.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r2.anchor: قال أهل اللغة : الشطر اسم مشترك يقع على معنيين . أحدهما : النصف

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r3.speaker: أهل اللغة
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r3.claim: The second lexical sense of shatr is toward, facing, or in the direction of something.

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r4.speaker: خقاف بن ندبة
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r4.claim: Al-Shafi'i cites Khiffaf ibn Nudba's line as evidence that shatr means toward Amr.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r4.anchor: قال خقاف بن ندبة : ألا من مبلغ عمرا رسولا … وما تغني الرسالة شطر عمرو

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r5.speaker: ساعدة بن جؤبة
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r5.claim: Al-Shafi'i cites Sa'ida ibn Ju'ba's instruction to turn the camels toward Banu Tamim as evidence for the directional sense.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r5.anchor: وقال ساعدة بن جؤبة : أقول لأم زنباع : أقيمي … صدور العيس شطر بني تميم

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r6.speaker: لقيط الأيادي
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r6.claim: Al-Shafi'i cites Laqit al-Ayadi's line using shatr for a direction toward the people addressed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r6.anchor: وقال لقيط الأيادي : وقد أظلكم من شطر شعركم … هول له ظلم يغشاكم قطعا

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r7.speaker: آخر
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r7.claim: A fourth poet's line uses shatr directionally; al-Shafi'i explains it as toward her, with the eyes' sight directed that way.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r7.anchor: وقال آخر : إن العسير بها داء مخامرها … فشطرها بصر العينين مسحور قال الشافعي رضي الله عنه : يريد تلقاءها

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r8.speaker: جمهور المفسرين والشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r8.claim: The majority of early and later commentators, and al-Shafi'i in al-Risala, understand shatr as the direction, facing, or side of the Sacred Mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r8.anchor: الأول : وهو قول جمهور المفسرين من الصحابة والتابعين والمتأخرين ، واختيار الشافعي رضي الله عنه

RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r9.speaker: أبي بن كعب
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r9.claim: Ubayy ibn Ka'b's reading has تلقاء المسجد الحرام (“toward the Sacred Mosque”) in place of shatr, supporting the directional interpretation.
RAZI-FULL:v4p102#2/r9.anchor: قرأ أبي بن كعب / تلقاء المسجد الحرام

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r1.speaker: الجبائي والقاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r1.claim: Al-Jubba'i and al-Qadi take shatr as the middle or midpoint of the mosque, where the Kaaba lies, so the command specifies the Kaaba's location.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r1.anchor: وهو قول الجبائي واختيار القاضي أن المراد من الشطر ههنا : وسط المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r2.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r2.claim: Al-Qadi argues that a worshipper outside the mosque who faces the mosque but not its midpoint, where the Kaaba is, has not fulfilled the requirement.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r2.anchor: قال القاضي : ويدل على أن المراد ما ذكرنا وجهان . الأول : أن المصلي خارج المسجد

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r3.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r3.claim: Al-Qadi says the midpoint reading gives shatr added force: saying only “the mosque” would not specify its midpoint, the Kaaba's location.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r3.anchor: الثاني : أنا لو فسرنا الشطر بالجانب لم يبق لذكر الشطر مزيد فائدة

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r4.claim: An objection says the side reading usefully accommodates distant worshippers; al-Razi replies that the following “wherever you are” clause already supplies that breadth.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r4.anchor: قلنا : هذه الفائدة مستفادة من قوله : { ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره }

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r5.claim: Al-Razi objects that a literal “half the mosque” is an implausible duty; the argument works only if shatr means the central place, which the wording itself does not establish.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r5.anchor: وفيه إشكال لأنه يصير التقدير فول وجهك نصف المسجد وهذا بعيد

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited in Sharh al-Sunna, says the Kaaba is qibla for mosque-goers, the mosque for people of the Haram, and the Haram for those east and west; Malik holds this view.

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r7.speaker: أسامة بن زيد
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r7.claim: A report in both Sahih collections says the Prophet entered the Kaaba, prayed in its corners without performing prayer there, then prayed two rakas outside facing it and said, “This is the qibla.”
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r7.anchor: عن ابن جريج عن عطاء عن ابن عباس ، قال : أخبرني أسامة بن زيد

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r8.speaker: البراء بن عازب
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r8.claim: Al-Qaffal cites al-Bara ibn Azib's report that the qibla was then turned to the Kaaba and the Prophet had wanted to face it; no grading is stated here.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r8.anchor: وفي خبر البراء بن عازب : ثم صرف إلى الكعبة وكان يحب أن يتوجه إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r9.speaker: ابن عمر
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r9.claim: Al-Qaffal cites Ibn Umar's report about Quba: a visitor told worshippers during prayer that the Messenger had changed the qibla to the Kaaba; no grading is given.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r9.anchor: وفي خبر ابن عمر في صلاة أهل قباء : فأتاهم آت فقال : إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم حول

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r10.speaker: ثمامة بن عبد الله بن أنس
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r10.claim: Al-Qaffal cites Thumama ibn Abd Allah ibn Anas's report that the Prophet's caller announced the qibla had been changed to the Kaaba; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r10.anchor: وفي رواية ثمامة بن عبد الله بن أنس : جاء منادي رسول الله فنادى : أن القبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r11.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r11.claim: Another view takes the wording at face value: the qibla is the entire Sacred Mosque unless an impediment requires another reading.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r11.anchor: وقال آخرون : بل المراد المسجد الحرام كله ، قالوا : لأن الكلام يجب إجراؤه على ظاهر لفظه

RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r12.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r12.claim: Another view takes the Sacred Mosque to mean the entire Haram; 17:1 calls the place of the Night Journey “the Sacred Mosque,” though the Prophet was taken from outside the mosque building.
RAZI-FULL:v4p103/r12.anchor: وقال / آخرون : المراد من المسجد الحرام الحرم كله والدليل عليه قوله تعالى : { سبحان الذي أسرى

RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r1.speaker: صاحب التهذيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r1.claim: Al-Tahdhib recommends that the imam stand behind the Maqam and worshippers circle the Kaaba; some may stand nearer to it than the imam.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r1.anchor: قال صاحب التهذيب : الجماعة إذا صلوا في المسجد الحرام يستحب أن يقف الإمام خلف المقام

RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r2.claim: The Shafi'i position invalidates prayer for a person in a long mosque row who is not aligned with the Kaaba itself.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r2.anchor: فلو امتد الصف في المسجد فإنه لا تصح صلاة من خرج عن محاذاة الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r3.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r3.claim: Abu Hanifa holds that facing the general direction is sufficient, so a row outside direct Kaaba alignment remains valid; al-Ghazali also selects this view in al-Ihya'.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r3.anchor: وعند أبي حنيفة تصح ، لأن عنده الجهة كافية وهذا اختيار الشيخ الغزالي رحمه الله في كتاب الإحياء

RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r4.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues from the verse that shatr means the side aligned with the Kaaba: one is said to face another's side only when directly opposite, not merely facing the same compass direction.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104/r4.anchor: حجة الشافعي رضي الله عنه : القرآن والخبر والقياس ، أما القرآن فهو ظاهر هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r1.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r1.claim: The Prophet prayed two rakas after leaving the Kaaba, facing it, and said “This is the qibla”; al-Razi treats the wording as exclusive, with no grading stated here.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r1.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام لما خرج من الكعبة ركع ركعتين في قبلة الكعبة وقال : هذه القبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r2.claim: Al-Shafi'i infers from “This is the qibla” and the other reports naming the Kaaba that the qibla is the Kaaba itself, not merely its general direction.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r2.anchor: وهذه الكلمة تفيد الحصر فثبت أنه لا قبلة إلا عين الكعبة وكذلك سائر الأخبار التي رويناها

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r3.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r3.claim: Al-Shafi'i's analogy is that the Prophet's repeatedly transmitted veneration of the Kaaba and prayer's status as a major rite support requiring exact alignment, which further honors the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r3.anchor: وأما القياس فهو أن مبالغة الرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم في تعظيم الكعبة أمر بلغ مبلغ التواتر

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r4.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r4.claim: Al-Shafi'i argues that since the Kaaba is certainly the qibla but other targets are doubtful, caution requires prayer validity to depend on facing the Kaaba.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r4.anchor: ولأن كون الكعبة قبلة أمر معلوم ، وكون غيرها قبلة أمر مكشوك ، والأولى رعاية الاحتياط

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r5.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r5.claim: Abu Hanifa reads the verse as requiring a person to face the side where the Kaaba lies; facing that side fulfills the command even without facing the Kaaba itself.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r5.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأمور . الأول : ظاهر هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r6.speaker: أبو هريرة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r6.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet saying, “What lies between east and west is a qibla”; al-Razi gives no grading here.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r6.anchor: ما روى أبو هريرة رضي الله عنه أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( ما بين المشرق والمغرب قبلة )

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r7.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r7.claim: Al-Shafi'i's followers say the hadith cannot mean every direction between east and west, since that would include the north polar direction, which is not a qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r7.anchor: قال أصحاب الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى : ليس المراد من هذا الحديث أن كل ما يصدق عليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r8.speaker: أصحاب الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r8.claim: They instead delimit the hadith by a particular winter sunrise and summer sunset; the direction between them is Mecca's bearing.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r8.anchor: قال أصحاب الشافعي رحمه الله تعالى : ليس المراد من هذا الحديث أن كل ما يصدق عليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r9.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r9.claim: Abu Hanifa cites the Quba congregation's pivot during a night prayer after news of the change from Jerusalem, without seeking further evidence; the Prophet did not object and the mosque was called the two-qibla mosque.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r9.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأمور . الأول : ظاهر هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r10.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r10.claim: Abu Hanifa argues that Quba worshippers could not have calculated exact Kaaba alignment instantly in the dark without surveying mathematics, yet their prayer was accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r10.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأمور . الأول : ظاهر هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r11.speaker: أبو حنيفة
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r11.claim: He also argues that Muslims built mosques across Islamic lands without surveyors setting each mihrab, while exact alignment would require detailed geometry.
RAZI-FULL:v4p104#2/r11.anchor: واحتج أبو حنيفة بأمور . الأول : ظاهر هذه الآية

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r1.claim: An argument against requiring exact Kaaba alignment says that the Kaaba is only about twenty cubits wide, so almost no eastern or western worshippers can line up with it, and even those few cannot know that they do.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r1.anchor: لو كان استقبال عين الكعبة واجبا إما علما أو ظنا

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r2.claim: An objection models all worshippers as points on a vast circle around the Kaaba, so even long rows curve toward its center while seeming straight to sight.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r2.anchor: الدائرة وإن كانت عظيمة إلا أن جميع النقط المفروضة عليها تكون محاذية لمركز الدائرة

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r3.claim: Al-Razi replies that every segment of the immense circle is truly curved, not straight; imperceptible curvature cannot be known, so a strict alignment condition would leave everyone doubtful about prayer validity, contrary to consensus.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r3.anchor: فالصفوف المتصلة في أطراف العالم إنما يكون كل واحد منهم مستقبلا لعين الكعبة لو لم تكن تلك الصفوف واقعة على الخط المستقيم

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r4.claim: A second argument says that if exact alignment requires geometrical proofs, learning geometry would be individually obligatory, but jurists do not make it obligatory.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r4.anchor: لو كان استقبال عين الكعبة واجبا ولا سبيل إليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r5.claim: An objection distinguishes probabilistic facing, said to be obligatory, from certain facing, which alone would require geometry.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r5.anchor: عندنا استقبال عين الجهة واجب ظنا لا يقينا

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r6.claim: Al-Razi replies that anyone capable of certainty cannot settle for probability; if exact facing is obligatory, such a person must learn geometry, and he says this learning is not required.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r6.anchor: لو كان استقبال عين الكعبة واجبا لكان القادر على تحصيل اليقين لا يجوز له الاكتفاء بالظن

RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r7.claim: A third argument says exact facing, whether known or presumed, needs indicators; if it were obligatory, learning those indicators would be an individual duty, so their non-obligatory status shows exact alignment is not required.
RAZI-FULL:v4p105/r7.anchor: الثالث : لو كان استقبال العين واجبا إما علما أو ظنا

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r1.claim: Al-Razi classifies qibla indicators as terrestrial (mountains, towns, rivers), atmospheric (winds), and celestial (stars).

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r2.claim: Terrestrial and wind indicators are not universally dependable: terrain may be hard to locate relative to the qibla, and winds differ from place to place.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r2.anchor: أما الأرضية والهوائية غير مضبوطة ضبطا كليا / فرب طريق فيه جبل مرتفع لا يعلم أنه على يمين

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r3.claim: Approximate daytime celestial signs use the sun: note its noon position relative to the face, its afternoon position, where it sets, the twilight for night prayer, and its rising for dawn.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r3.anchor: أما النهارية فالشمس فلا بد وأن يراعى قبل الخروج من البلد أن الشمس عند الزوال أهي بين الحاجبين

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r4.claim: The sun can indicate all five prayer directions, but its signs vary with season and locality because sunrises and sunsets differ.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r4.anchor: فكان الشمس تدل على القبلة في الصلوات الخمس ، ولكن يختلف حكم ذلك بالشتاء والصيف

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r5.claim: At night, use the nearly fixed star al-Jady; its position behind or at a shoulder, and its opposite position in southern lands such as Yemen, indicates the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r5.anchor: وأما الليليلة فهو أن يستدل على القبلة بالكوكب الذي يقال له الجدي ، فإنه كوكب كالثابت

RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r6.claim: Use the familiar local star and solar signs during travel unless a long journey changes their bearings; then consult knowledgeable residents or compare the stars while facing the town's main mosque mihrab.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106/r6.anchor: فليعلم ذلك وما عرفه ببلده فليعول عليه في الطريق كله ، إلا إذا طال السفر

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r1.speaker: أهل الهيئة
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r1.claim: Astronomers define the qibla bearing as the horizon's intersection with the great circle through the zeniths of the observer and Mecca; its deviation is measured along the horizon from the local meridian.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r1.anchor: قالوا : سمت القبلة نقطة التقاطع بين دائرة الأفق ، وبين دائرة عظيمة تمر بسمت رؤسنا

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r2.claim: To calculate the bearing, one needs Mecca's longitude and latitude; if a town shares Mecca's longitude but not latitude, its qibla lies on the meridian, south from northern lands and north from southern ones.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r2.anchor: ويحتاج في معرفة سمت القبلة إلى معرفة طول مكة وعرضها ، فإن كان طول البلد مساويا لطول مكة

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r3.claim: It is mistaken to assume that a town at Mecca's latitude but a different longitude has a qibla on the equinoctial east-west line.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r3.anchor: فقد يظن أن سمت قبلة ذلك البلد على خط الاعتدال وهو ظن خطأ

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r4.claim: Even places with both coordinates different from Mecca may have a qibla due east or west at the equinox; otherwise the angle of deviation must be calculated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r4.anchor: وقد يمكن أيضا في البلاد التي أطوالها وعروضها مخالفة لطول مكة وعرضها

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r5.claim: One astrolabe procedure locates the zodiac degree over Mecca, places it on the local instrument's meridian, and rotates its rete west by the longitude difference for a town east of Mecca.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r5.anchor: أسهلها أن يعرف الجزء الذي يسامت رؤس أهل مكة من فلك البروج

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r6.claim: Find the altitude at which the sun crosses that degree over Mecca, then align the local mihrab along the shadow from the center of a vertical staff to its tip.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r6.anchor: ثم يرصد مسامتة الشمس ذلك الجزء فإذا انتهى ارتفاع الشمس إلى ذلك الارتفاع

RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r7.claim: Asked whether learning qibla indicators is an individual or communal duty, al-Razi prefers individual duty: every worshipper is commanded to face the qibla and cannot do so without learning its signs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p106#2/r7.anchor: معرفة دلائل القبلة فرض على العين أم فرض على الكفاية ففيه وجهان أصحهما فرض على العين

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r1.claim: Although the command's wording covers people and circumstances generally, consensus exempts times outside prayer; facing the qibla then is meritorious, as the Prophet says the best gatherings face it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r1.anchor: قوله تعالى : { ما كنتم فولوا وجوهكم شطره } عام

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r2.claim: Accordingly, the obligation to face the qibla is specific to prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r2.anchor: فيبقى أن وجوب الاستقبال من خواص الصلاة

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r3.claim: Worshippers are either able to see the qibla or not; someone who cannot see it may be able to attain certainty, only probability, or neither.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r3.anchor: وأما الغائب فإما أن يكون قادر على تحصيل اليقين

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r4.claim: There is consensus that a worshipper who can directly see the qibla must face it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r4.anchor: أما المعاين فقد أجمعوا على أنه يجب عليه الاستقبال

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r5.claim: Someone absent from the qibla can attain certainty only through geometry; the duty to face it would therefore make learning geometry individually obligatory, though jurists deny this and some even deem it disliked or forbidden, a position al-Razi questions.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r5.anchor: لا سبيل له إلى تحصيل اليقين بجهة القبلة إلا بالدلائل الهندسية

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r6.speaker: صاحب التهذيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r6.claim: For a person in Mecca whose view of the Kaaba is blocked by natural terrain, al-Tahdhib permits ijtihad; for buildings, one view permits it because they also block sight and another rejects it because certainty remains attainable.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r6.anchor: قال صاحب ( التهذيب ) نظر إن كان الحائل أصليا كالجبال

RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r7.speaker: author
