RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r7.claim: Al-Razi prefers the view that a person blocked by buildings must seek certainty: the verse requires facing the Kaaba, and someone able to know it cannot settle for conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107/r7.anchor: وهذا الوجه هو اللائق بمساق الآية ، لأنها لما دلت على وجوب التوجه إلى الكعبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r1.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r1.claim: For a person who can form a probability but not attain certainty, al-Shafi'i's apparent view—and al-Razi's preference—is to use personal ijtihad before asking another person.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r1.anchor: الطريق الأول : الاجتهاد وظاهر قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه يقتضي أن الاجتهاد يقدم على الرجوع

RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r2.claim: Al-Razi's first reason is 59:2, which commands reflection; since the worshipper can reason about the qibla, the command applies.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r2.anchor: قوله تعالى : { فاعتبروا ياأولى * أولى * الابصار } ( الحشر : 2 ) أمر بالاعتبار

RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r3.claim: Others ultimately determine the qibla through ijtihad; imitation thus adds a second possible source of error to the first, whereas one's own reasoning has only one, so the less error-prone route is preferable.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r3.anchor: ولا شك أن الأول أولى لأنه إذا أتى بالاجتهاد فلا يتطرق إليه احتمال الخطأ من جهة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r4.speaker: رسول الله
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r4.claim: Al-Razi's third reason is the Prophet's command to do as much as possible: since the worshipper can investigate the direction by ijtihad, he must do so; no grading is stated.
RAZI-FULL:v4p107#2/r4.anchor: قوله عليه السلام : ( إذا أمرتكم بأمر فأتوا منه ما استطعتم ) فههنا أمر بالاستقبال

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r1.speaker: صاحب التهذيب
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r1.claim: The Tahdhib author says established mihrabs in a large Muslim town, or a known qibla marker on a Muslim road, must be followed as near-certainty; slight east-west deviation still permits personal ijtihad.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r1.anchor: صاحب ( التهذيب ) ذكر أنه إذا كان في قرية كبيرة فيها محاريب منصوبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r2.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r2.claim: After returning from pilgrimage, Ibn al-Mubarak told the people of Merv to turn somewhat left when orienting toward the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r2.anchor: وكان عبد الله بن المبارك يقول بعد رجوعه من الحج

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r3.claim: Razi objects that accepting another person's orientation or practice without proof or reasonable evidence is taqlid, while someone capable of ijtihad must use it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r3.anchor: لا معنى للتقليد إلا قبول قول الغير من غير حجة ولا شبهة

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r4.claim: If ijtihad permits a person to depart from a marker for a slight east-west deviation, it should also permit independent inference where town mihrabs point otherwise.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r4.anchor: جوز المخالفة في اليمين واليسار بناء على الاجتهاد فنقول : هو قادر على تحصيل الظن

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r5.claim: The Prophet praised Muadh for exercising judgment, which shows that ijtihad is not prohibited in identifying the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r5.anchor: معاذا لما قال : اجتهد برأي مدحه الرسول عليه السلام على ذلك

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r6.claim: Following a mihrab despite knowing or reasonably suspecting that it is misdirected would wrongly prefer imitation to inference.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r6.anchor: لو وجب عليه التوجه إلى ذلك المحراب لكان ذلك ترجيحا للتقليد على الاستدلال وأنه خطأ

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r7.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r7.claim: Shafi'i's rule that a qualified jurist may not imitate another qualified jurist also weighs against following a town mihrab when one can infer the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r7.anchor: مذهب الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه لا يجوز للمجتهد تقليد المجتهد

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r8.speaker: القائلون بترجيح محاريب الأمصار
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r8.claim: Advocates of preferring town mihrabs argue that their collective evidence resembles mass transmission and therefore outweighs individual ijtihad.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r8.anchor: أنها كالتواتر مع الاجتهاد ، فوجب رجحانه عليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r9.speaker: القائلون بترجيح محاريب الأمصار
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r9.claim: They compare reliance on the mihrab to learning the prayer time from the muezzin's completed call and the imam's arrival, without independently checking the time.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r9.anchor: إذا رأى المؤذن فرغ من الأذان والإقامة وقد تقدم الإمام ، فههنا لا يحتاج إلى تعرف الوقت

RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r10.speaker: القائلون بترجيح محاريب الأمصار
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r10.claim: They also argue that townspeople's acceptance suggests the mihrab is correct, since they would have noticed and rejected an error.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108/r10.anchor: أن أهل البلد رضوا به ، والظاهر أنه لو كان خطأ لتنبهوا له

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.claim: A trustworthy informant's report that the qibla lies in a direction creates a presumption in its favor; following such a report is a route to identifying the qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r1.anchor: مثل ما إذا أخبره عدل عن كون القبلة في هذه الجهة فهذا يفيد ظن أن القبلة هناك

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.claim: The parties agree that an informant must be Muslim and sane; a disbeliever's or insane person's report or judgment is not accepted here.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r2.anchor: الإسلام والعقل ، فلا عبرة في هذا الباب بقول الكافر

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.speaker: الخيضري عن الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.claim: Al-Khaydari transmits an explicit Shafi'i position that a child's report is not accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r3.anchor: حكى الخيضري نصا عن الشافعي أنه لا يقبل قول الصبي

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.speaker: أبو زيد عن الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.claim: Abu Zayd also transmits a Shafi'i position that a child's report is accepted.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r4.anchor: وحكى أبو زيد أيضا عن الشافعي أنه يقبل

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.speaker: قائلون
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.claim: One view rejects a morally unreliable informant's report by analogy with testimony.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r5.anchor: قالوا : لا يقبل خبر الفاسق لأنه كالشهادة

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.speaker: قيل
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.claim: Another view accepts a morally unreliable informant's report.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r6.anchor: لا يقبل خبر الفاسق لأنه كالشهادة ، وقيل : يقبل

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.speaker: بعض الفقهاء
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.claim: Some require multiple informants, as in testimony, especially jurists who also require multiple transmitters for reports.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r7.anchor: فمنهم من اعتبره كما في الشهادة لاسيما الذين اعتبروا العدد في الرواية أيضا

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.speaker: آخرون
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r8.claim: Other jurists do not require a particular number of informants.

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r9.claim: Evidence that yields a stronger presumption takes precedence: a certain informant outranks an ijtihad-based conjecture, which in turn outranks secondhand imitation.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r9.anchor: كل من كان الأخذ بقوله يفيد ظنا أقوى كان الأخذ بقوله مقدما على الأخذ بقول من يفيد ظنا أضعف

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r10.claim: Razi leaves uncertain whether a person should finish ijtihad after the prayer time, making the prayer late, or follow an informant to keep it within the time.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r10.anchor: فالأولى له تحصيل الاجتهاد حتى تصير الصلاة قضاء أو تقليد الغير حتى تبقى الصلاة أداء فيه تردد

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r11.claim: Someone who does not know the proofs for determining the qibla may, and indeed must, rely on another person's report during prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r11.anchor: من لا يعرف دلائل القبلة فله الرجوع إلى قول الغير حين الصلاة بل يجب

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r12.claim: A mihrab in a Muslim land may be followed under the earlier qualifications; an uncertain marker on a little-used or mixed Muslim and non-Muslim route, or in an unverified small village, requires ijtihad.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r12.anchor: أما إذا رأى القبلة منصوبة في طريق يقل فيه مرور الناس أو في طريق يمر فيه المسلمون والمشركون

RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r13.claim: If an informant supplies star positions, a person able to infer the qibla from stars must use that information when unable to observe the stars directly.
RAZI-FULL:v4p108#2/r13.anchor: يخبره إنسان بمواقع الكواكب وكان هو عالما بالاستدلال بها على القبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r1.claim: This category includes someone in darkness with all indicators hidden, a blind person unable to find an informant, or someone facing equally conflicting signs.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r1.anchor: وهو الكائن في الظلمة التي خفيت الأمارات بأسرها عليه أو الأعمى الذي لا يجد من يخبره

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r2.claim: Such a person cannot be commanded to perform ijtihad, because reasoning without an indicator would impose an impossible duty.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r2.anchor: من غير دلالة ولا أمارة تكليف ما لا يطاق وهو منفي

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r3.claim: Dropping prayer altogether is ruled out by consensus; prayer can be valid without facing the qibla in cases such as combat or voluntary prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r3.anchor: أما سقوط الصلاة عنه فذلك باطل بالإجماع

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r4.claim: Requiring a prayer toward every direction is also invalid because the duty is one prayer.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r4.anchor: إيجاب الصلاة إلى جميع الجهات فهو أيضا باطل لقيام الدلالة على أن الواجب عليه صلاة واحدة

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r5.speaker: قائل
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r5.claim: An objection asks why this case should differ from someone who forgets which of the daily prayers was missed and must make up all possible prayers to be certain.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r5.anchor: ولقائل أن يقول : أليس أن من نسي صلاة من صلوات يوم وليلة ولا يدري عينها

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r6.claim: With omitting prayer and praying toward all directions excluded, the remaining ruling is to pray toward whichever direction one chooses.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r6.anchor: ولما بطل القسمان تعين الثالث وهو التخيير في جميع الجهات

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r7.claim: Razi asks whether an unsupported inclination of the heart toward one direction counts as ijtihad and may be relied upon.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r7.anchor: من غير أن يكون ذلك الترجيح مبنيا على استدلال ، بل يحصل ذلك بمجرد التشهي وميل القلب إليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r8.speaker: النبي
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r8.claim: Razi cites the prophetic saying that a believer sees by God's light as support for relying on the heart's inclination when other methods are unavailable.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r8.anchor: لقوله عليه السلام : ( المؤمن ينظر بنور الله )

RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r9.claim: Razi accepts that inclination as a basis for choice because every other route to preferring a direction has been closed.
RAZI-FULL:v4p109/r9.anchor: ولأن سائر وجوه الترجيح لما انسدت وجب الاكتفاء بهذا القدر

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r1.claim: After a valid prayer based on the best available conjecture, the apparent rule is that no make-up is due because the person fulfilled the duty of the time.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r1.anchor: لأنه أدى وظيفة الوقت وقد صحت منه

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r2.claim: The apparent position of Shafi'i requires repeating the prayer whether the original direction proves correct or mistaken.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r2.anchor: وظاهر قول الشافعي رضي الله عنه أنه تجب الإعادة سواء بأن صوابه أو خطؤه

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r3.speaker: عامة أهل العلم
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r3.claim: Most scholars permit prayer inside the Kaaba, facing whichever side one chooses.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r3.anchor: تجوز الصلاة في جوف الكعبة عند عامة أهل العلم

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r4.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r4.claim: Malik dislikes obligatory prayer inside the Kaaba because the worshipper faces some of it and turns away from the rest, so does not face the whole qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r4.anchor: وقال مالك : يكره أن يصلى في الكعبة المكتوبة

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r5.speaker: مالك
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r5.claim: Malik allows voluntary prayer inside because facing the qibla is not obligatory for it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r5.anchor: وأما النافلة فجائزة ، لأن استقبال القبلة

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r6.speaker: بلال
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r6.claim: Ibn Umar asked Bilal what the Prophet did inside the Kaaba; Bilal reported that the Prophet positioned himself among its columns and prayed. The report is included by al-Bukhari and Muslim and also transmitted by al-Shafi'i.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r6.anchor: فسألت بلالا حين خرج : ماذا صنع رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم ؟ فقال : جعل عمودا عن يساره

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r7.claim: Razi says a solitary report cannot outweigh the apparent meaning of the Qur'anic command.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r7.anchor: خبر الواحد لا يعارض ظاهر القرآن

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r8.claim: He notes the possibility that the Prophet's prayer in the Kaaba was voluntary, which Malik permits.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r8.anchor: لعل تلك الصلاة كانت نافلة ، وذلك عند مالك جائز

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r9.claim: Malik's contrary ruling does not invalidate the report, but makes it somewhat weaker than a solitary report whose narrator does not contradict it, especially against the Qur'an.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r9.anchor: ومخالفة الراوي وإن كانت لا توجب الطعن في الخبر إلا أنها تفيد نوع مرجوحية بالنسبة إلى خبر واحد

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r10.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r10.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that the Prophet supplicated in the Kaaba's corners without praying there, then prayed two rakas outside facing it and said, 'This is the qibla'; the two reports conflict.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r10.anchor: عن ابن جريح عن عطاء : سمعت ابن عباس قال : لما دخل النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم البيت

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r11.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r11.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r11.claim: Razi identifies a direct contradiction between the report that the Prophet prayed inside and Ibn Abbas's report that he did not.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r11.anchor: والتعارض حاصل من وجهين . الأول : أن النفي والإثبات يتعارضان

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r12.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r12.claim: The statement 'this is the qibla' can imply that worshippers must face that specific point, whereas those allowing prayer inside permit turning away from it.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r12.anchor: قوله صلى الله عليه وسلم : ( هذه القبلة ) يدل على أنه لا بد من توجه ذلك الموضع

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r13.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r13.claim: Malik's argument from 'wherever you are' fails either way: if general, it includes people inside the Kaaba and their orientation fulfills the command; if not general, it does not decide this case.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r13.anchor: فإن كان صيغة عموم فقد تناول الإنسان الذي يكون في البيت فكأنه تعالى أمر من كان في البيت أن يتوجه إليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r14.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r14.claim: The operative point is that no one can face the whole Kaaba at once; each person faces only part, and someone inside likewise faces a part and fulfills the command.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110/r14.anchor: أن الإنسان الواحد لا يمكنه أن يتوجه إلى كل البيت ، بل إنما يمكنه أن يتوجه إلى جزء

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.claim: The qibla cannot be just the Kaaba's physical stones and timber: moving its rubble elsewhere and rebuilding would not make the new structure a qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r1.anchor: أجمعنا على أنه لو نقل تراب الكعبة وما في بنائها من الأحجار والخشب

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.claim: The qibla is not the building together with its original location, since after demolition and removal the cleared site remains the direction for worshippers elsewhere.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r2.anchor: لأن الكعبة لو انهدمت والعياذ بالله ، وأزيل عن تلك الأحياز تلك الأحجار والخشب

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.claim: Razi concludes that the qibla is the empty spatial volume occupied by the Kaaba, rather than the material building.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r3.anchor: القبلة هو ذلك الخلاء الذي حصل فيه تلك الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.claim: The name al-Masjid al-Haram refers to the constructed building, while its direction is the particular space occupied by that building; thus the verse points to the empty space as qibla.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r4.anchor: جهة المسجد الحرام هو الأحياز التي حصلت فيها تلك الأجسام

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r5.claim: If the Kaaba were demolished, Razi prefers Ibn Surayj's and Abu Hanifa's view that prayer from its site is valid, over his own school's invalidity ruling, since the worshipper faces part of the qibla-space.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r5.anchor: وذكر ابن سريج أنه يصح ، وهو قول أبي حنيفة

RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r6.claim: Razi likewise chooses Ibn Surayj's view that prayer on the Kaaba's roof is valid even without a wall in front, because the worshipper faces the qibla-space.
RAZI-FULL:v4p110#2/r6.anchor: إلا على قول ابن سريج وهو الاختيار عندي

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r1.claim: The command to face the qibla, together with the need for ijtihad to identify it and the rule that necessary means are obligatory, makes ijtihad obligatory; since it rests on conjecture, the verse establishes legal reliance on conjecture.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r1.anchor: لما دلت الآية على وجوب الاستقبال ، وثبت بالعقل أنه لا سبيل إلى الاستقبال إلى الجهات إلا بالاجتهاد

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r2.speaker: الشافعي
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r2.claim: Shafi'i uses this reasoning to argue that analogical reasoning is a valid proof in religious law.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r2.anchor: وقد استدل الشافعي رضي الله عنه بذلك على أن القياس حجة في الشرع

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r3.claim: Razi rejects the proof because it would establish analogy by another analogy, which he says is not valid.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r3.anchor: وهو ضعيف لأنه إثبات للقياس بالقياس وذلك لا سبيل إليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r4.claim: No separate intention to face the qibla is required: carrying out the commanded act suffices, as with covering the nakedness and purifying the place and clothing.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r4.anchor: الظاهر أنه لا يجب نية استقبال القبلة لأن الآية دلت على وجوب الاستقبال والآتي به آت بما دلت الآية عليه

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r5.claim: Facing the qibla lapses for combat, fear of an enemy or dangerous animal, a mistaken direction from slight east-west deviation, and voluntary prayers.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r5.anchor: استقبال القبلة ساقط عند قيام العذر كما في حال المسايفة

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r6.claim: This supports waiving make-up for someone who prayed while unable to obtain knowledge or conjecture, and for a jurist whose qibla judgment later proves mistaken.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r6.anchor: وهذا يقتضي أن العاجز عن تحصيل العلم والظن إذا أدى الصلاة أن يسقط عنه القضاء

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r7.claim: If a person's ijtihad changes during prayer, they should turn to the new direction and continue; the new judgment does not invalidate the earlier one.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r7.anchor: فعليه أن ينحرف ويتحول ويبني لأن عارض الاجتهاد لا يبطل السابق

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r8.claim: The same rule applies when a person first trusts one informant and then another trusted informant gives a contrary direction.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r8.anchor: ثم جاء آخر نفسه إليه أسكن فأخبره بخلافه

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r9.claim: The universal instruction is not redundant: the preceding command addresses the Prophet, whereas this one addresses the whole community.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r9.anchor: هذا ليس بتكرار ، وبيانه من وجهين

RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r10.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r10.claim: The preceding address could be taken as a command limited to the people in Medina; this wording clarifies that Muslims must face the qibla wherever they are.
RAZI-FULL:v4p111/r10.anchor: فبين الله تعالى أنهم أينما حصلوا من بقاع الأرض

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r1.claim: The locative conditional is jussive in syntax, equivalent to 'wherever you may be,' and the following fa is the apodosis.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r1.anchor: وموضع ( كنتم ) من الإعراب جزم بالشرط

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r2.speaker: السدي
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r2.claim: Al-Suddi identifies those given scripture as the Jews specifically and the scripture as the Torah.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r2.anchor: اليهود خاصة ، والكتاب هو التوراة عن السدي

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r3.claim: Razi prefers the broader identification of Jewish rabbis and Christian scholars, since the wording is general and the earlier scripture reference includes the Torah and Gospel.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r3.anchor: بل المراد أحبار اليهود وعلماء النصارى وهو الصحيح لعموم اللفظ والكتاب المتقدم هو التوراة والإنجيل

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r4.claim: The people who concealed this knowledge must have been a small group, because a large group could not plausibly collude in concealment.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r4.anchor: ولا بد أن يكونوا عددا قليلا لأن الكثير لا يجوز عليهم التواطؤ على الكتمان

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r5.claim: The pronoun may refer to the Messenger with his law and prophethood, making the truth include the qibla and other matters.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r5.anchor: فجاز أن يكون المراد أن القوم يعلمون أن الرسول مع شرعه ونبوته حق فيشتمل ذلك على أمر القبلة وغيرها

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r6.claim: Razi prefers taking the pronoun to refer specifically to the qibla obligation, since that is the immediate subject of the passage.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r6.anchor: وهذا الاحتمال الأخير أقرب لأنه أليق بالكلام إذ المقصود بالآية ذلك دون غيره

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r7.claim: One explanation is that some Jewish scholars found in the prophets' books reports about the Messenger and the qibla, including that he would pray toward both qiblas.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r7.anchor: أن قوما من علماء اليهود كانوا عرفوا في كتب أنبيائهم خبر الرسول وخبر القبلة وأنه يصلي إلى القبلتين

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r8.claim: Another explanation is that they knew the Kaaba was the ancient House that God made the qibla of Abraham and Ishmael.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r8.anchor: أنهم كانوا يعلمون أن الكعبة هي البيت العتيق الذي جعله الله تعالى قبلة لإبراهيم وإسماعيل

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r9.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r9.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r9.claim: A third explanation is that they recognized Muhammad's prophethood through his miracles, and therefore knew that everything he brought, including the qibla change, was true.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r9.anchor: وثالثها : أنهم كانوا يعلمون نبوة محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم لما ظهر عليه من المعجزات

RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r10.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r10.speaker: ابن عمار وحمزة والكسائي
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r10.claim: Ibn Ammar, Hamza, and al-Kisa'i read the final verb with ta as direct address to Muslims; the other readers use ya, referring to the Jews.
RAZI-FULL:v4p112/r10.anchor: قرأ ابن عمار وحمزة والكسائي : { تعملون } بالتاء على الخطاب للمسلمين

JISHUMI:v1p641/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r1.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r1.claim: Four explanations are offered for the repeated qibla passage: it confirms a replaced obligation; anticipates what follows; the first changes Jerusalem and the second specifies the Kaaba everywhere; or the first covers residence and the second travel.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r1.anchor: قلنا: فيه أربعة أقوال: قيل: لأنه لنسخ فرض قبله فكان موضع التأكيد

JISHUMI:v1p641/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r2.claim: The verse requires holding to the qibla wherever one is; it is the true commanded direction.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r2.anchor: الآية تدل على وجوب التمسك بالقبلة حيث كان وأنه الحق المأمور به

JISHUMI:v1p641/r3.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r3.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r3.claim: Forgetfulness and inattention cannot be attributed to God because He knows by His essence eternally.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r3.anchor: وتدل على أن الغفلة والنسيان لا يجوز على الله تعالى؛ لأنه عالم لذاته

JISHUMI:v1p641/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r4.claim: The community agrees that facing the Kaaba is a prayer condition, established by the verse and known necessarily from the Prophet’s religion; denying it is unbelief.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r4.anchor: ولا خلاف بين الأمة أن التوجه إلى الكعبة من شرائط الصلاة، وقد دلت الآية عليه

JISHUMI:v1p641/r5.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r5.speaker: أبو الحسن وأبو بكر الرازي
JISHUMI:v1p641/r5.claim: Abu al-Hasan and Abu Bakr al-Razi say those far from the Kaaba must face its general direction.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r5.anchor: فأما الغائب فقيل: فرضه الجهة، عن أبي الحسن وأبي بكر الرازي

JISHUMI:v1p641/r6.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r6.speaker: أبو عبد الله الجرجاني
JISHUMI:v1p641/r6.claim: Abu Abd Allah al-Jurjani says an absent worshipper must face the exact Kaaba out of reverence for the sanctuary.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r6.anchor: وقيل: فرضه العين، عن أبي عبد الله الجرجاني

JISHUMI:v1p641/r7.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r7.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r7.claim: The author prefers facing the general direction for those far away since they cannot reach the exact point; if direction is uncertain, they investigate and exercise judgment.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r7.anchor: والأول الوجه؛ لأنه غير قادر على إصابة العين، فكان فرضه ما قدر عليه

JISHUMI:v1p641/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r8.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r8.claim: If the mistake becomes clear during prayer, turn toward the qibla; if after completion, the author’s school requires no repeat, unlike al-Shafiʿi.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r8.anchor: فإن تبين أنها خطأ وهو في الصلاة استدار، وإن تبين بعد الفراغ فلا إعادة عليه

JISHUMI:v1p641/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r9.speaker: الشافعي
JISHUMI:v1p641/r9.claim: Al-Shafiʿi requires repeating the prayer when the mistake becomes clear after completion.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r9.anchor: فلا إعادة عليه عند علمائنا، وقال الشافعي: عليه الإعادة

JISHUMI:v1p641/r10.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r10.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v1p641/r10.claim: For a mistaken ijtihad in Mecca, Abu Bakr al-Razi requires repetition because certainty replaced judgment; Muhammad b. al-Hasan says no repeat, which the author finds more apt.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r10.anchor: فأما إذا اجتهد بمكة ثم بان له أنه أخطأ فذكر أبو بكر الرازي أنه يعيد

JISHUMI:v1p641/r11.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r11.speaker: محمد
JISHUMI:v1p641/r11.claim: Muhammad, transmitted by Ibn Rustam, says no repeat after mistaken ijtihad in Mecca; the author calls this more apt.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r11.anchor: وقال محمد فيما رواه ابن رستم: لا يعيد، وهو الأقيس

JISHUMI:v1p641/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v1p641/r12.speaker: أبو يوسف
JISHUMI:v1p641/r12.claim: If judgment directed one way but the worshipper prayed another, the author calls prayer invalid regardless; Abu Yusuf says it is complete if they in fact faced the qibla.
JISHUMI:v1p641/r12.anchor: فصلاته فاسدة سواء علم أنه أصاب أو أخطأ، قال أبو يوسف: إذا أصاب القبلة
